The big brush was pretty soft and seemed nice. The other brushes weren't that impressive. I was disappointed. Then, I tried to open the battery compartment. Now, I know it says "batteries not included" in the description. And I knew that going into this mess. Well, I wrestled with the battery compartment for what felt like three hours until it finally snapped open. At this point, I've lost about fifteen pounds because it is on so freaking tight. You'd think they were keeping the Krusty Krab secret formula inside or something. Well, it opened. No batteries, of course, like, I knew that. All I am saying is that this brush is originally $99, yet they can't include batteries? Okay.

So, I was reading the instructions, which seem pretty impossible to understand. I'd like to think of myself as a well-read, educated gal, but I couldn't understand them. I don't understand how this brush has eight speeds when it only has an on and off button but okay. I'll take their word for it. It's really hard to figure out how to order replacement heads; I'm not even sure that my instructions came with that part because I couldn't find it anywhere.

As I was inspecting the other brush heads, I picked up the pumice stone thinking, "Yeah, buddy, my feet are gonna be lovin' this!" Just as that thought crossed my mind, the pumice stone fell off of the brush head and onto my lap. I kid you not! I didn't even touch it! Like, I wasn't playing around with it or anything. I think it fell off when I picked it up. As if it was just glued onto it with Elmer's glue or something, not even super glue. Just Elmer's. So, that happened. It was sitting in my lap, and I just started laughing. Why would it be so easy to just knock off like that? This product is "worth" $99! You'd think it would have been super glued at least. It's not!

At this point, I've already decided to send it back. But that isn't even the best part. I take the little brush head off, and I try to put on the big soft brush head just to see how to change the brush heads. The little one comes off pretty easily. I pop on the big one and lock it in place. Okay! Nice, nice. Well, then, this thing gets stuck! The big brush head got stuck onto the base and would not come off. How weird is that? Why wouldn't they make it easy to come off? If I am using this in the shower, and I have wet and soapy hands, I don't want to fight my brush head to come off. I want it to come off real easy. I don't wanna play games; I wanna get clean.

Needless to say, I was pretty disappointed with this overall product, and I just wish it was made better. I know I got it for 20-something dollars, but now it's back up to almost fifty bucks, and that isn't fair. Because people are going to spend $50 on this dollar store face cleansing brush, and they're going to be really disappointed!

So, just take my word for it! If you're looking for a brush that "is as effective as systems sold by skin professionals for nearly $200," please look somewhere else. This is not that face cleansing brush. I get better results from my $15 Neutrogena Microdermabrasion System.

review_text:
This is a review of three comparable products: Jergens Natural Glow - 3 Days to Glow Moisturizer Medium to Tan Skin,True Natural: All Natural Self Tanner Face & Body, and Caribbean Solutions Beach Colors Natural Self Tanner. I have been using the Jergens product for years, but have been reading too much about the toxicity of the ingredients. I used several sites to research this, and found EWG's Skin Deep to be most helpful. So I narrowed them down, and tried True Natural and Caribbean Solutions. I have been using the latter two for about a month now, and here is my findings.
Jergens: Pros - It is the darkest color, two applications and you can really tell the difference. Cons -- Very potent odor. Smells your clothes and everything it touches, with the smell lingering for days. My family can't stand the smell. It dyes fabrics that it comes into contact with, like sheets, even multiple hours after application. Hard to get the last part out of the tube. Apply too much and color goes to orange. Aforementioned toxicity fears.
True Natural. Pros - very good color, not as dark as Jergens, but not as orange. Odor is not potent. Low toxicity and cancer concerns. Cons: Doesn't apply smoothly, have to really rub it in. Container is not the easiest to use, but better than Jergens.
Caribbean Solutions. Pros - Mild odor. By far, the easiest to apply. Low toxicity and cancer concerns. Smooth. Decent color -- not orange. Can apply any time. Cons: Color is the lightest of the three, but still makes a big difference.

My conclusion: I probably will use all three -- with Jergens use the least frequent. Maybe an application every other day for the first couple of days a month to get some rich color, and then touch up the rest of the month with the other two. I will not use Jergens more than that because of the toxicity, smell and mess. I imagine Caribbean Solutions will be used most frequently, because the color is almost as good as True Natural, and it is byfar the easiest to use. Really simple to use every two or three days: you don't have to figure out a good time when you won't stain anything, or be around other people to offend with the smell, or soil your clothes.

Of course, with them all, you have to wash your palms really well after using so they don't get the color.

review_text:
This brush may be the number one rated brush on Amazon, not sure how that happened, however it is an extremely poor performer. I bought this brush when I was first getting into double edge razors and wet shaving, and did not know any better, and hope this review saves someone else money wasted.
This brush is clipped, meaning instead of selecting badger hairs of various lengths, and forming the brush, they are randomly placed and then cut, what this means for the end user experience is a prickly and harsh "badger" brush. The entire purpose of badger brushes is to have a softer brush, with a little bit of backbone to make lather well.
The glue or epoxy used to hold the knot into the handle is also sub par, and the brush sheds hairs continuously, and in copious amounts. After reading other reviews, it looks like my experience was not an outlier.
Save your money, and if you are looking to buy a brush that is on Amazon, get a similarly priced Omega, Semogue, or Vie Long. It won't matter if its badger, boar, horse, synthetic, anything you buy at this price point, from those manufacturers, will be leaps and bounds better than this Escali shaving brush.

product_name: Banana Boat Sport Performance Sunscreen Lotion
review_text: First review ever, but I needed others to know about my experience with this product. Wore it today for the first time, and 10 minutes into my walk, I was already sweating profusely, and through my customary 2 hours walk, I was soaked all over as if my own personal cloud was raining on me unbeknownst to others. My situation is this: sure, I was out on the South Florida heat (morning, however, but it does get pretty hot nowadays), and sure, I walk at a fast pace; but I've been doing it every single day for the past 7 months, and using Hawaiian Tropic, and I can definitely tell you that I am below average in the sweating scale - never has anything close to this happened to me. The only reason I changed sunscreen was because I wouldn't pay 13 dollars for the Hawaiian Tropic I last (before the advent of Summer) bought for 4. I don't know if I got some faulty batch, or what, and I'd be more than willing to ship it back to the manufacturer if they want to find out. If this is normal for this product, I don't understand how a sport sunscreen can cause immoderate sweating so that it will absolutely skim off in no time whatsoever. Also, I couldn't understand all the positive reviews, unless everyone uses this staying pretty still around the pool or in the beach - which could be the case. So, if this is normal, and if you're planning on moving more than 100 feet per hour or so, I would recommend you not to buy this, not even to accept it as a gift. I most eagerly wish to speak with the vendor or the manufacturer - this product was a waste of 6 dollars, but, much more regrettably, it ruined one of my morning walks, which I won't ever get back.

review_title: Not my preferred purple hair dye
review_text:
I purchased this after reading reviews of its awesomeness because the purple dye I was using at the time seemed to be fading too quickly. Unfortunately, I found out that this color does NOT work better than the one I was using (Paul Mitchell) - it faded even faster. I used this on both newly bleached hair and over previously purple dyed hair. On the newly bleached hair, it faded to the expected ashy lavender color in less than two weeks with washing hair every 2-3 days while I got at least 3 weeks out of the Paul Mitchell dye. It worked ok on the previously colored hair - got basically 2 weeks out of it - hence the 2 stars rather than 1.

Obviously, take this review with a grain of salt... everyone's going to have a different experience with hair color because there are so many variables: hair status, bleach outcome, dye process, wash frequency, shampoo used...even one's environment can make a difference. But for me, all things being the same, I like the Paul Mitchell better.

review_title: I fell in love with the colors (and the price) online
review_text:
I fell in love with the colors (and the price) online. However, the colors and the quality of the polish do not perform well.

A few things about my relationship with Nail Polish:

- I have 30-50 colors at any given time.
- If a color doesn't look good with my skin color, if I get bored of it, or I notice it doesn't get much play in the rotation, I give it to my nieces.
- I LOVE bright colors. I also love Blues.
- I love opaque polishes.
- I always use base coat and top coat, and usually use 2 coats of color.

So this purchase:

- The Green paints on very, very thin, almost sheer. The first coat makes my nails look diseased. Additional coats didn't do much for color saturation. It was very ugly.

- The Yellow was sheer as well, and despite rolling the bottle before application, the color seemed to pool in the corners. I had to use 3 coats and it just looked too iridescent. I was hoping for a bright Daisy yellow - not a dull Banana or Pale Lemon and this was a mix of both.

- Red, Purple, Blue, Pink - were opaque (as seen in the photo), but the polish is very goopy and takes forever to dry. I make sure that the brush isn't dripping and do 3 simple strokes - side/side/center.

- The Red looks "cherry red" online but the actual color was a pinkish orange. I'd rather it have been a bright NEON orange as the photo suggested.

review_title: Spend Most Of Your Time Worrying About It Falling
review_text:
'Barely' worked.

Surprisingly (to me anyway), every table/desk I tested this on had a beveled edge. This product does not do well with beveled edges because this product has to reach so far to get past the beveled part to get to the actual 'top' of the table that only a very small part of this product is actually touching the top of the table.

So this makes the cane swing very far under the table, which means the cane is at about a 45 degree angle, which means that this product is at about a 45 degree angle and therefore VERY close to slipping off the table.

My dad and I had to place it absolutely perfectly on the table so there would be no swinging at all when we let go, otherwise it would slide off. And even when it didn't slide off, it sure acted like it was ready to slide off at any minute.

The material wasn't a grippy, rubber type material like would be expected either. It was actually fairly smooth (which increases slipperiness). This was very surprising.

There were two of these slats included in the package and they suggested trying one slat above the table and one below, that was supposed to hold it a bit tighter by kind of gripping the table. review_title: Works reliably, but not the best cut.
review_text:
I love Panasonic stuff normally, but this isn't about what I love. It's about what you, the informed consumer, should buy. So, if I had it to do over again, I'd do more research and get a better model. It's decent, but just that. My old rotary Norelcos cut better and shave smoother, and one of those sounds like it's ready to explode.

I think this shaver is built well. Feels solid. This is something I've noticed from Panasonic for many years and one of the reasons I bought it, as they rarely make anything that isn't good. But when you switch it on, especially after a full charge, it basically sounds like it's running at about a hundred thousand RPM, and gives you sort of a lackluster cut. Multiple passes over the same area. Really hard to get a decent shave on the neck. The flip-out trimmer is also not a very aggressive cutter, but it's fine inasmuch as it won't let you get too out-of-control on your moustache. Other reviewers have mentioned a "linear motor" available on higher-end models, so they may do a better job. My experience so far leads me to believe rotaries cut better, or at least faster.

product_name: Secret Outlast Clear Gel Antiperspirant and Deodorant Scent, 2.7 Ounce
review_title: It's here! It's clear! It's not that special!
review_text:
I received a free sample of this product from Secret in order to test it out, so for a few weeks I used my normal deodorant on one armpit, and the Outlast Clear Gel on the other to get a good comparison. Final conclusion: It's just ok. Not bad, but not the greatest thing ever to happen to my armpits.

I generally don't like gel deodorants...something about putting a gooey liquid in my armpit is less than appealing. As gels go though, this does dry relatively quickly and is only a little sticky. The product is clear and leaves no white marks, but I've never had any problems with white marks myself, and definitely not any issues with clumping (eew!). If white marks are a concern for you, this may be a product worth trying out.

The odor protection continues to be inconsistent, but so does my current deodorant. The most significant thing for me was the scent of the product. The other versions of Secret Clear Gel have a very clear label indicating the scent. The fact that the Completely Clean version doesn't mention scent at all is somewhat misleading, and I assumed that it would be relatively unscented. If you don't want a noticeable smell coming from your armpits throughout the day, be sure to get the version that says "unscented", not Completely Clean. All in all, Secret Outlast doesn't seem to be any better than my usual brand, but it's not any worse either. It may be worth a shot if you have issues with white marks!

It is not a bad product but it is not my favorite face serum. I've tried a few now and in comparison I'd say this product is just ok. I like that it comes in a dark bottle with a pump and was mostly full but applying it is a little more challenging than others because it is much more liquid-y. The pump takes a couple presses to get started the first time you use it and rotates very easily but getting the serum out is easy enough. It's just that every time you get a drop the serum runs down your finger if you are not quick to get it to your face. You could apply it with a cotton ball but that way you lose a lot in the transfer. For the price point it's good that the serum is completely clear and gets absorbed quickly so you can put it on before makeup but I haven't seen any real results from using this product so while I don't hate it because I don't think anything bad can come from putting vitamin C on my face I'm also not giving it a raving review.

product_name: Lockhart's Hair Pomade Goon Grease Heavy Hold
review_title: Buy directly from Lockhart if you want to guarantee which scent you get
review_text:
When I bought this I knew that there were two potential scents for this product (lemon/cucumber or cinnamon/sandalwood.) Looking back I wish I had bought directly from Lockhart to ensure which I got. Although between the purchase and writing this review, give or take 6 days, it seems they have changed how they let you select the fragrance on their site (the description for goon grease states that you can choose the scent, but the option to do so has dissappeared.) If you are looking for the citrus scent, I assume that's what their Lemon goon grease is for now, so I would recommend getting that if that scent sounds more appealing to you.

To be fair though, I don't mind the cinnamon scent, it's one of the better spice scents I've used in products like these. I would compare it to the scent of Anchor's Teddy Boy original pomade mixed with murrays.

As far as how well the product works, my first impressions thus far are underwhelming. I have very thick and wavy hair, with an undercut and about 3-4 inches on top. I usually style in a sort of comb-over/pomp in a way that let's the wave in my hair seem natural. So far, Goon grease doesn't seem much different in application to murray's superior, besides the slightly easier scooping from the can and the spreading in the hands. When I apply it and start styling, I don't really feel like I have the control that I want from a petro product. My pomps so far have seemed pretty short and I REALLY don't appreciate how many fly aways I am having, even with a generous application. On top of that, it has not lasted throughout the day like I had expected it too, with my bangs falling over my forehead just after getting home from work (a desk job where I don't spend a lot of time sweating or moving.) I'm used to having an oil-based product do that only after I lift weights in the evenings.

I will say that I like the level of shine in this product and that makes my wavy hair look great in a side-part comb-over.

For reference I have used murray's superior, dax w&g, and o'douds heavy hold. If you are looking for a less greasy high-hold oil-based pomade I personally recommend the o'douds over this for hair like mine (although the scent on that product isn't as pleasant.) And so far, both goon grease and o'douds are expensive compared to the value of murray's and dax. This is the main reason I'm giving this a 3/5 for initial impressions.

I'll look to make an update for this review after I've used this product more.

product_name: Lanoline Manuka Honey Skin Renew Firming Creme
review_text:
This creme is extremely rich. I'm picky with my facial cremes and serums because I know the wrong one can lead to disastrous results. I have adult acne for which I have a day to day regimen. My regimen is very simple and effective and I really didn't want to change it. In the morning I wash with Obagi Foaming Cleanser Gel using my Clarisonic. I use the Obagi Toner after letting my skin air dry and apply 2.5% benzoyl peroxide. I then use Complex 15 (which has been discontinued in the US to my great upset) and the Obagi Healthy Skin Protection SPF 35. This works wonderfully for me. At night my system is similar except that I exfoliate first with microexfoliator (blanking on the name). Then instead of my regular moisturizer I take this time to use an anti-aging product - Skindanavia Night Time Restorative Treatment. It's amazing! It always leaves my face hydrated and buttery soft even though is insanely expensive. Now the company has gone under and the arduous product replacement has begun. Enter the Lanoline Manuka Honey Creme.

I purchased this product, from Marshalls, for a few reasons:
1. Manuka Honey is highly antibacterial. Its akin to a miracle treatment for those patients that have suffered full thickness burns its even better than silverdene in some clinical trials. Honey is also a humectant - it pulls water into the skin.

2. It contains benzoyl alcohol and salicyclic acid. Both of these agents have proven efficacy in dealing with acne

3. It contains a number of natural oils - sweet almond, Jojoba, Sunflower, etc that are great at penetrating the skin and working naturally with sebum to seal in moisture.

Here is my initial impression of this product.

A little goes a long way. It's very creamy and spreadable so you really don't need to use that much to provide full facial coverage.

It burned with application. At least for me I had 2 or 3 patches on my face that I would describe as burning stinging level of discomfort on my face that calmed down after about 30 minutes of application. This effect goes away with continued use.

It is extremely moisturizing. Skin was softer and more supple than it had ever been using any other product. I believe this is in large part due to the manuka honey, aloe, and glycerin.

The smell, for me at least, is a bit overwhelming. One reason I enjoy the products I use in my regular regimen is that they are fragrance free. I prefer that clinical clean removed smell to the over floral and orange scent of this product. It was almost too much for me but it does dissipate as the duration of application increases i.e. throughout the day.

It does not in my opinion contain any agents that directly combat aging such as retinol, or LEXA complex, etc. In short its a powerhouse of anti-acne and moisturizing creme. I'll have to see if there are any anti-aging benefits down the line, but I'd like to continue looking at other products that are directly targeted toward those issues.

review_title: Not the 2 step system for me, but Crest is still a winner
review_text:
So crest has come out with another 2 step whitening toothpaste system. I love the first one I tried, the Crest Pro-Health HD Daily Two-Step Toothpaste System, but this one falls short. So I will stick with my loved Crest brand, just not this product.

The process is simple, brush for one minute with step one. Spit, but don't rinse, and brush for one minute with step 2. Rinse and done.

The problem with this system is in the paste itself. It is gritty and pastey with a fake sugar taste. I understand the theory of the gritty paste is "buff" off stains but I have not noticed any difference in the color of my teeth. Now perhaps that's a good thing, as Crest mentions in their Crest 3D commercials, "If you're not whitening, you're yellowing." but when a product claims to be "99% as white as a professional polish" then I expect better results. I won't be purchasing this particular toothpaste again, but I do like the 2 step process, if for nothing else, it keeps me honest and I brush for the full 2 minutes. So I will be buying the Crest Pro-Health HD Daily Two-Step Toothpaste System again, which I recommend you try for yourself. Happy brushing.

I am trying the product for free thanks to Crest® and BzzAgent.

review_text:

The Feel: The mascara goes on smooth and clean, but the short little bristles make it clump and feel awkward. To make it feel okay for me, I had to use an eyelash curler and a separate eyelash brush to separate my lashes. I suppose this is the trick to getting manga eyelashes, to stick them together, but it felt very uncomfortable. I can see using this on fake lashes and being okay. The mascara didn't irritate my eyes, but it messed with the lashes so that it was uncomfortable and I kept messing with them all day.

The Look: There is definitely a very graphic, manga look when wearing this mascara. After putting some on one eye and not the other, I observed my eye looked more open and alert. A few observers that did not know what I had put on it, said one eye looked awake and the other asleep. So the look, is definitely a plus if you want that big lash feel.

Overall: I won’t be getting this again. Although the look is great and the mascara itself is of nice quality, the brush making my lashes stick together was not comfortable. I don’t want a mascara I have to use two other products to apply. Like I said, if you are using fake lashes, this may be the best product out there.

review_title: Good for Uneven Skin Tone, but Watch for Flakey Skin!
review_text:
I was sent the Skin Brightening & Lightening Cream by ‪Key West Health and Beauty to review. All opinions are my own.

Here is the product description from http://keywesthealthandbeauty.com:

“At last, a safe and natural alternative to skin lightening and brightening has arrived! Most skin lightening & brightening creams contain hydroquinone, which is clinically proven to be toxic, carcinogenic and is banned in many countries. Our proprietary blend of 97% natural and 72% organic ingredients offer a safe but effective hydroquinone free alternative.”

This product contains these active ingredients:

Glycolic acid to exfoliate
Salicylic acid to unclog pores
Kojic acid to brighten dull skin
Hyaluronic acid to provide hydration

After using it topically for a week, I can safely say this evens out my acne-scarred, uneven skintone and undereye circles. However, I would not use more than 3x/week without exfoliating to prevent flakey skin. If you have dry skin, I would not use this as an every day moisturizer, as it can make your skin a bit flakey if you are using other anti-acne products. But if you use this product and withhold from acne treatments (other than spot treatments), I think it could be used everyday.

I used it for 12 days and incorporated it into my existing skincare routine. After washing my face with my clarisonic + my Dial acne face wash, I dried my face off and applied the cream lightly all over my face. I found it made my skin a bit flakey after 5 days, so I took out the acne wash and the flakey-ness went away.

This is the second time I’ve ever been sent a product to test and I’m so grateful.

(Check out http://keywesthealthandbeauty.com for more information.)

review_title: A Little Goes A Long Way
review_text:
I have used mud masks for years so I am very familiar with them.

When I put this mask on I wasn't looking in the mirror, I just scooped some out and put it on my face. When I went to look in the mirror I was very disappointed because most of the mask was a thin veil of mud and I thought no way will this stuff be effective. I let it dry on my face and I was surprised to feel how well it dried on my face even though it was a very thin layer.

I could feel my face tighten nicely, but it didn't make my face itchy like some other mud masks have done. I did notice my pores were temporarily smaller.

Although this is by no means the tightest mud mask I have tried, it is a good mask. One of the tightest masks I've used is the one that comes in powder form that you mix with water or ACV. I can totally see myself using this mask more often than the other simply for convenience, plus this mask tightened enough to my satisfaction.

For some reason it is not easy to find masks in my local drug store, so I will probably buy this product when this jar runs out.

review_title: REAL REVIEW - I did NOT receive this product discounted or free
review_text:
First off, I did not receive a discount or receive this product for free. I also was a little skeptical and wondered if some of these positive reviews I read were real or fake? I'm guessing they are actually real because I'm happy to say I've found this to be a good product. Just so you also know, I am a huge product junkie. I am constantly buying/trying new face products all the time, expecting miracles in the end. Unfortunately, I never seem to be fully satisfied. For me to rate this 4 stars means I'm pretty happy.

I decided to try this 3 months ago after using Radha's Skin Clearing Serum (this is actually a good product as well) for a month. With this order, I also bought the Radha Retinol Moisturizer to use with it. I am in my 30's and have some very small fine lines forming on my forehead and get occasional mild breakouts. What I found works best for me is using this product on alternating nights. I use the Radha Skin Clearing Serum one night and then the Radha Vitamin C Serum/Radha Retinol Moisturizer the next. After 3 months, I can honestly say I am quite pleased. The small fines lines on my forehead definitely have a softer appearance. Some days, they are completely gone. For an "over the counter product", all 3 of these are quite good. If you are expecting it to work a miracle overnight, then you're going to be disappointed. However, if you use these products consistently for a few months, then I think you will be pleasantly surprised.

The only negative I can think of is the bottle it comes in. It gets exposed to air every time you use it. I read in the Q&A section that they only recommend using it for 3 months after opening. The Skin Clearing Serum and Retinol Moisturizer come in a much better designed system that is airtight. I wish they would also put this in that same type of container. I only use this every other night so I still have half of the bottle left. Since this serum is inexpensive, I don't mind repurchasing this every 3 months. I can't believe I just said REPURCHASE. I usually never try the same skin care product TWICE ;-)every 3 months. I can't believe I just said REPURCHASE. I usually never try the same skin care product TWICE ;-)

review_title: Great battery life and simplicity! Does tug thicker hair
review_text:
This is a great trimmer - I'm still a shaving/trimming novice, and I was noticing that my Norleco Aquatec shaver (awesome shaver, by the way) was leaving some long hairs behind - no fault of the shaver, it just isn't designed to take care of that kind of hair! I noticed however that the beard trimmer attachment would cut the hairs close enough to be whisked off by the shaver.

Recently I decided that I would start using a trimmer for regular grooming, and use my shaver when I needed a little extra help. I wanted to get a device that was designed specifically for trimming, and this trimmer fit the bill - solid construction, good name (Wahl), good reviews.

Pros:
- Solidly-built
- Trims close (fits my needs)
- Holds a charge well

Cons:
- I kind of prefer the Norelco comb shape - Norelco teeth are rounded, and seem to be spaced a little bit further apart. This helps me to avoid "tugging" as my beard is pretty thick. The Wahl teeth come to a sharper point, and if I shave at the wrong speed, things become a little uncomfortable. However, I will continue to use this trimmer because of it's good construction, simplicity, and battery life.

UPDATE: I used this product several times, and as I mentioned in the original review, it does tug regularly. Battery life remains good, but I don't find myself using this device very frequently due to the tugging.

The Travel blend is better than the Destress blend in the other 3-pack.

These are three different blends in roller ball bottles. They seem to be secure and don't leak, even if on their sides. The caps are well made. The container box has two partitions, and they are secure in the box due to a good design.

Energy - the orange label. It's bright and uplifting, but it's not as strong as I'd hope. However, you could use this is the evening and it probably wouldn't affect your sleep.

Travel - the green/aqua label. It's soothing and calming without being sleep inducing. I really like it, even more so than the Energy blend.

Sweet Dreams - the blue/purple label. I use this at night, on my wrists. It's very soothing and relaxing.

I was familiar with the Tisserand brand, so when I saw these in a store for $9.99 for the three, I knew it was a good deal. I'm very pleased with this purchase, and I recommend these blends and this brand. If you do online research about Tisserand, you'll see what a quality brand it is.

review_title: Honestly one of the best products I have used
review_text:
I don't normally write reviews, but this product (Laneige Lip Sleeping Mask, 20g) was truly extraordinary. Allow me to tell you why this product merrited a 5-star review:

1) I have incredibly dry skin, and wake up with chapped lips every morning. Rather, that was the case before I picked up this lip sleeping mask. Now I wake up with supple lips, and it is an amazing feeling.

2) I toss and turn a lot at night. This product stays on my lips all night long, which is truly amazing. I will say that if you do not like things that are almost sticky or tacky on your lips, then you might not like it. I personally do not mind, as the outcome is amazing to me.

3) It has a soft berry scent, but it isn't strong, and it doesn't taste like anything.

4) A little goes a long way. I cannot stress that enough. Even with a "thick" layer of the stuff on my lips, I barely scratch the surface. I believe that this product will last at the least 6 months of nightly usage.

5) I have used a "thin" layer during the day in liau of lip balm, and it works amazingly.

6) It's a small container, making it perfect for travel as well. Like I said before though, a little goes a long way.

All-in-all, this product is well worth the money, and I will repurchase it once I have finished the first one.

I do find myself feeling a need to shave twice a day, and I take that as an indicator that perhaps this doesn't shave as close as a blade, but it's close enough. This has made shaving simple, convenient, and painless.

review_text:
I was very surprised with the size of the bag. It is about twice as long as I had expected, which is perfect for trips where I like to keep all my makeup and beauty supplies in one place. I can even put my makeup brushes in here and not have to cramp the bristles.

The makeup in this set is amazing. It is one of my favorite brands and I love that I could buy the set online without having to purchase a very expensive product at the makeup counter in order to add this on to an order. I like being able to sample many different products this way and have been happy with all of them. The remover is excellent and very gentle. The face wash works well and makes my skin feel great. There is an eye cream which brightens the peepers and a moisturizer which is rich and effective without clogging my pores. The colors in the mini-palette are divine...neutral enough to be worn every day but unique and make a statement if I go heavier for a night look. The set came with both a lipstick and a gloss which is the first one I have found like that. I have probably done the GWP offer 3 or 4 times in stores but this set had way more products than I have ever gotten that way. Love the shades and the quality is unquestionable.

I would absolutely buy this set again... next time I will try one with a different colored bag and new shades for a change, but I will be happy to have a new set when these bottles run out. It's such a great way to experience all the products without paying retail for full sizes. I purchased this set at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review and all opinions are my own after personal use.

review_text: It was a risk ordering a clothing item from overseas with no reviews to rely on--so here's one for you. The listing says to check their size chart for accurate fitting. I did so. I'm sure that would improve with washing, but since I'm not keeping it, there's no way to know. The only reason for 2 stars instead of 1 is I still think the design is cute. I wish it actually fit. I'm guessing by the fit (I bought a large), I would actually have to buy an XXL, even though the measurements given project otherwise. review_title: creates a bulge around the top
review_text:
I'm 5'4" and 145lbs. I received the M/L size for review, and they are nice, but they barely fit. The sizes are listed as:
S/M = 5'0"-5'4" and 90-140 lbs
M/L = 5'4"-5'10" and 130-180lbs
X/L = 5'7"-6" and 170-210

So, at my ht and wt I am at the very low end of the scale for the M/L. I should have probably been able to get the S/M, but I went up a size instead. Even with stretching the things tight, the crotch region doesn't actually reach my crotch; there is a gap. Also, I was hoping that the way the butt area is designed, that it would provide some lift, but it doesn't.

Lastly, my main complaint with these things is that the waist band come up very high (3 inches under my breast) and is much tighter than the area directly under the band. So, there is not enough "control" in the control top, but the waist band area is tight. This leads to the creation of bulges, particularly a slight muffin top. It isn't bad, but I don't normally have those bulges, so to have panty hose that are meant to control stomach fat actually create a bulge, it's a little annoying.

They either need to make the band looser, or the control top tighter.

I received this item as sample for review, either free or at a discount. I am keeping it for permanent personal use. These are my honest thoughts.

One gentleman in particular, who happened to be sweating profusely, assured me that his bandana gave him the power of invisibility.  At least, I believe that's what he said.  It was hard to understand him with the copious amounts of mushrooms he was stuffing into his mouth, a rather odd decision based on his obvious lack of pizza.  He also complained that his blotter was too strong, but I paid him no mind.  Who uses typewriters these days anyways?  In conclusion, it's a pretty dope do rag, but I was told immediately and in no uncertain terms that I was quite visible when I attempted to walk nude through my neighborhood shortly after using some eye drops kindly provided to me by the aforementioned gentleman.

product_name: Chun Zheng Men's Winter Casual Down Hooded Warm Jacket
review_title: Nicely made, good quality materials, but runs VERY small and has a trim cut
review_text:
This jacket has a lot going for it -- great build quality for the price, and a nice, understated overall look. The biggest problem is the fit. This is a jacket for very thin people!

The construction quality is very good -- I was unable to find any loose threads, all seams were tight and even, and the cuffs and waist band are well-made and comfortable. Both the outer material and the lining feel substantial and able to withstand a decent amount of wear and tear. The pockets are positioned for easy access and have good quality snaps to close them. It came tightly bundled up in a package, but it unfolded and plumped up very quickly.

The only so-so item in terms of quality is the zipper. It has nice, chunky teeth, but the pull tab is on the small side, and the entire zipper is plastic.

I like the overall look. It's very simple (solid black) but with a nice contrasting checkerboard lining pattern. The hood is attached and, in an odd design choice, the zipper runs the full length of the hood, so you could, technically, zip yourself totally within the hood.

The biggest problem is the fit. I knew that this would run small, so I got it as an XXL (I normally take either a L jacket if it's dressy, and an XL if I want a more casual, baggy look). Even as an XXL, this is tight in the chest and shoulders. I have a pretty slim build, and I find the fit constraining. This jacket is completely unworkable if you have a good amount of meat on your bones.

The sleeve length is fine, as is the overall coat length. It's just cut for a very, very slim built person even in the XXL size.

It's hard to judge the warmth since it's summer, but the material bulk feels like it would be a fine coat for fall in any climate, and would be OK in winter if you live in a more mild climate.

At this price point, it easily is worth a 5-star rating for construction, 5-stars for material quality, and 5-stars for overall look. However, the fit/cut is a 1 star. Overall rating is 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 given the price point. However, this rating comes with the STRONG caveat that if you're not super slim, don't get this coat even if you size up to XXL.

product_name: Whoinshop Women's Rayon Fading Color Strapless Bodycon Party Cocktail Bandage Dress
review_title: No Need for Tape or Spanx!
review_text: I loved the ombre purple in the picture of this bandage dress so much that I, who hate wearing strapless, took a risk and bought it. It was the right thing to do! Unlike my previous strapless experiences, this dress lets me reach for things without a \\"wardrobe malfunction\\"! :) The secret is that not only are there compressing, skin-tight bandages, but there is also an exposed strip of elastic inside, at the very top of the dress. It comfortably clings to my skin and doesn't slide down. I tested the dress by reaching up several times and it stayed put. No need for tape or keeping my arms glued to my sides all night! The stretchiness also makes ironing unnecessary. Yay!    I'm a bit of an exhibitionist, so I bought a small and am happy with it. I'm 5 feet 7 inches, 126 pounds, 34B-26-36. Like any bodycon bandage dress, this one really holds and hugs almost every curve. No need for Spanx! I said \\"almost\\" because there are no cups in this dress. If you go braless and have natural breasts, they will look a bit flattened. I'm OK with that. In case you're curious, the full-length back zipper is set into two exposed, medium purple, vertical bandages.    The bandages are sturdy, high-quality. However, on my monitor, some of the bandage colors are different from those in the actual dress. In the actual dress, the bottom bandage is white. The two bandages just above it are a beige-y pink. Then there are three pairs of slightly different light purples. The rest looks just like the picture. Because it was the top purples, the triangle in the middle, and the ombre effect that I liked most, these color differences don't matter to me.    I haven't had an opportunity to air this dress out, but fresh out of the bag, it has a bit of a rubbery smell. It's the only reason I'm giving this gorgeous dress 4 stars instead of 5.

product_name: Wrangler Authentics Men's Classic Carpenter Jean
review_title: Functional - fit me a little large but otherwise a nice pair
review_text:
I have to start off by saying I am not a fan of the Wrangler brand. But these jeans - they just might have made a believer out of me.
-
I am SUPER picky when if comes to jeans. I hate shopping for them, because nothing kills your spirit more than grabbing a pair of jeans that are in your size, only to have them impossible to zip up, leaving you feeling like a fat lard. I'm a 34" waist, dammit! I also hate bad denim. There are a million ways to make and treat denim used for jeans, and the stuff that Levi's and Wrangler put out feel like cardboard. I have never liked them.
-
But - this pair you're looking at here - not too shabby. I'm a 34"x30", straight up. But when wearing boots, I need a 32" leg. I put these on and they fit well around the waist. But they're a bit baggy down below. The page here doesn't say, but these are definitely "boot cut" - they're pretty big on the ends there, and they're awfully long, for me. I usually need a 32" leg for boots, but these hit the floor, even with my boots on. They fit well in the waist-area, but the legs are baggy. Which, I suppose, is good for working. The jeans also have these little pockets behind the right knee - good for jamming a tool in there when you have nowhere else to put it. There's also a little hanger-thing on the left leg for a hammer. I'm sure there's a name for it - shows you what I know about blue-collar work. Hey - there's a reason why my sink leaks, ok!?!!
-
The material isn't smooth denim - it's a little rough but still comfortable. For the price, these are a really nice pair for working in.

I cannot express enough how much I love these shirts! Firstly, if you are used to wearing the maternity clothing and t-shirts currently out there, these will be large for you. I was not a fan of seeing other maternity shirts fit like a glove. Yes, I think it's great to "show off the bump", but when your bump isn't showing even in the 2nd trimester because you are already fluffers, I don't like the idea of having a 2nd skin to show off my fluff. :D hehe
Most maternity shirts fit like a "girls/women's" t-shirt, where the manufacturers believe you should be thin, have no boobs and no broad shoulders, and adore sleeves that might as well not be there because they are so short. All I wanted, were some cute maternity shirts that fit like my regular t-shirts... and Crazy Dog has done it. :) My chest and shoulders don't feel like I have to rake a shirt over them (and when you're pregnant with sore boobs, that's no bueno), and this thinner, super soft material is just what I need. Also being a bit warmer nowadays, I appreciate not roasting in an overly thick cotton t-shirt as well.

Overall, my rating is a 5 star on the Woot scale! ;D

review_text:
My review is based solely on the physical affects from this product.

The recommended dose is 2.5 tbsp and I used 1 heaping tbsp in a smoothie I make everyday, this was the only difference.

I started getting jittery and somewhat anxious feeling within an hour or so. I also had a mild headache which lasted quite some time.

Some people seem to be sensitive to this, especially those with adrenal issues.

As far as the taste, it was decent. Nothing like what I imagined. Kind of bitter and just bland. Very dry tasting if that makes sense.

review_text: I went to my local Walmart this evening and purchased a bag of these dates. When I opened the bag in Walmart's parking lot, I nearly threw it across my car. Why? It looked like some kind of tiny alien pod/bug was emerging from one of the dates.  Curiosity, however, outweighed my desire to hurl the package of "pitted" dates into my windshield. I picked up a few more and they all had this weird pod-looking thing inside. It took me a solid two minutes to determine what I was actually looking at was a PIT  (Like I said, I've never seen a date and the bag said "pitted" on the front). I would understand if maybe one or two slipped through the cracks with their mutant-esque pits intact, but why do I have an entire bag of these tiny pit-filled abominations when they cost nearly $4 per package?

review_text: I first found this water at Starbucks and immediately became addicted to it! I can not drink anything with artificial sugars because of severe and chronic migraines. So, when I came across this water, I was a little skeptical thinking that it would be like all the other flavored waters out on the market and offensive to my taste. But, I was pleasantly surprised when I found that true to its name, there is just a little hint of the Blackberry flavor, my favorite fruit btw, and refreshing water. Living in the South, it's always nice to find a refreshing drink that isn't heavy and to be honest, water can get pretty boring even to a person who drinks a lot of water like I do. I have really liked the other flavors also but this one is completely DISGUSTING!!!!! I want to return it and exchange it for a different Hint Water. Thankfully, our main grocery store and health store do carry several of the Hint waters but I still order at least two cases every couple of weeks and at the end of the month I place s large order. This last month, I decided, why not be a little adventurous and try other flavors. So, I ordered several other flavors that I knew in the past I had added to actual glasses of water and enjoyed. Cucumber was one of them. THIS is the ONLY Hint water that is absolutely disgusting for me!!!! I am not sure what it is but the aftertaste so yucky it's like the bitter peel of the cucumber left in your mouth. Nope, this water is really not for me at all!!!!elming in the very least. It's a wonderful find and a great buy.

product_name: Joyva Tahini 15 ounces
review_text:
I've used and liked this brand a lot in the past when I could buy it locally where I used to live. Where I live now, I can't find tahini at all, so as you can imagine I was happy to find it here on Amazon even if it is pricey. The tahini has always been creamy before and easy to mix the oil in (refrigerate after to mixing to avoid further separation). However, that was not the case with the product I received yesterday. I was shocked to see how HARD the solids were. I actually had to use a knife to cut them into pieces. There was no way I could mix this by hand. Instead, I poured everything into my food processor with the knife blade in place and processed it for quite a while. Anyone who buys this product knows there is no open "best by" or "sell by" date, though there is a closed code on the top of the can, whatever it might mean. But, I'm convinced this product is OLD, having sat around for a LONG time for the solids to have congealed into a hard mass that needs to be cut apart. I'm very disappointed with my purchase. The only reason I gave it two stars in this review is because I could get it to a creamy state with the food processor.

UPDATE: Amazon did its level best to make this right. They sent me another can of the tahini. Unfortunately, I found the same problem, hard as a rock. So, it's not an Amazon problem, and it's not a Joyva problem. It's a problem with the stock the Online Grocery Outlet provided Amazon for distribution. Next time, I will buy it from another source on Amazon.

review_text: As a child, my grandmother forced me to drink the original V8 veggie juice. Needless to say, I hated it. So I was hesitant to try the V8 V-Fusion + Energy. However, looking for a healthy alternative to my daily coffee, I decided to give it a try. I received a coupon for a free 6 pack from V8 V-Fusion Energy. I had my heart set on the Black Cherry flavor, but I couldn't find it at Target, Walgreens, or my local grocery store. So I settled for the Pomegranate Blueberry. The packaging really stands out among the other energy drinks, as the V8 logo screams, "healthy". On a particularly exhausting afternoon, I gave the drink a try. The first sip tasted...less than desirable. But as I continued drinking the can, the flavor grew on me. To be fair, I'm not really a pomegranate fan, but again, this was the only flavor available. The green tea definitely gave me a boost of energy. Not as much as a cup of coffee, but just enough wake me up without feeling jittery. I skipped my usual afternoon cat nap that day and was able to continue running my errands. Overall, the V8 V-Fusion + Energy delivered on energy, but not on taste. I'm going to keep looking for the other flavors and maybe I'll find one that I like and will stick with.

review_title: Combination of chocolate and caramel comes up smell and flavorless
review_text:
Normally I would have eaten more than the 4-5 cookies out of the bag. I ate two, then another. Then I waited a few days and ate another two. Still no bueno. As to the aroma, I can smell something that smells a lot like artificial butter flavoring. I have smelled the bag over and over again, and individual cookies, too. All I can come up with is "faintly buttery" but that butter is about to go bad. It doesn't smell like dulce de leche.
In the name of science and fairness, I took a sharp knife and sliced the cookie in half. Interestingly enough, the chocolate layer side and the caramel layer side separated neatly, which gives you a clue as to how these are made. I tasted the chocolate, the chocolate with the cookie, the caramel, and the caramel with the cookie. All of those were okay. The chocolate was much better than the caramel. But since the caramel was okay by itself, and somewhat okay with the cookie, I conclude that the chocolate flavor and caramel flavor simply do not go well together here.
When eaten as an intact cookie, I can't taste anything that is remotely like caramel. Or chocolate for that matter. The combination ruins everything. Sometimes it's a marriage made in heaven and sometimes, well you get it. I I love caramel, and I love dulce de leche everything. But not these cookies. Too bad!
I'm sure Pepperidge Farm did loads of taste tests and product research on these. But it comes up short for me. Try them for yourself and reply to me either way. I predict these will be bought up for a bit and then go into obscurity as people go back to their old stand-by's. I hope they'll try again, though, and will look for the Improved Flavor notice on the package in case they do.

review_text:
When you get a good bag of Blue Horse kona, it's really good coffee. Unfortunately, I don't feel I can count on it to be consistently good. I've purchased it twice now, and the first time it was heavenly. However, the second purchase was a totally different experience. The first couple pots from the bag were fine, nothing special. But after that, the beans lost their aroma, the coffee started tasting sour, and I have had to throw the rest away. An expensive few cups of coffee!

I stored the coffee and prepared it exactly the same way as before. I have no idea what may have happened. Perhaps the beans were exposed to extraordinary heat during the shipping, causing them to spoil. I don't know.

I emailed Blue Horse to let them know of this experience, and while they were apologetic that it happened, they couldn't offer any explanation, nor did they offer a replacement or refund.

It pains me to write this review. I had been so excited and looking forward to enjoying this coffee as my weekend treat. The cost means it's not something I can do for myself but a few times a year. I won't be purchasing from Blue Horse again because I simply can't afford to throw away $36.

What is pasture-raised?
Pasture Raised with Love! In a way cows are like kids – the more time outside the better. Our farmers send their cows out into lush, organic pastures for fresh air, exercise and grazing (weather permitting of course). Our Pasture-Raised™ animals receive the majority of their nutrition from organically managed pastures and stored dried grasses/forages. To ensure they get the complete nutrition they need, our cows may also be fed supplemental organic grains, both during the grazing season and into winter months.

Supplemental organic grains can include any of the following: corn, soy, oats, barley, triticale and other small grains. Animals also receive necessary mineral supplements that sometimes include non-iodized salt.

product_name: Skippy Creamy Peanut Butter, 64 Ounce (Pack of 2)
review_title: In no way will I be referring to the nutrition label or ingredient list like many people do for these reviews
review_text:
First of all, this review has nothing to do with health factors of peanut butter or the “naturalness” of peanut butter. All this review is about is taste and quality. In no way will I be referring to the nutrition label or ingredient list like many people do for these reviews, just taste.
Skippy Peanut butter is always a favorite among kids and I remember having the tubes of Skippy peanut butter as a kid. You may ask yourself, what is the main reason for this? The answer is clear; Skippy is so much sweeter than any other peanut butter on the market that kids can’t get enough of it. But most of us college students want something more savory and that has that classic peanut butter taste. Skippy is simply just far too sweet to handle for me.
Another reason that I cannot handle Skippy is the texture. When I but creamy peanut butter, I expect creaminess. However, when I stuck a knife into the jar of Skippy, the peanut butter gave far too much resistance. This is not only a problem with accessibility, but with distribution. If a peanut butter is too thick, it can tear bread apart and nobody likes his or her pb&j sandwiches to be ripped up.
One last thing about Skippy is the cost. A 64 oz. jar of Skippy is about $9, while a 4lb jar of Jif peanut butter is the same cost. That is more peanut butter of a higher quality for the same cost. To me that just doesn’t make any sense. So in conclusion, If you really want a top of the line peanut butter that is just the right amount of creamy and has the classic peanut butter flavor that everyone loves, reach for Jif and you will not be disappointed.

product_name: LINDT: 99% Cocoa Excellence Bar: 12 Count
review_title: Decent taste, but very expensive and reduced health benefits
review_text:
I love dark chocolate because of its taste *and* health benefits. Cocoa is a good source of antioxidants such as flavonoids which, among other things, provide beneficial effects for cardiovascular health. Alas, a high cocoa content in dark chocolate is not necessarily a guaranty for these health benefits, because some vendors process their cocoa powder with alkali (Dutch Processing), which destroys a significant fraction of before mentioned flavonoids. This 99% Lindt, as well as the 90% variant, unfortunately belong to this category.

Thus, if you are looking for health and taste, the 85% cocoa Lindt is the best product to buy from this brand. If mere taste is most important, this may be your chocolate bar. Dutch Processing creates a darker color and smoother flavor.

Lastly, this chocolate is very expensive, compared to other Lindt dark chocolate bars, like the 90% or 85%. It's not just almost twice the price, but also half the weight per bar (only 1.8oz = 50g), while the package size stays the same. Fascinating.

product_name: Idris Fiery Ginger Beer - 330 ml Can
review_text:
Over the last year, I've become something of a ginger connoisseur. I started with ginger beers, then graduated to crystallized ginger, ginger snaps, ginger-based nutritional supplements, and Indian curry sauces drizzled with ginger. And I must say, I've encountered few new products which demonstrate just how good, or just how bad, ginger can be, than [[ASIN:B0077PAUVA Idris Fiery Ginger Beer]] and [[ASIN:B00KGC89FK Gosling's Ginger Beer]].

I bought one of each at a British imports store in a local downtown, from a cooler wedged between a rack of Doctor Who DVDs and a display of Premier League logo scarves. As you'd expect, these both follow the mainly British recipe of sweet ginger brews which you can drink straight from the package. This as opposed to North American ginger ale, such as Canada Dry, which is almost sugarless and too dry for use as anything but a mixer.

That, sadly, is where the similarities end. Gosling's is a complex, flavorful ginger beer, which isn't overly sweetened, but leaves a lingering ginger flavor in your mouth. It's almost a coating sensation, like you've been holding candied ginger under your tongue. Though not \\"fiery,\\" it has a spicy taste and a robust finish I've encountered mainly in two other brands: Barritts and Ginger People. Whether you prefer a non-alcoholic late nite drink or a Moscow Mule, Gosling's won't disappoint.

Wish I could say the same about Idris. When something promises to be \\"fiery,\\" I really expect it to burn going down. I snack on pickled jalapeños, so my standards of spice are pretty high. This is about as \\"fiery\\" as a microwaved burrito from an all-night convenience store. Worse, although it promises ginger root extract in the ingredients list, I could barely taste any. A prior reviewer called this the worst ginger beer ever. I doubt that, since I've tried Cock & Bull. But heavens, this ain't good.

Both varieties advertise themselves as good cocktail mixers. Idris suggests mixing half-n-half with regular beer to make a shandy, while Gosling's claims they're formulated for making a Dark 'n' Stormy. I have no idea what the latter even is. However, I'll say this: Gosling's tastes great straight. Since I want something non-alcoholic and non-caffeinated to take my late night supplements, Gosling's works. Idris just tastes like sugar water. I know which I'll have again.ts mixing half-n-half with regular beer to make a shandy, while Gosling's claims they're formulated for making a Dark 'n' Stormy. I have no idea what the latter even is. However, I'll say this: Gosling's tastes great straight. Since I want something non-alcoholic and non-caffeinated to take my late night supplements, Gosling's works. Idris just tastes like sugar water. I know which I'll have again.

product_name: JIF Peanut Butter Creamy 40 oz Jar (2 Pack)
review_text:
When I was growing up, my grandmother used Jif peanut butter as she read that it was ranked as the best peanut butter among the main brands. Having worked with a nutritionist, she recommended that I buy the Teddy's brand of peanut butter as there are no added ingredients. She also said to refrigerate it after opening it to keep the nutrition in the peanut butter. As Dr. Oz said on Oprah, he keeps his nuts in the frig and then wondered why the audience laughed.

When I looked at the ingredients in this Jif peanut butter, was disappointed to see added ingredients as follows:

made from roasted peanuts and sugar, contains 2 percent or less of molasses, fully hydrogenated vegetable oils (rapeseed and soybean ), mono and diglycerides, salt.

Jif's makers should make a healthy version of this peanut butter for those of us who don't want sugar, diglycerides and added salt. In the meantime, I'll be buying Teddy's peanut butter.

review_text: It's unfortunate that the vendor does not state that this TVP product is completely UNFLAVORED otherwise, I believe the reviews would be better. When you buy TVP that is labeled "chicken" or "beef", etc. you expect it to be seasoned to mimic those tastes.  If it's unflavored, as this product is, it is typically labeled as such because you're expected to decide what you want it to taste like and then, season it yourself.  I purchased this product in its "chunk" form (not actually these dish-shaped strips - which actually aren't strips, at all) and cooked up a batch and was very pleasantly surprised at the authentic texture - but again, was disappointed that it was completely unseasoned.  After a quick fix with a serving of McKay's "chicken" seasoning and a dab of soy sauce, this made a very satisfying chicken-like product that holds together well and can be added to pasta dishes, soup or stews successfully.

review_text:
This 5 pound bag of almond flour from Morning Pep is the one you should buy if you know how to use almond flour in your baking because this is not an alternative flour that you can just substitute in for whole grain or traditionally processed wheat flour; the results will simply not be the same. You'll have to experiment more to see how much more liquid you'll need to add. Be careful, the batter seems similar to whole wheat flour batters but is it more gritty and it will not react to heat the same as wheat flour at all.

The positives here are that this is organic, that it is gluten free, and that the bag is resealable for easy storage which is important when you get so much flour and may need to store it for several months before you've use it all.

review_text: Let me first say that for flavor, I give this 4 stars, maybe even 5. It's very hot, but with purpose and the flavor really comes through. It's not just hot for the sake of being hot. I have a very high tolerance for heat and it definitely got me going.  For texture though, this jerky is a 2 star at best, maybe even 1 star. It is TOUGH! When I say tough, this jerky is like chewing on tree bark. I don't mind tough jerky in general, but I really hard a hard time with this. It wasn't so hard it was like a jaw breaker, but it's quite difficult to bite into and is a chore to eat. I got the 8oz so it's two 4oz packs. I haven't even touched the 2nd pack due to how difficult the 1st one was to chew. So to recap, 4-5 stars on flavor, 1-2 stars on texture, so a 3 star overall. BTW, a word of warning: It's very oily, and it seems like it's pretty much straight capsaicin oil, so use dish detergent to wash your hand thoroughly after, and don't touch any sensitive areas for a while.

product_name: Quaker Chewy Granola Bar
review_title: Current Nutrition Facts And Ingredients........... See Photos~
review_text:
Since my husband and I love our Old Fashioned Quaker Oats and are constantly trying new snack bars, I was stoked when I found these bars with a coupon running... I went ahead and added them to our Subscribe and Save order for the additional savings and thought these were a steal! A total of 48 bars for under $7, not bad at all...

I didn't pay too much attention to the reviews or nutrition facts and ingredients, since they were such a steal. I'm uploading some photos to include all of the current info, along with an idea of just how tiny these bars are. Essentially they are two to three bites each.

While they are just enough to satify a sweet tooth (and between the chocolate and peanut butter, of course taste wonderful!), they really pack a lot of combined sugars and carbs.

Although they are free of High Fructose Corn Syrup, if you were to eat two of them, making them more the size of most protein type bars, you'd have 44 effective carbs. And still you would be eating under 1.7 oz, which really isn't a whole lot.

The ingredient list being so lengthy, I don't think these are non GMO. They do not contain some of the ingredients other prior reviews mentioned so it seems the facts have been updated. They are quite delicious little snacks but I still would not choose them for being the healthiest of choices.

You can see in the photos that the box is nicely designed, with perforation for easy access to bars from the pantry. Even considering the value to be more like 24 bars, in my opinion, these are still a great value with the current pricing.

I rated these three stars, primarily because of their size and nutrition facts. Based soley on flavor, I'd give them five stars and would say they are worth trying if you're not super carb conscious or gluten sensitive. Smile. Hope this is helpful!

review_text:
I received a coupon to try these for free via BzzAgent in exchange for my honest review.

I am definitely a coffee girl through and through, but I was interested to try these V8 V-Fusion® +Energy Drinks. It has a full serving of fruits and veggies, B Vitamins and Vitamins A+C, and no added sugars. Unlike most energy drinks around, these have natural energy from green tea giving you 80 mg of caffeine in each can. (For comparison, an 8 oz. cup of brewed coffee has 90 mg of caffeine.)

The verdict? Delicious! I tried the Peach Mango flavor and it truly tasted like fruit juice. As for the energy factor, I didn’t notice a difference… but I didn’t notice a change from not having my usual cup of coffee, so that’s a plus!

Overall would I buy these on my own? Probably not very often, I definitely prefer coffee instead… but some days you need an afternoon pick-me-up and you don’t always feel like coffee, so I would consider these. A nice change of flavor… But not something I would buy regularly.

review_title: I Would Like It A Lot Better With Less Salt And A Little Less Cheese.
review_text:
Pepperidge Farm Goldfish, Flavor Blasted Xtra Cheddar, 6.6-ounce (187g) bag (pack of 8) by Pepperidge Farm Goldfish [Foods], from Pepperidge Farm.
These Goldfish Xtra Cheddar crackers are good, but the extra cheddar is too much of a good thing. I liked the regular Goldfish crackers better. To me, Goldfish crackers are similar to Sunshine Cheez-It crackers, just in a different shape. Both companies produce a number of different cracker varieties to try to be a little different from the competition. You need to compare the cracker companies' cracker styles side by side, to see which ones that you prefer. From a food standpoint, these Pepperidge Farm Xtra Cheddar crackers are a bit too cheesy (though not in a bad way, just too much cheese) to suit me. And for anyone on a low salt diet, they are way too salty as well, at 270mg of salt in a serving of 1.1 ounces. Three Amazon stars.

review_title: The sun sure didn't have any mercy on these.
review_text:
I don't eat a whole lot of chocolates any more, but when something new comes around, I give it a shot.

Quick note- the chocolates arrived to me with over half of them melted, being reduced to half the size of their individual plastic wrapped sizes. It wasn't a pretty sight when I opened the mailing envelope and saw chocolate oozing from the sides of the box.

Of the batch, my favorite was Praline Cream. I've never had this before and when I took a small bite from the piece, I was hooked and took out the rest of it, and the second one in no time. All the others...to be honest, were pretty plain. If I hadn't read the wrappers or anything on the box, I wouldn't have really known what it was that the others were supposed to be. Most of them tasted like regular chocolates to me. Granted, at this price point, you can't expect anything extravagant or mind blowing, but it sure isn't the "finest" Europe has to offer by any stretch of the definition. And some of this might be because of the whole melting thing. Either way, I wasn't that impressed.

If I ever get around to buying another box of these, and they aren't melted and I end up liking them, I'll update this review. Until then, I just see this as a basic chocolates in a fancy cigar box-looking presentation. Well, melted cigars anyway.

product_name: Numi Organic Black Tea, Loose Leaf Tea
review_text:
I'm not a tea expert, but have been drinking for 5+ years now. I'm used to some of the standard nicer green and white teas: Jasmine Pearls and Silver White Needle. I mention this, because the taste of this Gunpowder floored me, compared to the lightness of those other two. I didn't realize that a green tea could taste so heavy. I steeped it under 176 degrees, to avoid the strength of the tannins, but, wow, this had a very smoky flavor. I couldn't rate it down for this, because that may very well be the true flavor of the tea -- I just am not a fan of it. I've purchased the Numi mint, in an attempt to balance out the harshness of this Gunpowder. I've read on another site that blending the two makes a 'Moroccan Mint' -- Numi does label their mint tea with that name, but the ingredients show only mint and no Gunpowder. I hope the mint tea will truly be as "light" and "sweet" as their description claims, in order to counter the overwhelming smokiness. There are mixed reviews on the mint -- very love/hate.

UPDATE 5/29/15
I've received the Numi Mint and I think it is a nice light flavor, that adds a balance to the Gunpowder. I drink the Mint on its own, as well as blending it with the Gunpowder to make the Moroccan Mint. I'm not sure how true to the real Moroccan Mint this is, but it salvages my pound of Gunpowder. For what it's worth, I step the Mint first at 208- degrees, for 3-4 minutes, then add the Gunpowder to the same water, once the temp has gone down to 176-, and step no more than 2 minutes.

product_name: Bulksupplements Pure Stevia Powder
review_title: tastes great, had issues with dissolving, but resolved
review_text: I'm a longtime user of Trader Joe's stevia extract powder.  I got the BulkSupplements stevia extract powder to try for free and review.  Well, the flavor is fine, but it has difficulty dissolving.  The Trader Joe's stevia is called a powder, but the BulkSupplements stevia is more like dust or flour.  It's almost too fine, so it tends to clump when added to liquids, whether hot, cold, or room temp.  Since it is so super fine, it takes even less than the TJ's.  So, where two of the teeny weeny scoops of the TJ's would be just right, only one scoop of the BulkSupplements stevia was needed.  I first used the same amount, and it was too sweet.  I tried mixing half TJ's and half BulkSupplements stevia together before adding to liquid, and there was still clumping.  It did eventually dissolve, with lots of stirring.  I have found a similar effect with spices, such as onion powder or garlic powder.  They're called powders, but they're actually tiny little granules.  If they are actually powders, with a flour or dust-like fineness, they tend to clump and not dissolve well.  For the quantity and sweetening power, the BulkSupplements stevia extract powder is a great deal!  TJ's, or Now brand 100% stevia extract powder goes for about $10/oz.  I'm pleased to have been offered this product to try and review.  If I had purchased it, I might be more distressed at the way it dissolves.  I'll continue working with it, but I'm unsure if I'll purchase this in the future.  Some folks find an unpleasant aftertaste with stevia, and some don't.  I've only found an unpleasant aftertaste when using products that are not 100% pure stevia, that have other stuff added, like inulin or dextrose.  Stick with 100% pure stevia for best results.  Update: Jan. 2016  I got some erythritol to mix with this stevia powder, and it's worked out great.  I mix two tablespoons of erythritol (Swerve brand) and one tablespoon plus two teaspoons of the Bulk Supplements stevia powder.  It's just the right sweetness, dissolves well, and, I think, works out pretty good cost-wise.  I'm now getting low on the stevia powder, but have quite a bit of the erythritol left.  (Erythritol by itself tastes weird, and gives a strange cooling sensation/mouth-feel.)  I will probably re-order this stevia powder.  Update 2-4-16.   I ordered more of this stevia, planning on mixing it with erythritol again, but I don't need to.  This batch is dissolving much more readily than the one I got previously.  Yay!  Tastes great.  Also, this package has info I don't recall being on the previous batch. (Maybe it was there and I didn't see it.)  It says:  stevia extract....40mg.    steviol glycosides...38 mg (per 40 mg serving).  Rebaudiosides...22mg (per 40 mg serving). On their website it shows Stevia extract...40mg.    Steviol glycosides 90% 38mg.   Steviosides...35mg.    Rebaudiosides...16mg

product_name: Ghirardelli Chocolate Sauce, Black Label (16oz Squeeze bottle)
review_title: Intense chocolate in a great bottle - but could it be overkill for your mochas?
review_text:
I make mocha at home on a daily basis, and I always have at least one bottle of chocolate syrup/sauce in the kitchen. I have tried Hershey's, Nestle, and Torani as they are the only accessible items in local stores. Knowing Ghirardelli brand, I decided to give this one a try.

The bottle design is something separates this one from all the others. It has a special tip that prevents spillage and mess. Not a drop stays outside of that tip after a firm squeeze.

Comparing to other 3 I mentioned above, it smells, tastes, and looks more like chocolate. However this level of quality is something I have to adjust to. Unlike Hershey's or Nestle, this sauce is denser. Meaning, it is harder to incorporate with beverages (like mocha). Being more like natural chocolate, it is not as sweet as other brands. If you add more of the sauce, you will end up with dark chocolate taste which takes over the coffee flavor. I think I need to use less but add a little sweetener. I have used it 3-4 times, and I still haven't perfected the ratios for my taste.

It doesn't require refrigeration as long as it's in a dry & cool place, but it is recommended that you use within 3 weeks of opening the bottle.

Considering price, accessibility, and taste I think Torani and Nestle are better value overall for me as a mocha consumer. But, if you are looking for a high quality chocolate sauce, this is it. I don't recommend Hershey's as it tastes the worst among 4, and also the only one that contains High Fructose Corn Syrup.

review_title: good taste and decent texture for a GF item
review_text:
These are a little hard compared to wheat crackers, but for a gluten free product, the texture is not bad. These are pretty thin and they taste really salty. So it is amazing to me that one serving only has 135 mg of sodium. That's much lower than I expected based on taste (which is a good thing).

I like how a lot of the grains in these are whole grains (i.e., brown rice flour, whole grain yellow corn) instead of just simple starches. In my experience, starchy (and non-whole-grain) GF products are easier to come by than versions with some whole grains. These are fairly low in fat and have a little fiber and protein. You can see the full ingredients list and nutrition facts panel in the product images.

Because these are pretty salty, you would want to use savory spreads or dips if you are going that direction. (And don't use anything that will conflict with the flavor of sesame seeds, because that is definitely noticeable here.) Cheese and hummus would both be good. These are also vegetarian. And they don't stick in or on your teeth after eating, unlike some other crackers I've had lately!

Overall, I love the flavor and the texture is something I can live with. Even though I don't need to eat GF, I would seriously consider buying these again.

I found the product to work well on my recipe and look forward to trying it in a few others.  I don't see this sauce being something I use as a dip. review_title: Amazingly good for coffee out of a can.  Locally roasted here in So Cal.
review_text:
I'm amazed.
My coffee obsession is such that I buy and roast my own beans, have been on and off for 20 years. I have most every type of brewer.
When I don't roast my own, I buy Peet's beans locally, there's a Peet's down the street from me.
I hate charcoal burned coffee- people drinking it, is to me a sign that they have no idea what they're doing. Drinking cups filled with hot milk, flavored with a few drops of charcoal coffee. I'm talking about Starbucks, most of what Peets sells, most of what the "craft" roasters make. The Peets blend that I drink is Cafe Solano, what they call "light roast". It is similar to a northern Italian roast, pioneered by Ernesto Illy.
Speaking of Illy, the only canned coffee I would ever consider drinking is Illy Caffe medium roast. I keep a box of Illy medium roast ESE pods around for my espresso machine for extreme emergencies. 100% of the canned coffee in Italy is absolute stale swill other than Illy, so when I travel there, one of the first things I do is buy a few cans. The worst of course is Lavazza. Absolute swill. They brag that "Lavazza is the #1 coffee in Italy". Sure maybe, but you can also say that "Wonder Bread is the #1 bread in America". Not much to brag about.
So, no canned coffee for me other than Illy. Until now. I was at an awards dinner last week, one of the gift bag items was a can of this Gavina espresso. I thought to myself, "uh, huh. probably swill", but I was out of beans over the weekend, so I cracked it open and loaded up the Bialetti moka pot. Holy Arabica Batman, it's not over roasted, it's fresh and aromatic, it's very well blended and nothing sticks out at you to ruin the experience. No charcoal, no wine-y sourness, no aftertaste, etc. Just good coffee.
The first pot was of course the best, when the can was first opened. Now 3 days later it's showing it's age and getting oxidized so I hope I finish it before it gets completely stale.
I hope Amazon starts selling this again.

review_title: Not an all-arounder, but paired with the right gin, it's sublime.
review_text:
After getting a SodaStream we wanted to make our own tonic water for G&Ts, and this one's tasting reviews sounded like we would like it. The manufacturer says it was designed to pair well with Beefeater, but we didn't have any of that in the houses. So we tried it with Bombay Sapphire (usually our favorite gin) and it was … meh. Kind of watery, sort of dull. But then we tried it with Hendrick's gin, and it was just WOW! It opened up like nothing I've ever tasted--floral and complex and wonderful. It was so much better than routine grocery store tonic water.
