review_title: Chrysanthemum Buds Tea, I find Refreshing
review_text:
Just received my tea today! It arrived in a small tin with the tea and a bag clip. There are two clear round sticker things that hold the tin lid for shipping so you need to remove those first. I cut the bag open with scissors and inside you find the dried flowers.

I did not see any instructions so I decided to try 4 flowers to 8 ounces at first. I find this makes a nicely mild tea that does not require any sweeter. It is really mild made this way. When I went to make a second cup I noticed there are English instructions on the bottom of the tin!! lol Says to stop in a shady, dry place (no strong orders in air) and to brew with 5-10 bugs in 250ml (1 cup) of warm water for 3 minutes.

So I did that next but did not wait 3 minutes because I do not like strong tea. I brewed it about 1.5 minutes. Very tasty!!! I used my French Press to brew the tea since I do not have an infuser. Works great!

The description of the Chrysanthemum tea is "bitter sweet" . Brewed mildly I personally do not really get a bitter flavor. I did let it seep longer and as it sits, to me the flavor becomes strong and then it is bitter to me.

Overall I really like this tea and am sipping on it as I write this post. I think this is going to become a favorite for me.

I did receive this tea at a discount for the purpose of testing and was asked to write an unbiased review when I was done testing. All of my reviews are uninfluenced by the vendors as I just enjoy helping out shoppers.

review_title: Great for a lazy BBQ day!
review_text:
I don't know about anyone else, but I'm the guy who is willing to take the 45 minutes to an hour to either get the Kingsford charcoal going or will use the smoker for a good steak. However, sometimes my family isn't willing to wait the 45 minutes to an hour for steak and honestly, sometimes I just get lazy. Basically, if I can find a shortcut now and then I'll take it.

Anyway, I put this on some t bone steaks with a little steak seasoning and just slapped them on the gas grill to see what would happen. I was a little worried but was willing to make the sacrifice one time. I was very surprised! The steak turned out with a nice smokey flavor, but not too overwhelming. I wouldn't say that it tastes exactly like smoking it or barbecuing it, but it definitely has its own unique smoke flavor that is very good. And if you're like me, I usually prepare my steaks almost the exact same way every time. So, they taste the exact same way every time. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but changing it up once in a while isn't a bad thing at all. I will definitely order this stuff from here on out.

review_title: Great, healthy, and wonderful for rehydration
review_text:
I'm sure most people have heard the amazing benefits of coconut water.

"What Is Coconut Water?
Naturally refreshing, coconut water has a sweet, nutty taste. It contains easily digested carbohydrate in the form of sugar and electrolytes. Not to be confused with high-fat coconut milk or oil, coconut water is a clear liquid in the fruit’s center that is tapped from young, green coconuts.

It has fewer calories, less sodium, and more potassium than a sports drink. Ounce per ounce, most unflavored coconut water contains 5.45 calories, 1.3 grams sugar, 61 milligrams (mg) of potassium, and 5.45 mg of sodium compared to Gatorade, which has 6.25 calories, 1.75 grams of sugar, 3.75 mg of potassium, and 13.75 mg of sodium." (http://www.m.webmd.com/food-recipes/features/truth-about-coconut-water)

I love to use coconut water. You can drink it by itself. I will when sick, or right after having a baby to help rehydrate my body. However, using it in smoothies, add juice to it, and cooking with it is wonderful.

I was able to try out a 12 pack of CoCoZia 100% Organic Coconut Water. The container comes with a twist spout that you can drink or pour straight from, and then put the lid back on if you don't use it all right away. I love that it is organic, and I also love that the packaging is recyclable paper cartons. The plastic spout also pops off to make recycling much easier.

After I received these containers, I found a new way to use coconut water when my kids were sick just a couple weeks ago.

I wanted to go buy Gatorade to get some electrolytes in their system. I really hate the artificial dyes in it, along with some of the ingredients. I then wondered how to make a homemade version myself.

That's when I tried this recipe.

product_name: Kraft Macaroni & Cheese Dinner
review_title: What's more american than heavily processed cheese and refined noodles packaged by a major corporation?
review_text:
If you're an American over the age of 8 (or a Canadian over the age of 5) and eating solid food then you probably know what this stuff tastes like. That said, if you're not an American (or a Canadian), and/or a recent immigrant (welcome) then let me start off by saying that this stuff is more or less a defining part of American cuisine... i'm actually surprised that it's not on the naturalization test... and when I say that, i don't mean macaroni and cheese in general, i mean "Kraft Macaroni and Cheese". This is like Marmite or Vegemite if you're from England (yuck), like Swedish meatballs or that weird fish stuff that comes in a tube, it's like french baguette or Japanese ramen. This stuff is a national treasure (though, for some reason, if you're Canadian you eat more of this stuff than even Americans)

So what does it taste like? Well, it's a little mis-leading... if you come from a culture that has cheese, then let me preface the rest of this paragraph by saying that you should not expect this stuff to taste like cheese, and when you empty that bag of neon orange powder out onto your noodles this will become clear, and you will be a little taken aback... but fear not! A wave of deliciousness is in bound. It's hard to describe exactly what it tastes like... I'd say; salty, milky, cornstarch with limp noodles (but that doesn't exactly market it well)

There's something comforting about it and you won't be able to put your finger on it (probably the high fat content, or the salt, or the carbs... or the fact that there's probable nothing in this that's any good for you). And what's more! Once you have consumed an entire box of this stuff on your own you will be a true American! (or a Canadian). And the fun doesn't stop there. You can add stuff to it! For beginners i suggest, ground beef or hot dogs...if you're feeling like going for the advanced levels try a can of tuna fish for that extra hit of sodium... and hot sauce... lots of hot sauce.

• Dark & Handsome (9 included): This is my favorite. It’s a strong flavor with a really smooth taste. I feel like the product description fits it perfectly, “velvety, bold coffee”. Yummy!

• Smooth caffeinator (9 included): This is an all around nice blend. Not too bold, not too weak. It’s a smooth, nutty, medium blend that works for me in the morning or afternoon. I usually enjoy it as my second cup of coffee.
• Choconut (4 included): I really didn’t think we’d like this, but it’s not bad. It’s not the first cup of coffee I reach for, but it has a surprisingly nice flavor. I taste more coconut than chocolate, but the chocolate undertones are there. With a pinch of sugar and a little cream it’s a nice desert coffee.

product_name: Natural Stevia Powder - Highly Concentrated Stevia Extract Sugar Substitute- No fillers, Additives or Artificial Ingredients of Any Kind
review_title: By far the best stevia powder I have ever used - period
review_text:
Let me start my review by saying that I have been using stevia for about twenty years now and have used lots of different brands, so I may not be the best person to say whether or not someone who never used stevia before would like this.

That being said, this is certainly the best stevia I've ever used. Up until now my favorite has been Trader Joe's for their pure powder, and SweetLeaf for liquid drops. There are lots of brands I've tried (Like Whole Foods 365) that just taste artificial, have that pronounced licorice flavor, or are downright bitter. Being happy with my usual brands, the only reason I ordered this was because I'm a member of Amazon Prime and I didn't want to have to make a trip. What a surprise! This is BY FAR the best. It has a fantastic flavor, and it's the only stevia I've ever been able to use where people who aren't used to stevia can't tell I used it. This is fantastic in everything from lemonade to desserts. One note of caution: this is extremely sweet. I have to use about 2/3 of what I typically used from the Trader Joe's pure extract. That being said, even if I accidentally put a little too much, it never, ever gets that bitterness or artificial flavor. It's just incredibly sweet. Somehow this is just purely sweet without any real flavor of its own. I don't understand how it works. It's amazing!

It was so remarkably different from other stevia powders that I started playing with it in the kitchen. For example, I found that a little bit added to melted dark chocolate makes it intensely sweet but still dark, and when added to hot tea with just a tiny amount of honey, it tastes like I used way more honey than I did. A minuscule amount added to cut strawberries made them taste like fruit from heaven, enhancing their own natural sweetness. I had to cook for 35 people for an event and made a honey-sweetened lavender lemonade, and I was able to sweeten five gallons with just half a cup of honey and a little bit of stevia powder, which saved me a fortune in honey (since I buy local), and everyone loved it.

On another note, whenever I talk to people about stevia I like to take a minute to differentiate between stevioside-based extracts and the more commercial extracts based on rebaudioside (Reb-A, Pure Via, etc.). There is a mountain of research that has been done on the safety - and actual health benefits - of stevioside, which is what Nature's Candy uses. Reb-A, on the other hand, was made as a patent-worthy product by huge corporations trying to exploit the natural foods movement, and is often cut with other flavorings or sweeteners. Some research seems to indicate that it may not be as safe as stevioside-based sweeteners. That's another thing that makes this brand so great. When I first tasted it I double-checked the package to make sure it was the right kind, and it is. This is the pure, natural stevioside extract that has been shown in multiple Japanese studies to help with metabolic disorders, and which has been proven safe time and time again.

I don't think the product itself needs any help, I can think of a couple of improvement:
- I would really love it if it came in a shaker
- It would be a dream if I could find the same quality and taste in a liquid version!
- That dream would be even better if there were flavored liquid versions (I love to make my own sodas with sparkling water and flavored stevia, and the liquid versions don't foam as much)

In any event, these are just suggestions for making a phenomenal product even more versatile. review_title: Slippery on leather and not big enough
review_text:
So I'll start by saying that the Lyzzo Travel Dog Hammock does the job; it more or less covers your back seat. It certainly doesn't do it any better than a blanket with straps, but it does keep hair and dirt off of the seats, mostly.

I bought this a few months ago and have been using it for trips back a forth between home. It claims to have non-stick backing, but my experience has been that it slides around even with my 75lb dog on top of it. The material on the top side of the hammock does well to trap hair, but good luck getting any of it off without washing it. The pockets included seem to be a nice feature, but I haven't used them. The description also states that this fits cars from small passenger vehicles up to SUV sized cars. I drive a Mazda6, and this product is not big enough to comfortably stretch from my backseat to the front seats without cramming my dog into a narrow area.

My biggest gripe with this product is the price for what you get. A furniture pad with gussets to attach straps to your seats would do the same thing as this product, at a fraction of the cost. The one selling point for me was the non-stick backing since I have leather seats. Unfortunately I haven't had any luck with this product NOT sliding around with my dog on top.

If you're looking for a quality back seat dog cover, this will do the job, but for the price this is listed at, I would look elsewhere first.

Update: After my dog had an accident on the seat cover, I needed to wash it. Following the washing instructions on the tag of the cover, it came out of the washer and had shrank a bit and shriveled around the corners. There's no reason a seat cover for your dog should shrink when washed in cold water and air dried. I'll be replacing this expensive waste of money with something that will actually do the job right.

I would rather vacuum every day than go back to this lightweight litter, I still have half a box and it is getting tossed. HIGH QUALITY BULLY STICKS DO NOT HAVE A NOTICABLE SMELL, AT ALL, PERIOD, END OF SENTENCE. And the fact that these bully sticks have a noticeable smell even before they have been chewed on by your dog should be the biggest red flag in the world...because once your dog starts chewing on this thing, the smell is intensified. I like to compare it to talking with someone who has mildly bad breathe. Their breath will not kill you, nor will it make you throw up, but damn - why should you have to stand there and be assaulted by that?

But the worst part is that there seems to be little to no quality control because the sticks look like they have been deep fried in chicken grease.

I'm sure that this company is well intentioned, and I'm sure that the other 5 star reviewers feel justified in praising these sticks - most likely because they haven't actually tried a really high quality bully stick. review_title: Please be careful if you do buy this
review_text:
It's amazing how such a simple device can make my cats go crazy. The thing about this one is that you have to be REALLY CAREFUL when playing with it. Never, ever leave it out when you're done, and that should go for any kind of cat toys with long stringy parts. When playing with this, don't let your cats chomp down on the wire. I try to hold it at a length where the cats can bat around the cardboard part at the end, but not get their paws or mouth on the wire. It takes practice and a very watchful eye, but that's the only safe way to use this toy. There's a small, sharp hook at the end, where the wire was bent to hold the cardboard on. I can see how that could easily rip through a cat's cheek or paw pad like a fishing hook. Also, if they're jumping for it, sometimes the wire gets caught between their little fingers. I can't imagine that feels good.

So, two stars because all three of my cats go nuts for it. It even gets my old, lazy one off the couch. But it does make me worry that less-informed cat parents might not realize how dangerous it is. At the end of the day, I couldn't recommend this to anyone.

review_text: This gate is tall enough that my cats won't try jumping over it -- or on it. The mesh is sized in a way that makes it (at least for my cats -- so far) unclimb-able. The action is not good -- it doesn't slide open and closed very well. In fact, I have to use my foot to move the bottom and my hand to move the top, otherwise, it won't open/close. The space you put the gate in needs to be just a touch narrower than that of any of the lock widths in order to provide enough tension to keep the gate in place (the locking increments are spaced at around 3/4"). In my case, it doesn't work.  We put felt pads on the rubber stoppers to increase the width of the gate enough to keep it in place. I wouldn't count on the gate to keep a large dog (or heavy child) in/out -- a good, forceful push will displace the gate. The action issue mentioned earlier makes it a pain to put the gate up and take it down. If your space is just right, you have small/light animals, and you don't need to move the gate often, it's decent. It is very inexpensive -- you get what you pay for.

My family joked that it calms separation anxiety by giving her something else to do.  I even had our trainer check that I had the right size and was putting it on properly, and she said some dogs find it calming and some don't.  She was "impressed" b y how quickly our little escape artist could get out of it.  Ultimately, I decided, because several professionals swear by this, to donate it to a local animal shelter, in case it can provide comfort to another dog. But it is a pricey item, and I have to give an honest review based on my experience with the product...which is that it was that it was not well-made enough to "swaddle" our puppy in any meaningful way.

product_name: Sunsun 4-Stage External Canister Filter with 9-watt UV Sterilizer for Aquarium, 370 GPH
review_text: I was pretty displeased with this product.  I have a 75 gallon African Cichlid tank.  I'd never used a canister filter before but after 2 months of use, I decided to unhook this one and use a bit bio-wheel instead.  First off, setting this thing up isn't the easiest if you've never done this before.  The directions  are obviously written by a Chinese person who struggles with the English language (product made in China).  Once hooked up, I used 4 types of media:  the included filter pads, charcoal, bio-balls, and ceramic rings.  My biggest complaint was the filter pads spewed small white particles throughout the water, especially after priming the pump.  That couldn't have been good for my fish.  I did not want them constantly breathing that in.  This happened despite rinsing the pads.  The filter also spewed poop, which was really pleasant.  Yes, it did keep my water chemical levels at a healthy range but my tank always LOOKED dirty.  I am very happy with my bio-wheel.  I don't know if all canisters are like this one but I will never use one again after this experience.  Yeah, it is inexpensive  but for me anyhow, having to replace it 2 months after my initial purchase made it way more expensive.  Very disappointed.

product_name: GAMMA2 Vittles Vault Airtight Pet Food Container
review_title: Unless space is an issue, go with something else.
review_text: I purchased one of these from a different retailer and will likely be buying another one despite my poor review. Why? Because living in limited space, the space saving design outweighs the litany of problems. That said, if I had the space, I'd much rather have one of Gamma's larger twist-top Vittles Vaults.  The space saving design is really this product's only saving grace. If you're looking for something that absolutely has to be air tight, look elsewhere. The rectangular rubber seal attached to the snap lid of these Vittles Vault Select models are wholly inadequate for making an air tight seal. Air (and bugs, and pets) can easily find their way in. To keep the pet food fresh and adequately protected, I portion the food out into one gallon zipping storage bags before placing them in the bin. It seems redundant but, again, it helps with managing storage space.  Additionally, the front label says the Select 15 can hold 15 pounds of Dog Food or 26 pounds of Cat Food and I'm here to tell you that's not the case. I purchase 16 pound bags of Purina Cat Chow Complete for my cats and when poured directly into the container this container can't hold the full bag amount. It leaves about 2 pounds of kibble in the bag.  This capacity is reduced further by using the storage bags to preserve food freshness.  Finally, the molded plastic hinges on both the back of the lid and the lid's snap closure are flimsy. "Flimsy" is putting it mildly. Within a month or two of use, the snap hinge was so weak that a light tap could open it. It is very easy to accidentally pop the entire snap lid off the back hinge as well.  In summary: Pros: - It's a space saving design that's stackable if you live within limited space.  Cons - Not air tight, easily allows air, pets, and bugs in. - Will require secondary protection for food freshness. - Doesn't hold as much as advertised. - Poorly constructed hinges.

review_title: Worst Organic Lip Balm Ever...Oh wait, it's paw protectant.
review_text:
First off, I got burned on this purchase, but it was by my own doing. I should have read closer and looked at the product specs with more scrutiny.

Second, this product would probably work if you have one of those super tiny dogs that doesn't normally walk around outside in the back yard or go for walks. The product is smaller than some of the lip balms I've ordered, and comes in the same size tube. For $7.95 I was expecting more than organic lip balm. <---Oddly enough, it contains many of the same ingredients as organic lip balm products I've purchased in the past. So I might as well have put $4.95 organic lip balm on my dogs feet and saved $3.

There isn't sufficient product to last the entire outdoor season and cover the feet of a small (14lbs, so not tiny, but not big) chihuahua mix....Much less the feet of a 70lb Lab mix. I put this stuff on his feet and immediately used 1/3 of it. The product does not absorb nor glide on smoothly. If the intention were to not heal/soothe/absorb, but to provide a wax barrier, I would expect a smooth application that leaves a thick waxy layer on the dogs foot. Instead I had bumps and plops of product in some places, and none on other parts of the paw pad.

I appreciate the natural ingredients, but here's the thing: It turns out MOST PAW PROTECTOR products already use natural ingredients as dogs are prone to licking off the product or using their paws to scratch their face/eyes. So I find it a bit deceptive toward pet owners who want to look into protecting their pets feet, but don't know enough....

product_name: Aspen Pet Lebistro Programmable Food Dispenser
review_title: A few niceties, but overall poor execution
review_text: While this automatic pet feeder certainly accomplishes its main goal of automatically feeding your pet a measured amount of food up to 3 times per day, I believe it has some major design flaws that make it not worth purchasing. I'll start with the good features and then list the bad.  Good: 1. You can program the machine to dispense food for up to 3 times per day (nicely labeled as Breakfast, Lunch, or Dinner). 2. You can program each of these times to dispense food in intervals of 1/4 cup. Meaning, each of the 3 times that food may be dispensed can have different amounts of food dispensed and in intervals of 1/4 cup (e.g. 1/4 cup for breakfast, 1/4 for lunch and 1/2 for dinner). 3. The container can hold a relatively large amount of food. I don't know the exact volume but I have to refill it roughly once every 3 weeks and I feed my cat 1/2 cup of food per day. 4. It's relatively easy to take it apart, clean each separate piece, and then reconstruct it.  So far so good. Here are the bad points: 1. Perhaps the biggest design flaw is that my cat can hack the machine to give her extra food. She figured out that she can reach her paw up the chute where the food falls and push the hatch to allow extra food to fall. The way the machine is designed is that it has a wheel with four extruding flaps, and 1/4 cup of food can fit between each flap for a total of 1 cup in the wheel. My cat can push the flap to drop down an extra 1/4 cup of food. This means that when it's time to feed her, the wheel rotates and no food drops down so I don't know if the machine actually turned the wheel or if my cat pushed the flap to get her meal early. 2. The bowl from which your pet eats, and into which the food falls from the chute, is poorly designed. It does not click into place when you connect it to the machine, and it often falls off at the slightest touch. Because it is loose, food often falls around the bowl and makes a mess. The plus side is that it is easy to clean, but that should have been a given anyways. 3. The controls are very non-intuitive and require me to reference the manual every time I use them. There are three buttons, Enter, Down, and Up, and their usages are confusing and difficult, if not impossible, to remember. 4. Continuing with the poor control design, if you want to manually dispense food, you have to hold the up button for 3 seconds and 1/4 cup of food will come out. If you keep holding the button then it will keep dispensing food indefinitely until you hold it again. This happens to me roughly 1/2 the time, which is quite a lot because I manually feed my cat sometimes due to not being able to tell if she's gotten food per the #1 bad point above. 5. It does not have AC power. It seems to last a very long time on batteries, but not being able to plug it in and not worry about it is pretty annoying. Edit: 6. As another downside to the bowl being detachable -- my cat has figured out how to pull it out of the feeder...so that when she does this (and I don't notice), her food gets dispensed all over the floor. This is extremely annoying, and a further indication of the lack of thought put into the fundamental design of this product.  I hope this review helps you in your purchase.

review_title: Costs more than it is worth
review_text:
I have been having an issue with my cats playing in their drinking bowls instead of drinking from it. I was so excited to finally get something that would fix this issue. After reading positive and negative reviews, I decided it would be worth the $40 to not have water all over my floor everyday. It was not worth it.

The first issue is absolutely my own fault for not thinking the size thing through. I bought the 10 oz bottle version. I did not realize how absolutely miniscule 10 oz actually is. Think of it this way: A regular can of soda is 8 oz. This bottle is only slightly larger than a soda can. That may work for one cat if you refill it every day, but I have two cats, so even if I refill it every day, it isn't really enough water. So the size really is a downside. I bought the smaller size to save money, but if you are thinking of buying this product, definitely go with the 20 oz bottle.

The second issue that I find with this product is that it leaks a bit out of the nozzle. I bought this to avoid messes, and while the mess isn't nearly as bad as an entire bowl of water, it is annoying to have to clean up when I thought that this product would alleviate that need.

Another down side is that this is absolutely not worth the price they are asking. A person could easily make this product for a fraction of the price. All you need is a wood square, PVC piping, a hamster water bottle and some duct tape. Easy. This thing isn't made with any special kinds of materials, and the only real plus to buying it versus making it is the clip that you use to affix the bottle to the piping, something that could easily be replicated with tape.

So far, my cats have not really been using the bottle. I keep seeing reviews saying, "My cat immediately started using this, no problem!" I would love to meet these cats, because my two little guys are just confused by this thing. I read that putting tuna juice in with the water could help, or putting something tasty on the tip would lead them to try it out and things would fall into place from their. I tried putting wet cat food on the nozzle, but, after licking that off, there was little interest in this apparatus. I am going to give it another day or so and see if this changes and they figure it all out, but in the mean time, they need water! I am not going to leave them thirsty!

In other words, this thing may turn out to be a huge waste of money. I will give it a few days, but I have a feeling I just spent $40 +s&h on something that we will not use. It is too small for what I need, and I have been thinking of buying a larger water bottle and just taping it to the stick. It would be cheaper to do that than to buy the 20 oz bottle.

All in all, if you have one clever cat or small dog, this product might work for you, but I don't think it is going to work out for me. Also, the price is way to high for what you are buying. review_text:
The life jacket overall design is great. We bought the size small for our 23 pound corgi, and it did a good job of keeping her afloat all day. The additional flap under the neck was an added bonus as well, since it made sure to hold her head up higher in the water. It also was a very nice-looking life jacket, not too bulky looking and a great blue color.

The reason for the low rating is the stitching around the handle. Although she was within the weight-limit for the small life jacket, as soon as we used the handle once to pull her out of the water and into the boat, the stitching immediately ripped. This seems like a very poor design, where the straps seem to only go partway up the jacket so there is a lot of stress put onto the material on top. In addition, it doesn't appear that I can even sew it back myself, since the material ripped apart when the stitching tore.

On the flip side, we bought the Outward Hound life jacket for our 65 pound dog and it held up all day with no ripping, despite us pulling her out of the water into the boat many times. Comparing the two directly, I would most likely recommend Outward Hound moving forward, especially since they're in the same price range as this brand.

product_name: CatGenie Self Washing Self Flushing Cat Box
review_text:
The cat genie runs like a Landover, meaning it is great when it’s working and a nightmare when it’s not.
While it does (usually) work properly it makes one heck of a noise doing so and the advertised “less than 30 min” cleaning time is a joke. When it does clog, or have anything (like a single piece of string) get caught in the impeller, it simply backs up with cat sewage. You really start to review your life choices when you’re cleaning cat sewage at 5am when you’re supposed to be heading to the airport for vacation. Fortunately this happens frequently enough that you become adept at learning where the problem likely is.
I also second the other reviewers that if even a small amount of cat poo is left behind the smell is terrible.
The actual quality of the machine is spotty at best. Cheap plastic and components hinder an innovative idea. It’s like they slapped a patent on it 10+ years ago and haven’t bothered to make any improvements since. Simple things like a dampened strainer that doesn’t bang around and a better mesh on the strainer would greatly improve performance.
Another problem is the box itself is really just too small for anything bigger than a small cat. I purchased the door for the cat genie and my cat was so upset he stopped using it as he already barely fits, and don’t get me started on returns.
I only have one cat but I strongly suspect having more than that would be pushing it at best.
Bottom line: Below average quality, high maintenance cost, and spending at least one day out of every 90 cleaning cat sewage.

review_text:
Using their measurement guide, I ordered the medium for my 2000 Explorer. I believe I would've been better off with the large. The medium fits but is so tight that it will not pull down all the way on one end and it looks nothing like the photo in as far as how smoothly it looks that it should fit. It is very obvious that it is slightly too small. It's like trying to fit a sheet on a bed that is one size too small. Plus, if you want to add seat belt availability the instructions say to CUT SLITS for them! So, I buy a new product and then have to cut holes in it? Fortunately for me, I will not be cutting slits. I bought this for intermittent use with my daughter's 100LB German Shepherd. I ordered it knowing that I was going to have to have it while I dog sat for a month and then periodically after that. I have not used it yet as the dog just got here on the day of this review. Also, there is a Velcroed slot in the middle of the cover that runs along the crease between the back of the seat and the seat itself; I assume that this is for a middle arm rest. I don't see it pictured in the advertisement. I did not have time to return the item and get a different size or a different one altogether. I probably would not buy this again. and would look at a different one.

Pros:
It seems pretty sturdy
It is not difficult to install (if the fit was better it would be even easier)
It appears that it will stay on the seat pretty well
It covers pretty well on the backside of the seat back and down along the bottom of the seat cushions
It seems like it will be easy to clean

Cons:
Size chart is not accurate, at least not for the Explorer (and I measured my seat before buying)
To use your seatbelts, you have to cut slits in your brand new item. I believe this would compromise the integrity of the material and weaken it
Due to the sizing issue mostly, this Velcroed area along the seat back and cushion pulls really tight andI am guessing that it will pull apart after a short bit of use, especially with a large dog

review_title: while after these fixes it's an awesome cat toy
review_text:
This review explains solutions to problems that are common with this. I still left it at 3 stars, because, while after these fixes it's an awesome cat toy, I still had to DO these in the first place to make it usable, which I find ridiculous.

This toy has a MAJOR FLAW - the motor will shut off if your cat holds the wand for 5-10 seconds.

For me, this meant that I basically had to sit there with the toy as he played with it, turning it back on every 15ish seconds. I was hoping to use this to distract him while I was doing homework, so this flaw rendered it essentially useless. My cat would trigger the turn-off, and then start howling because the toy wasn't playing with him anymore.
But I found a trick to this. If you put the base on a turntable (lazy susan), the base spins while your cat holds the wand. Eventually, my cat lets go for a second to attack it again, and it spins around again. A turntable made this toy do exactly what it's supposed to do, and now my cat plays with it for as long as I'll let him.

review_title: I do think it is a good quality food and my cat ate it and enjoyed ...
review_text: Although I give this 3 stars, I do think it is a good quality food and my cat ate it and enjoyed it for several years. Unfortunately he just suffered from a urinary blockage and a partial blockage a month ago and his diet will need to change. I thought I was doing great feeding him a grain free, quality, food, but after researching, I am wondering if there are just too many things in some of these types of foods that cats just don't need or are actually counterproductive to their health. For instance, there are almost a dozen fruits and vegetables listed in this food + potato flour. Cats get a minute amount of veggies in the wild and need mostly an all meat diet. Sounds great and healthy to us but do our cats actually need spinach and carrots? The answer is no. I also read that some of the senior foods (as well as all drys) have even more of an impact on a cat maintaining proper hydration, which can lead to blockage issues in males. An all wet or raw diet if really the best. If my female cat likes this dry, I will probably feed the rest to her with wet as well. But our male will be on a prescription diet as he transitions to all wet  Also, as someone else mentioned, for some reason only half of this food would get eaten by my cat. Lots of it ended up on the floor outside of the bowl, so there can be some waste. I appreciate company's that try to make more quality pet foods, I'm just not sure some of the ingredients are of benefit, and may even be detrimental.

review_text: In my opinion these leashes look pretty cool! They come in fun colors and they look like the real deal. One thing I do really like about the leash is the "extra handle" near the clip that allow you to grab your dog on a shorter lead if need be. The padded strap of the actual handle is very nice too. The bungee in the middle is a really interesting concept, as it is supposed to help absorb some of the force your dog generates. Personally, I think this feature gives you less control should your dog decided to pull. The bungee allows the dog to stretch to their maximum length (if you don't grab the "extra handle") and gives you less control, similar to retractable leashes. Also, pay attention to the size recommendations for the leash--as they are designed to absorb different weights from different sized dogs. If you are serious about leash manners and training your dog the proper way I would recommend a traditional nylon leash is lieu of this. However, if you love how it looks or already have an expertly trained dog this leash is not bad. You can use the "extra handle" if your dog gets distracted or tugs too much, so you are not at a complete loss if something happens.

review_title: Let me get straight to the point, does this ...
review_text: Let me get straight to the point, does this product work? Yes, but only to a small degree.  If I was to put a number on its effectiveness, I’d say it provided roughly 20% bark reduction on the dogs I was targeting.  No real science on how I got the 20% reduction, it’s just my own personal observations.  The dogs in question are two small terrier mix dogs in the neighbor’s yard roughly 15 to 20 feet away.  I have the item mounted over the fence line and angled slightly downward right into the neighbor’s yard with no objects or barriers in the way.  Before I had the product, the dogs barking would be continuous and long lasting, often times lasting several minutes long.  After installing the product and making necessary adjustments when necessary, I have found the dogs barks to be more singular, such as a bark, pause, bark-bark, pause, bark, etc.  And the duration of these barks have shortened somewhat to about a minute.  However, this “bark, pause, bark” is not always consistent.  There are times when the dogs would just bark incessantly, regardless of the dog silencer being on.  So yes, in my opinion the product does work, but only to a small degree in my experience.  Supposedly, it takes time for dogs to be trained with these types of silencers. I plugged them in 3 days before we left for our trip as they recommend for full effectiveness they need to work for 7 days. I plugged one upstairs in bedroom in the middle of the house with the door open to the hall and one downstairs behind a chair they love to scratch to my displeasure.

The only thing I did notice when I got back is that one of my cats suddenly liked hanging out in the hallway by that bedroom whenever she was relaxing or suddenly became stressed (loud noise, etc.). But as far as the one downstairs, I don't think that stopped them from wanting to scratch the chair even thought there is literally a giant cat tree with several scratching posts next to it. I did notice that while we were away they liked sleeping on the couch because I had to vacuum a thick layer of cat hair that was in the shape of a sleeping cat.

Relatives and neighbors stopped by to check on the cats and both said they seemed calm. My neighbor brought over her 8 month old baby and both cats were friendly; they were scared of her as a newborn.

I will have to test this product again to see how effective it is. My cats without a diffuser are generally sweet, laid-back, and happy go lucky.

Here's the thing, if you sell refurbished or USED products, give us a warning so we can make an informed choice. Also previously USED products generally are sold at a discounted price. The first crate I got from them was too small to be in for more than sleep so that is why I bought this one but I'm not returning it because IT has been USED, I get it. I might sell mine on Craigslist stating its USED and I will charge less than I paid for it because it's USED.

review_title: Fun while it lasted, but didn't last long

My minpin loved this thing! She was crazy about it before she figured out an exploit that basically makes it useless.

She is about 5 pounds but she's smart...she figured out that if she takes it on the couch or to a high place, she can drop it and the sides will come apart and spill all the food. She also figured out how to pick it up and carry it around - by putting her tiny lower jaw inside the hole of the container.

One of the reasons I chose this treat ball over other balls is that it has the adjustable plastic inside so that you can choose how much food comes out. My dog is small and her kibbles are very small. And I was still able to make it a challenge for her to shake the food out of it. There are 2 separate plastic pieces that let you adjust the size of the dispensing hole. Unfortunately, after my dog busted open the toy, she hid one of them and I have yet to find it.

If you have hard flooring like tile or wood, this ball is super noisy. I had to take it away from her if I was on the phone, watching TV, or trying to do something that involved listening. All you can hear is "bang! bang! bang!" as it smashes into furniture and rattles across the floor.

The big plus is that while it lasted, it was an awesome outlet for my dog's puppy energy. Whenever I saw her trying to teethe on a no-no object, I put a few kibbles in this ball and her energy was spent in no time.

I'm currently looking to replace the one she destroyed but will probably look for a design that minimizes the flaws described above so it lasts longer.

review_text:
I’ve flown with my 17lb dachshund before with a handheld travel bag and I bought the OxGord so I could wheel her and also carry my own bag, thus avoiding the need to check anything. We’ve now flown twice with this plan and both trips went smoothly.

The OxGord rolling pet carriers have the same exterior dimensions as the medium Snoozer rolling bags, which have many reviews of successful carry-on plane travel. The OxGord is also a fraction of the price.

To stow this bag under-the-seat-infront-of-you, you have to remove the bottom structure of the bag. This can easily be done in the isle by detaching the velcro and removing the exterior floor. From the reviews I read, this is the same procedure for the Snoozer bag.

Pros:
- More mesh than our previous bag which kept Eva (our doxie) from getting hot and panting
- It works
- Very incognito, when Eva was in bag most people didn't notice I had a dog, including the person sitting next to me

Cons:
- Not sturdy, strong or stable - I definitely handled this bag with care, it feels very breakable, not made for any heavy use - especially with the added weight of Eva I avoided uneven ground and curbs, I also only lifted it by the nylon handles and not the metal retractable
- No interior padding - I added a thin pillow that we usually use in her kennel, without that addition she would have been extremely uncomfortable flying for 3hrs
- Retractable handle sticks - which worried me but luckily it didn't stick at any crucial moment like security or boarding

FYI:
Standard airline under seat dimensions
22" deep x 14" wide x 9" heigh

OxGord Rolling Travel Carrier
14" (Length) x 11" (Width) x 19" (Height)

* The feathery toys were very appealing to my cat. Mine did not seem to have a preference between the pink or blue toy.

* The string broke in multiple places.

review_title: You might want a rubber mallet to help put this together
review_text:
I bought two of these through woot (fulfilled by Amazon) for a really good price. If it's not at a deep discount, this cage is very overpriced.

Almost every piece that has to fit together for the boltless construction on both cages was bent... either too much or too little. I had to use pliers and a rubber mallet to get the pieces together. The locks require assembly too, and most were fine, but some of the places they had to fit into were bent like crazy too. The food bowl holders were the worst.

Both of my cages also are missing a "spring" for the latch to keep the tray and grill from moving during transit. The instructions mention it but they weren't included.

Even if I assume that most of bent parts are from shipping, the top panel on one actually had a wire welded on crooked. So I'm inclined to believe that they have poor quality control in general.

Once constructed, they are pretty solid. 25 lbs solid. This will be a good cage for temporary housing such as for boarding or on vacation, as well as for going outside, but as a carrier to go to the vet, etc, I'd choose a different cage unless you want a workout. I have large flight cages that weigh less than this beast.

Overall, I was disappointed with these. I have an AA cage from before Midwest bought them and the quality between the two products is staggering.

product_name: Oceans Wonders Coral Frag Plugs 100pc
review_title: Decent quality frag plugs.  Just make sure to rinse!
review_text:
I was in need of some frag plugs and ultimately opted for a package of the "Coral Frag Plugs 100pc" sold by Oceans Wonders. The price was right and coupled with Amazon Prime any shipping and returns issues would not be an issue.

The plugs seem to be of decent quality for their purpose. They are bright white in appearance so keep that in mind if you're looking for plugs that will blend in with your rock-work. They are quite "dusty" due to being "Made from 100% Pure Caribsea reef sand" so definitely give them a good rinse. I knocked one star off the rating simply due to the amount of "dust" and rinsing required. Not really a major concern though. After rinsing in RO then tank water I plopped about a dozen into the sump and let them remain for about a week prior to usage for curing purposes. No negative effects in tank parameters were seen.

They're the perfect size for zoas, palys, small SPS frags and have found them useful for small monti frags, too. The surface is rough enough to make gluing a non-issue. After about two weeks the frags seem to already be exhibiting growth onto the plugs most likely due to their composition and one even has what seems to be the beginnings of a bit of coraline.

Nice, basic frag plugs, these are. No issues whatsoever and when the time comes to purchase more I'll be heading back in this direction.

review_text:
I switched over to WBCL last month and honestly, it's such a nice product. It makes me feel better that its all natural and the most important part is both of my cats love it. No accidents outside of the litter boxes.

I originally started with the red bag (multiple cats, clumping) and it was okay. The litter smelled like corn but after awhile it started to put me off when I scooped the boxes. I tried the LAVENDER scented bag and oh my goodness. Such a difference. I'm not usually a fan of lavender but now I get a whiff and for once Im not disgusted by my cat room.

Scooping the litter is easy and I live on my own land with a private septic so I flush everything. So much easier and with summer coming up, Im so excited that the random fruit flies won't be around. I started with a 15lb bag for two litter boxes and now I just buy the 7lb bags to top them off. It lasts a good amount of time and I feel like I'm not wasting a bunch of litter each week or two weeks. Obviously there is a little dust but not as much as the crystal litter. My favorite part is the fact that I have a very easy routine. I scoop and flush twice a day and that's it. I'm happy and my cats are happy. No more cat litter smells!

I rated it 4 stars bc after a while the lavender scent starts to fade. Adding more litter seems to help a bit but now I'm thinking of picking up some lavender essential oil and adding a few drops from time to time.

Highly recommend this product! You'll actually get excited to scoop litter because of how easy it is!

review_title: I've had it about a month and it works!
review_text: Originally, I wrote this review giving the item 5 Stars. I recently downgraded after owning it for a month and discovering the price jumped from $29.99 to $49.99.  For the past year(+) I have lived with three very annoying chihuahua's whose owners let them run a muck. They run out the back door barking and continue to do so the entire time they are outside. I cannot be in my back yard without those things barking at me. A co-working mentioned this item to me. I ordered it with rush delivery and attached it to a tree branch level with my neighbors deck. As I was hanging it up, one of them run up to the balcony barking. I immediately turned it on thinking when better to test and see the results. It stopped barking right away, turned around and ran into the house. Just as I finished zip tying it to the tree the other ran out, got out half a bark and turned around so fast it lost its footing as it was running back into the house. It is so effective that my neighbor on the other side asked me if something happened to the neighbors dogs. They hate my neighbors chihuahua's just as much as I do. This thing is absolutely great! The best I can tell, the ultrasonic frequency is directional. I frequently take care of a friends dogs when he travels. His German Sheppard is a very well trained, disciplined dog and will only let out an occasional bark when we play in the backyard. He is not affected by the birdhouse at all! I told him to speak while within ten feet of the birdhouse just to test it and he displayed no reaction at all. The birdhouse faces the neighbors deck only. If Trigger's barking sets it off, it only sends the sounds wave at my neighbors house.   However! When I originally purchased this item it was $29.99. When I logged on to copy the link to send to a couple neighbors and friends I noticed the price jumped $20.00. I would not have purchased this birdhouse for $50 and waived off my recommendation to my neighbors. Here is why. The birdhouse requires 6x AA batteries. Like any electronic, the duration the batteries last will depend on frequency of use. Mine lasted less than a month. If you account for the long term cost of 6x AA batteries once a month on top of the current $50 price plus shipping, I would not recommend this product unless you are having a really serious issue or they have developed a version that can run off batteries or be operated by an AC adapter.

review_text: I just wanted to mention: Many individuals (including my vet) are recommending this product for use in hamsters who have lice or mites. The back of this bottle warns against getting this product in your eyes, it warns against getting it on your skin, and it even warns you about inhaling it. The fact that it is dangerous to breathe this and get it on your skin worries me; how can I put this on my animal when it is toxic? Specially on these small and delicate animals. Now, I understand that this is meant for birds and that there is a higher risk of toxicity with hamsters. I'd just like to speak to any hamster owner that is wandering over here with intentions of buying this for their pet. There is a higher risk of this product harming hamsters because hamsters will lick this product off themselves. Please be very careful; don't douse your hamster or their cage with this product because it will most certainly poison them. Even just a few squirts can be very bad. If your hamster becomes poisoned by this it may have fur loss, seem distressed, become lethargic, refuse to eat, develop lumps, etc. Please refer to some hamster forums for more advice on this.

review_title: I have no idea what's in it but...
review_text:
It worked wonderfully for my 4 gallon tank. I'd been testing and testing the water, doing daily water changes, and the cloudiness wouldn't quit. Online forums said to stay away from products like this but it was bothering me quite a bit. Some things to keep in mind: It takes time to work. I added a dose to my tank in the afternoon. The water wasn't clear until the next morning (but it was CRYSTAL clear). The product does warn you it may take multiple doses but do NOT overdose as it can apparently kill your fish. You also may wind up needing to clean your filter more often than you had been prior to using this product. My filter was only two weeks old and is used exclusively for a betta but I happened to adjust it slightly while wiping down the sides of the tank for algae and the backwash...it was disgusting. When I opened my filter...it was disgusting. It says it will make your filter more efficient, and I guess that translates into 'you will need to change your filter more often'.

Apart from the filter issue, my main problem is the lack of an ingredient list anywhere on the bottle. I'm currently having to use another product in my tank for a separate issue, but that product can't be used with certain other chemicals. Accu-Clear does contain chemicals, but what they are I have no idea. The only thing I've found online is the MSDS for Accu-Clear, which is great for telling me what it might do to ME, but I'd love to know what products I potentially can/can't use it with for my FISH'S sake.

review_text:
We got this collar as a replacement collar for our Pit Bull, Trouble. It does work well for him because he is even scared of the beep it makes. There are a few pros and cons about the collar which the seller was very good at explaining my concerns about the collar.

PROS:
It beeps on the first two barks instead of instantly shocking the dog.
It turns off after 7 level of static shock so that your dog is not constantly being shocked.
It is automatic, which means I don't need a remote to warn my dog.

The Nylon collar is plenty long enough to go around his big neck. If you have a tiny dog you will have to cut off the excess, but is is plenty long even for my Pit/Dane mix who has a 22 inch neck.

Cons:
The level of sensitivity on the collar is a dial which Trouble was able to turn it up to full power just by scratching his neck. It is very easy to just barely touch it and it turns on high.

When it is on the highest sensitivity, it picks up everything. He would just shake his head and it would go off. OR my little Italian Greyhound would bark and it would go off. I am constantly checking it to turn it back to the lowest setting.

Overall it has worked well for him. I don't think I would buy another one unless they changed the dial to a push button strength setting. HOWEVER I must say that this is a new collar being made from the company and they are working on improvements. I will definitely buy from this seller again, maybe other products, because of their exceptional customer service.

I've attached some pictures just so you can get an idea of the collar's size in comparison to my Pit Bull and so you can see what I mean my the sensitivity dial.

review_text:
Our pup is under 10-12 lbs. We were given Yunnan Baiyou by her vet, thereafter they suggested we get it on-line. This capsule is a little larger and the gel doesn't melt as quickly. That makes the "giving" of it more difficult, even with a pill-plunger. She gets it stuck in her throat and then coughs out the powder herb as the capsule softens -- she never gets enough swallowed, so it is a multi-pill struggle. The vet's capsules had Chinese writing on them, which I assume is just the plain gelcap vessel making the difference, but that capsule was smaller and swallowed. So, I wish it was easier to administer the herb... disguising it, sprinkling on food, wrapping it doesn't work.

The herb itself is miraculous for a dog diagnosed with probable cancer. It helps the energy & appetite as well as in the clotting of blood. It has been somewhat miraculous in renewing her spirit. No pain is evident to the docs, therefore we took this route of living with possible cancer. She is very happy overall and it is a joy to have her better in this way..

The other option was invasive exploratory surgery; if cancer was found, she might have 3 to 6 months and that would be consumed with helping her recover from the surgery. Whatever happens, this herb is the wiser option for her.

I've never even heard of these dog chews. I read the directions here on Amazon said to microwave them for 45 seconds. I was very hesitant to do this because it seemed weird. When he was done he looked at me and thumped his tail heavily in happiness.

Overall, I think these Himalayan Dog Chews are a fantastic special treat for your dog that I'm sure they'll love. They're natural and have no additives, which is an extra bonus.

product_name: Pet Supply Imports Herm Sprenger Chrome Plated Training Collar with Quick Release Snap
review_title: I don't know why I waited so long...
review_text:
It's been said way more times already, but I just wanted to reinforce the idea that this is ideal for dogs that are pullers. My puppy is 8 months old, and I was patiently trying to train the pulling out of her using all the methods I found online. But one day I just broke and decided to shell out twenty odd dollars for this collar and it was a Godsend! Why the heck did I wait so long?! She was literally a completely different dog from our very first walk. She was a little hesitant about letting me put it on, but after it was fastened (make sure you guys watch some youtube videos on how to size it) and the leash was attached, she walked like champion. She didn't lunge at other pedestrians or children, and barking dogs only distracted her for mere seconds (before she would just stand fast on the other side of the fence and I had to forcefully pull her away).

I decided to get the fast release version because I read that the original was a bit tougher to put on and take off. I actually accidentally ordered the original collar the first time around and my wife had a lot of trouble trying to unfasten the collar. I got it right the second time, though! I saw some reviews and youtube videos about why you shouldn't get the quick release version, and the main concern is that the dog can somehow get the collar off. I really don't see how that would happen unless the dog was wrestling with another dog and the fastener was miraculously wedged in just the right way to undo the clasp... but you should really have the collar on unless your dog is on leash anyway.

product_name: Marineland Rite Size A Filter Cartridge 6 pk
review_title: Exceeds expectations in addition to being a cost effective solution to small aquarium filtration.
review_text:
Item was not in the same box as pictured and I am not sure of the difference between what I received and what I ordered (if there is any). I received the item in the photo I uploaded so I am very pleased with this order. It is hard to beat Amazons price especially if you are purchasing from local stores. I have been using these for years even after trying other brands and self-assembled filters however, I always go back to these since they work very well and simple to replace. This is the most cost effective filter for my 10-gallon fish aquariums.

Remember to change your filter every 3 weeks and not to perform and other maintenance for at least 3-5 days to avoid disturbing the biological chemistry. Here is my schedule for the filter swap:
Week 1 - 10% water change.
Week 2 - 25% water change (suctioning debris from gravel).
Week 3 - change out the filter (remove just enough aquarium water to rinse the filter).
Week 4 - restart cycle at Week 1 (Week 4 = Week 1).

Note: I use Seachem Prime to treat new water for the water changes.

product_name: Doggie Dooley Standard Pyramid Dog Toilet
review_title: Just a little bit flimsy, but does the job!
review_text:
The Doggie Dooley is a miniature septic tank. Environmentally, it is probably the best choice to get rid of your dog’s waste. If you are willing to spend some time setting it up and follow the enclosed directions EXACTLY, the Doggie Dooley works extremely well. This is a small project so plan on several days (or one entire day) to get everything set up. For sure, digging the hole for the unit is the most difficult part. I bought the 3500 Model, which came with a starter packet of digester tablets.

DRAINAGE - Your soil has to drain in order for this system to work. If your soil does not drain within 24-48 hours, the Dooley will not work. Before purchasing, you should first test your soil by digging a small hole in your yard and filling it with water. If it doesn’t completely drain in 2 days, you have to find a different spot in your yard where it will drain. Consider the climate in your area. If you live in a very wet climate, this may not work anywhere in your yard. I used to live in North Carolina and our soil there sometimes took a week to drain. Here in Northern California, it drains pretty quickly.

ASSEMBLY - The unit is made of fairly hard plastic and the assembly was pretty easy. It took maybe 15 minutes to put it together. It came with 4 sides, screws and nuts, the green flip lid, and a square ring that snaps inside to help reinforce the top.

DIGGING - Digging the hole took me about 3 days total - in 100 degree heat and working on it a little bit at a time. The 3500 requires a hole of least 20” by 20” wide and 14” deep. That does not sound like a big hole, but it is after you start digging. My soil has a lot of rocks, so it was no small task. I used two shovels, a wheelbarrow, and a small pick axe to dig the hole. Using a little water to soften the ground helped a lot in the digging. Be careful where you dig - if you are unsure, use a utility locator to identify pipes or conduit in the ground. A lot of reviews complain about the sides collapsing when filling in the dirt around the unit. Mine only did this slightly. When you fill in the sides around the unit, you have to be gentle and do it very slowly, alternating the sides (the enclosed instructions say this). I used a garden trowel to fill in the sides and took my time. Do not step on the soil to pack it down, as this will certainly make the walls collapse. There is a rigid reinforcement ring that fits inside the unit, just underneath the lid to help keep the shape. If this piece were made of stronger material (maybe metal), I feel that the shape would be less likely to distort after filling in the dirt and the lid-closing problem would not be an issue. After you fill it in, you need to make sure that the lid closes properly before committing to starting up the Dooley. Spray water around the area with a hose and make sure everything is settled. Refill the area around it, afterwards if any settling occurs. The lid needs to close completely to keep flies out and the smell in!

ENZYMES - You can use either the Dooley tablets [[ASIN:B00CJBH5K6 Doggie Dooley 36 Waste Tablets, White]] or the powder [[ASIN:B0002I0F96 Doggie Dooley 3116 Waste Terminator, 1-Year Supply]] (which you mix with water first). I have also read that you can use Rid-X. I prefer the Dooley tablets because they are easier to use. The enzymes help to feed the bacteria which break down the stools and turn the solid into liquid. You add the enzymes once per week. The solids will eventually break down into a semi-liquid state (sludge) and then drain away into the soil. In general, the warmer it is outside, the faster the breakdown will occur.

WATER! - Just like a house septic system, you have to keep putting water into the unit weekly (or even daily) in order to keep the soil-leaching process going. You cannot let the unit dry out completely. If you do, you will get flies and you will have to restart the digester all over again. The more water you use, the more leaching will occur. It’s best to install the unit someplace where you can easily put water into it (near a hose, etc.). I just fill up a bucket and it is a short walk to the Dooley. Keeping the system wet will minimize fly problems.

Follow the instructions and this WILL work! Also, it is made in the USA (Ohio)!

review_title: Surprisingly high quality for a plastic product
review_text:
This product is of surprisingly high quality. I put together dozens of plastic things of similar complexity as the kids were growing up, and expected this to be the same barely-fitting-together, loosely assembled, rickety thing. But no - the parts fit together snugly and cleanly, the few metal parts fit in their designated spots perfectly, and the whole thing feels solid. Another nice touch - the sizes of the screw-on metal parts are selected such that they won't fit in another part's place, so you can basically do what little assembly is required without looking at the instructions - again, an unexpected level of sophistication. I was planning to glue on some no-slip rubber pads on the bottom to prevent the whole thing sliding too easily on the hardwood floor, but no - non-slip rubber feet are already included. That last bit of touching forethought almost made me cry.

One little gripe I have about this enclosure is that I wish it would fold up like an accordion when you want to put it away. As it is, the joined sections fold neatly in one direction but not in the other. So to put it away, I will have to separate it into four two-part sections rather than simply break the circle and fold up the whole thing as one piece. I imagine there is a good reason to not allow the sections to fold both ways that I have yet to discover, otherwise it would be done - the rest of the product is too well thought for this to be omitted unintentionally.

This pet carrier backpack is awesome! I had been looking at them for a few weeks and comparing different styles, options. We go on trips a lot with our dog but sometimes it's too far for her to walk or there are too many people around to walk her. She's 6 lbs but has very long legs. Also, I can't wait to try using it as a car seat for her since there is a strap to slide a seatbelt through in the back to secure it to the car seat.

One thing that I would like to see improved: the shoulder straps need more padding. They aren't very comfortable with the weight of the dog inside the carrier and for any distance of walking. So if there's any way to add more padding that would be a huge plus!

I am very happy with this product and it will get a lot of use. My dog and I both love it!! review_text: This is a beautiful stroller.  We purchased our SECOND Pet Gear, no zip, supposedly top of the line jogging stroller not too long ago and it has obviously undergone material changes and is no longer good quality.  Deciding to try another brand, we went with Gen7Pets G7 Jogger and it is noticeably superior with its much smoother, cushioned ride, lighter weight, zippered storage basket underneath and the parent tray with a secure lid (on the other one I worried about losing my keys or glasses in the tray). It was so simple to put together, even I, who can hardly put shoes in a box in the correct configuration, put it together myself in minutes.  It has so many nice features, I'm sure we'll enjoy our weekend promenades with Prince and Cio-Cio, our Japanese Chin dogs.  Of course I can't speak about its longevity at this point, but I am confident and hopeful that this one will last quite a long time.  I believe it was worth the money.  The bed part itself is a few inches shorter than the Pet Gear stroller, so do take that into consideration when choosing your stroller...however, since the Pet Gear one's zipper broke (my dog escaped from the back at the vet's office because of that), and the brake bar broke, the frame broke, the wheel fell off, etc...I DO NOT RECOMMEND PET GEAR.  I recommend GEN7PETS!  Thank you to Gen7Pets for providing such a nice stroller when I saw my other one becoming a pile of junk.  And Prince and Cio-Cio thank you too!  UPDATE:  After three months, the red fabric is developing tears around the edge of the frame.  This is not going to last too long, unfortunately.  That fabric needs to be much better quality, like the kind used in luggage, and put a little padding around the edge so the metal bar doesn't poke through. review_text:
In my quest to complete my whole home stereo system (which is really just a trial and error exercise for various gadgets amps speakers and cables) I've found myself in need of some compact muscle to fill in the gaps.

In my opinion this handsome little amp falls in the error column. It is a good looking little amp that's got some weight to it and feels solidly built but lacks any real power. I ran this amp side by side against the lepy 2024+ using various inputs and speakers both 4 and 8 ohms and the lepy beat this amp in every conceivable way (except looks maybe) at half the price.

Firstly this amp begins clipping at cuts out at volumes that the lepy cruises right on past. Both amps tend to clip when driving my 8 ohm klipsch speakers which I have a couple different models of but the lepy does so at far higher volumes then the smsl . When driving 4 ohm klipsch satellites the lepy drives them far past comfortable volumes and the smsl wimps out again. All the small amps I've tested do a way better job with 4 ohm speakers likely due to less resistance on their digital circuitry but the lepy leaves this amp in the dust.

The lack of any tone nobs makes this amp a far lessor option for a whole home rig because I don't really want to be making these adjustments on my computer because will affect the sound throughout my entire house.

The second input on both amps does not deliver a quality sound on either amp in comparison to the rca inputs but I guess that's to be expected and I've used other gadgets to eliminate the need for them but again the lepys second input delivers superior sound to the smsl delivered.

I'm no electrical engineer but I've been playing in bands for over 20 years and been listening to music since being in the womb and I trust what I hear. My advice would be to skip this purchase, get the lepy 2024 + and save yourself at least $30 in the process!

review_text:
Updated:

After the second recharging on an intelligent charger, these batteries will no longer hold a charge. My original four star review has been updated to one star. Old review:

This is going to be a two pronged review focusing on the batteries and then the travel charger.

These SecurityIng 18650 Li-Ion Rechargeable Batteries have been working well in the lights (tactical style LED torches) that we have been trying them in today. Those lights have low to moderate draw, and are acceptable use for these style batteries. I would recommend these batteries to others for such use, based on our experience, though would like more information on the source battery used and the specifics of the drain and overcharge protection. For the sale price (currently under ten bucks for the entire set), the batteries have worked quite well.

The travel charger that came with these batteries truly seems underpowered or over constrained. After plugging in the travel charger for our test, putting it and the batteries in a fire proof soft case, and heading out to lunch... we returned two hours later to find them not yet charged.

After another couple hours, they had enough charge to work but were still not fully charged. I used Nitecore Intelligent i4 Charger (version 2) to finish the job, and once the batteries were properly charged they lit up the light well.

So here is my quandary: Inexpensive 18650 batteries that do the job when charged in a quality charger, five stars, delivered with a travel charger that just does not get the job done, one star. Since it really is the batteries that we care about, I blended those ratings into four overall stars.

The Amazon listing notes that these batteries are covered by a \\"30 Days Money Back Guarantee\\" and a \\"12 Months Warranty\\", so if an issue occurs within those periods I will return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. I am not going to bother replacing the travel charger since we have other options. We did receive these batteries gratis from the seller and put them to use to objectively find out how well they performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

If you are looking for 18650 batteries of this style, capacity, price and size, and if you are familiar with the properties and risk of these types of batteries and take appropriate precautions when using and charging, then these SecurityIng 18650 batteries might be just the batteries that you are looking for... but maybe you should consider other charger options like we did.

review_text:

I went back and tried to rerecord the same parts and noticed the same thing, as well as loss of audio thinking that my Tascam was having electrical problems. I tried out old tapes and noticed a loss in signal in tracks that had recorded fine. After a casual tape head cleaning I noticed that the signal on my old tapes had been restored, and that signal recorded back onto them just fine. I threw in one of these tapes and tried to record and got the same thing: total loss in whichever track I recorded in, and then a loss of playback in those same tracks.

I double checked and had my Tascam looked over, and had no electrical problems. Everything ends up fine after a head cleaning, but once I throw one of these in it seems to leave some sort of residue on the tape heads. Doesn't look like anyone else has had a similar problem here, but I can say that after countless hours troubleshooting that these tapes are definitely gumming up the Tascam's heads.

review_title: If time is not an issue, feel free to waste your time on this.
review_text: This is the third review I have given on this product (my original reviews have seem to have mysteriously vanished), and my opinion on it continues to deteriorate.  DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME, DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS PIECE OF CRAP.  You could spend your time with your lover, you could spend your time at a fine restaurant, you could spend your time with a good book or a video, but if you buy this crap you will waste your time on it. There were times when the computer would show the songs and the list in the folder moved to the clip jam, but the clip jam would say the play list was empty and would not play.  If you want songs in a particular order, and there are a lot of them, it can be a labor intensive process re-arranging them in your computer player before saving them as a custom playlist, but the final transfer to the clip player was not always successful.  I am too busy to waste this kind of time.  Good that all it does is play audio - nice for runs; good sound; DEFINITELY NOT USER FRIENDLY.  MORE, two days later.  DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY.  THIS IS A TOTAL PIECE OF JUNK.  I went in to edit one of my playlists, and now it will not read the new one.  It says that playlist is "empty" but the computer says there are files in that folder. review_title: NOT RECOMMENDED: Horrible song management, confusing hardware layout, unintuitive and ununiformed controls, and more
review_text:
I originally wasn’t going to review the Tom America MP3 Player. Though, it’s so bad, that I felt an injustice by ignoring it. This is what you’d buy from Chinatown as a Christmas gag gift. If it isn’t a gag gift, you’ll either use it once before it breaks, or break it yourself. Details inside, including a full TLDR.

▶ Package Contents
• Tom America MP3 Player
• 16gb Micro SD Card
• Mini USB Cable
• 3.5mm Stereo Earphones
• User manual

▶ Specifications
Usually I’d state specifications here, but this MP3 player has absolutely no documentation for such information.

▶ Hardware
The hardware of the Tom America MP3 Player is very confusing. It tries very hard to be an iPod Nano clone, but fails miserably.

It measures at 3.75” x 1.6” x 0.25” with a 2” LCD screen. As the iPod Nano, at the bottom features a “mouse wheel”, which really is four buttons: Menu, Volume, Next Track, and Previous Track. At the center of the mouse wheel is an ON/OFF/Back/(Other?) button, but I’ve noticed that the switch at the top controls ON/OFF as well.

The top features the micro SD slot for inserting memory cards. This should be expandable up to 128GB, but I wouldn’t understand using a $100+ micro SD card on a cheap MP3 player.

The bottom features a 3.5mm audio port, for your standard headphones, a microphone, and a mini USB cable port. It’s very interesting to be using a mini USB port, since it’s a deprecated charging interface that hasn’t been used for many small electronics in almost 8 years. It should have featured a micro USB port, as it’s common in cell phones, tablets, speakers, and several other small electronics.

A micro SD card reader is unnecessary, as you’re able to connect the MP3 player to your computer and transfer files.

▶ Software
What seems as a trivial pursuit in hardware is even worse in software.

Picture this. You turn on the media player and are welcomed by a wonderful multi-color display. The display is very much pixelated, but pictures and video are easily recognizable. It’s nothing to complain about at its price point.

There are several menus to choose from: Music, Record, Play (Recordings), Movie, Radio, Picture, Settings, Text (eBooks), and Games (yes, that isn’t a misprint).

Lots a choices! Let’s choose one: Music. That’s when you realize how unintuitive the controls are. While in main menu selection, you’re required to press the “Menu Button”, because the center button doesn’t select, instead it powers your MP3 player off.

The controls in your desired menu will vary. Sometimes they’ll be as described, but many times they aren’t. It became very frustrating to have the Center button select in one menu, and then turn off my MP3 player in another. There simply aren’t any uniform controls, let alone intuitive ones.

▶ Testing
I’ve been trying very hard to objectively use this MP3 player for the past few days. Unfortunately, it has become very difficult to use an MP3 Player with lackluster buttons. I’ve literally had to hard press the buttons in order for them to work. I’ve never had to apply such force to an MP3 player before.

This made playing games almost impossible. It’s difficult to play Tetris or Snake when the feedback of the buttons are over a second long.

Music quality of songs were clear and crisp. Though, how the media player handles music is awful. Despite including a micro SD card that can hold almost 2000+ songs, it’ll only play a handful of them. I’d say about 30-40. The music isn’t shuffled either. There is no way to shuffle music.

Recording audio was very nice, as the microphone is sensitive but not too sensitive. I didn’t hear any static on playback.

▶ Final Thoughts
At times it pains me toreview items that are so bad that I wonder why I accepted the review unit in the first place. Button feedback is bad, interface is unintuitive, and the MP3 player doesn’t play more than a handful of songs. The way I see it, you paid $24 for a 16GB Micro SD card, a Mini USB Cable, and 3.5mm Ear phones. The MP3 player is just the item that cons you into buying it.

1 Star (I’d rate -100 Stars if I could)
NOT RECOMMENDED (NEVER EVER EVER EVER BUY THIS)

▶ TLDR;
Pros:
+ Cheap price point.
+ A vivid colorful display.
+ A wide menu variety.
+ Includes 16GB Micro SD Card, Generic Earphones, and a mini USB Cable
+ Able to transfer files without the need of an SD Card reader

Cons:
