- A very confusing hardware layout. Two ON/OFF buttons?
- Very unintuitive and ununiformed controls. Center button will turn player ON/OFF in one menu, and be required to select in the next.
- Horrible song management. No shuffling and only plays a handful of the songs on the micro SD (Only about 30-40 of the about 400 songs for me).
- Buttons wear very quickly. Will require you to hard press in order to get any feedback. Makes playing games impossible.

Sound quality is pretty good too. I think there is a bit too much bass and it ends up overshadowing the treble, but an EQ easily solves that.

The bluetooth connectivity however has been really bad so far. The range itself seems to be fine, but the connection is too unstable. Sometimes, just by putting my phone inside my pocket or maybe covering the earbuds' volume control with my hands, the music starts breaking up badly. And sometimes it keeps working perfectly well even with some distance and heavy/dense objects between the earbuds and my phone. There doesn't seem to be a pattern, and it's driving me mad.

My phone is a Nexus 5 and I've extensively used its bluetooth connection with other audio devices before and I've never had this kind of issue.

Overall these are really good earbuds but this bluetooth problem is just too annoying.

EDIT: I did some tests and the connectivity is not unstable, it is permanently terrible. Way worse than I had previously thought. Even the slightest interferance (eg: my hands or my empty backpack, or even just tilting my head a little bit) can completely block out the bluetooth signal, which is absurd for a $100 device.

review_title: Sweat problems with remote almost from the start
review_text:
I've used these first lightly when I received them last February (2014). I progressed to using them more and more from September or so, up till about two weeks ago when I decided that enough is enough and I'm looking to buy better earphones. Bought them with a group of friends through a third party that orders from Amazon in bulk and forwards to our country where Amazon doesn't ship electronics (Israel).

Pros:
These were great when I used these earphones running or walking in the autumn and the winter.
The music sounds clear, they're comfortable to wear most of the time and they're really light.

Cons:
The memory wire doesn't really keep in place properly, it needs adjustments every 15 minutes or so, but it's not so bad.
The clip that supposedly attaches to the shirt isn't strong enough so I didn't use it. The metal spring that holds it rusted from my sweat but it still holds. The problem with it is that when it's not attached firmly, it bounces and makes a lot of noise that makes it hard to hear the music that's playing.

The real problems started when the spring and summer approached. Running in a humid climate with 30+ degrees Celsius outside is what really did it for me - the sweat did enter the remote/microphone device, and it did do something wrong to the electronics inside. Maybe it's just mine that's faulty, but since the first time that it let the sweat go in, it takes a few minutes of playing with the volume control to make it play in both ears simultaneously. I wish it ended there, but it didn't. So now I put the remote inside my shirt when I run so that it doesn't bounce, and there it encounters the aforementioned sweat yet again. At several points, the sweat made it pause, rewind and forward the songs up to a point where I just turned the music off.
Another sweat problem is when it gets in your ear and makes the buds slide out. Guess they're not strong enough to stay inside when it gets wet :-(
And another small con is the volume control which is separate from the mp3 player's volume control. Maybe I just got used to remotes that controlled the player's volume, but I don't like it the way it is with this product.
Also, the microphone wasn't good from the start - it always transmits ambient noises too loudly making the other side not able to hear me.

review_title: Great sound but build quality is down a little
review_text:
Like other customers, I had trouble with the paint finish being chipped on it from the factory on this set that was purchased through Amazon. I called SAS and asked about it (the only way to contact them. The email route doesn't work or gets ignored). They RMA'd them with little trouble and I received a new set promptly. The new set looked and sounded great when I used it for the first month with my iPhone 4S. The main problem I had with them is that when using them to make a hands-free call, the person on the other end would hear themselves in a severe echo. I couldn't hear any sound problems at all during the call. If I unplugged the earbuds the echo would go away until I connected them again. I tried using a set of the Apple Earpods with the same phone and there isn't any echo problem with them at all so I believe the echo is from the Woodees earbuds. The Mic/ Volume controls on the earbuds finally died abruptly one day but the sound is still good like always. It doesn't have a damaged cable or anything like would normally cause something like that to go out. I believe the Mic/ Volume control had a electrical defect that caused it to go bad. Since I had another problem with this set I tried to email them again from the same email regarding the paint and have not received any response over a two week period. I will have to call but haven't had the time.

Only other gripe is the earbud tips are sized weird for my ear canal. The largest one seems to be too big (but it fits the best out of the three sizes) and the medium size seems to be too small where they don't seal properly. I also had to get them angled just right to get a good seal even with the large size, otherwise the sound quality is poor. I would suggest a set of the Comply earbud tips made for these earbuds. I haven't tried them out yet since the Mic part quit working before I had a chance to buy them so I quit using the set until I get it replaced.

TL;DR - Product looks and sounds great, build quality is questionable and customer service is lacking since the only way you can get a response is to call. The email doesn't work apparently.

I'm an old timer so I'm not fussy about buds too much as long as the sound is pretty good I'm ok with it. But then I bought some new music and tried to transfer it to the Evo but ....nothing. So I'm stuck with the same original songs that I started with. Someone suggested that I load music from Amazon but I don't really see how to do that without the Drop n' Drag option, unless somebody in here can steer me right. The radio feature is good....if you're sitting in the same spot, if you move around at all you lose the station. So I liked it at first....a lot actually, it did what I wanted it to do. Until it didn't. I contacted Kubik to see if they could help but no answer yet. If nothing soon, I'll be looking for a different device. Too bad cause this one was pretty cool.....for a bit. So now I'm looking for a new item that will serve my simple expectations and last longer with the option to add some new music now and then. I would not recommend buying this. Since I wrote this I have played around with an old laptop I have that runs on Windows 7 and lo and behold, I can load music on this with the old laptop so now it isn't a total loss for me. I like the device in every other way other than the fact that without the ability to load music, to be able to open the folders, it is pretty much useless. So now I can use the old laptop for that purpose. I'm not changing the review though because I contacted Kubik and they never got to me. review_title: Can't secure them to your head
review_text:
There's one thing I like about these, and that's that sweat won't get into them since they're designed to be sealed! Sweet! No more headseats shorting-out! However, that one awesome feature is not enough to keep me using these. Connecting via bluetooth was painless.

Issues I have are:

Battery: The battery compartment is not intuitive, you'll have to read the instructions to figure out how to charge this thing. It takes one rechargable AAA battery (included) which must be removed in order to charge, and removing it is not completely easy as there are 2 "doors" that need to be opened to get to it. Would be great if it could be charged in the headset. A USB charger is supplied for the AAA that has the ability to charge 2-AAA batteries at once, which is a nice feature.

Sound: Sound comes across as muddy. I did try to make adjustements to improve this, but was not happy with what I got. It's not terrible, but it's not great either. I guess that's the trade off for getting something that is designed to transmit through bone.

Head Straps: Included with these headphones are 2 rubber straps that go on the rear of the headset to help tighten it to your head. Only one is needed, the second one is just an extra. They are not pictured with the product but they are an essential part of it. The problem is that the way the strap is designed, it comes loose very easily and you must re-tighten/adjust the strap very frequently. This is what makes these headphones completely unacceptable for using for exercising or working out, or even sitting at the computer. The strap is a critical piece and does not perform as-needed. Also, when wearing this headset, strap or no strap, when I look up or down, the headset gets moved out of alignment and I have to readjust it. This too is unacceptable. The headset is just unable to be secured well to the head. Even sitting at my desk, the back of the headset will hit the back of my neck and get out of alignment. If the rubber strap was able to be redesigned so that it wouldn't slide off from where you set it, perhaps some of these problems would go away, but as it is, there's just no way.

Although it doesn't get rave reviews, the best exercise headset I have used has been Denon AH-W150BK Exercise Freak In-Ear Headphones. I would recommend looking at those if you need something to exercise in.

review_text: The design of this speaker is very well done and it looks great (save for the random sticker in the corner that says the product title "Jomby Jukebox". The lights work well and I do like how the buttons are discreet (you press it on top and it actually pushes the cube down to push the button on the bottom of the box). So why am I giving it two stars? Whenever you turn on this speaker, it has the absolute most loud and obnoxious opening dubstep sequence with a strange distorted voiceover (It sounds like it's saying "this is your iPhone 4 speaking") and then immediately followed by a voiceover saying the bluetooth is on, however it's not a pleasant voiceover like Siri or Google, it sounds like a direct recording of someone's voice, however it doesn't seem like English is their native tongue. When the bluetooth connects the same person speaks again, and they're actually a bit difficult to understand because of their accent. I would much prefer a "beep" in confirmation, and no sound at all when it turns on. While I do feel the pricetag of 25$ is definitely reasonable considering this box can get rather loud for it's size, music quality is okay, and the lights are cool, I really can't get over the awkward voiceover and having to listen to the weird 15 second dubstep opening everytime I turn it on. I haven't had this product for long, so I can't attest for it's durability over time, but it's decent--- and if you dont mind the opening sequence and voiceover, it's definitely worth the money. I previously owned the Mobi Cube and bought this to replace it since my Cube died due to the common problem of the Cube refusing to charge after a few months. I prefer the lights and design of the Jomby Jukebox, but the Mobi Cube had a better build quality, adjustable light functions, much better sound quality, and most importantly, no dubstep, no voiceover.

-------------------
10/20 Update:
So 13 days after Sol Republic received my return, I am just now getting a refund. This is after basically calling Sol every other day, asking about the status of my refund. And I had to call from a different phone number, because for *some* reason, I could never get through to a customer service agent when using my phone, sometimes even getting sent straight to voicemail.

Bottom line: If you buy this, DO NOT BUY DIRECTLY FROM SOL REPUBLIC

10/15 UPDATE:
Sol Republic’s customer service is the worst. My return was received by Sol on October 8th, and a week later I still haven’t received my refund (or any kind of notification that it is coming soon).

I then call Sol’s customer support, who say they will call back me back soon with more details. Flash-forward 2 hours, still no call. So I sit on hold for 10 minutes and get kicked off, then again for 5 minutes. Still nothing.

So I dial *67 then Sol’s customer support #, and then miraculously they answer my call! What good fortune!

So to recap Sol’s poor customer service: it took them over 24 hours to email me back, then they didn’t refund me, and then they were obviously screening and not answering my calls. Just amazingly poor customer support.
-------------------

It just wasn’t very practical to have one earbud in, and the other just hanging down the front of my dress shirt. Also, I didn’t have a great experience with Sol Republic’s customer support (this time I bought from their website due to coupon code). I emailed customer support, inquiring about their return process and I still haven’t received a response as of 24 hours later. I then called customer support, and they said they would email me a RMA form so I could ship my return, but as of 1 hour later I haven’t received any email from Sol Republic customer support. I guess I need to call them again...

I think these headphones are great for when you are able to have both earbuds in while wearing a tshirt/polo shirt/unbuttoned dress shirt, but they just aren’t practical for a corporate office setting.

review_title: Ports stop working randomly! Power reset fixes that.
review_text:
This is our team charger at the office, the ports unfortunately sometimes stop working randomly, I was thinking it was a faulty port at the beginning, as only one had the issue, and I was assuming that, well, one out of six is still a keeper. But then I unplugged it and plugged it again, and all ports were working!

Then, a couple of hours later, bam, two ports stop working... Always a cord unplugging will reset the issue, but it is annoying. Sometimes four ports don't work, then two, and so on...

I think the PowerIQ circuitry isn't working properly or wasn't tested enough. As there is a higher probability that a port that hasn't been used in a while will not work when a cable is connected. So, maybe there is a shutdown in the circuitry that doesn't turn on again.

But well, now everybody at the office knows that a quick unplug/plug will reset the charger, so, we are keeping it.

I got so sick of the connection issues I bought the Anker Portable Speaker (A7909) and WOW - the Anker is totally better. The sound quality is so much better and battery life is twice as long. I didn't realize the DKnight sound quality was poor until I played it side-by-side with the Anker. Voices are crisper, bass is richer and I hear the various parts of the song better. It also has volume buttons on the speaker and if I get a call, the persons voice doesn't transfer to the speaker. I wish I had just paid more a few months ago and saved myself the hassle. I realize this has turned into a review of the Anker but I hate reading poor reviews of a product and wonder what product ended up working for that person... so if you can spare a few more dollars, buy the Anker ($27 vs $70). If you are strapped on cash, the DKnight will do and hopefully yours lasts longer than 3 months with no issues.

review_title: Not Recommended - Issues with Optical Output - Noise Glitches, Audio Mute Problems Cause Frustration - Bad With Pandora
review_text:
Note: Updated to reflect experience found after trying the sister device, Monoprice Bluetooth receiver with APTX support. I have owned both.

I had high hopes for the Satechi Bluetooth receiver, as I use the TOSLINK optical digital output to use with an external digital-to-analog converter (DAC) for great sound quality. I purchased this unit to replace my former Belkin BT HD which worked well and mostly very reliably and also features a TOSLINK optical output but not APTX support.

However, after having tried the Monorprice unit as well as it's companion, repackaged as the Satechi model, I found they share the same frustrating problems. What problems, you may ask?

Note: I use the unit within about 1 ft from my phone and have no nearby Bluetooth units that may cause interference. I do not use the analog stereo outputs, in order to get maximum use out of the capabilities of the receiver.

- Audio dropout (muting) problems: There appears to be a somewhat frequent problem with the beginning of audio tracks losing the first ~2 seconds of sound when playing media, especially when using Pandora. For example, when switching songs in Pandora, the beginning of each song just "dissappears". I have discovered that the sound is being greatly reduced for some reason, and therefore can't be heard momentarily.

This happens very often, although not 100% of the time. Similar with movies and .MP3s, etc. It is as if the unit has sync problems or has muted audio when no signal is momentarily present, and can't catch up correctly when data is sent over Bluetooth. Very frustrating!!

Again, this was not an issue when using my original Belkin HD receiver.

- Random noise problems: There seems to be a random issue with a crackly, grating sound lasting for just a moment that seems appear for no apparent reason at times. No idea why this is happening.

- Sound quality: no complaints; upper frequency range is nice, and I have tested with videos, Apple lossless .M4A files and 320kbps .MP3s as well as .CDA (standard CD) tracks. So far, the APT-X support seems to sound nice and works well.

Unfortunately, I will have to switch back to my Belkin BT HD Bluetooth receiver which did not exhibit the problems listed above and seemed to work well.

If you change media or music fairly frequently, I would recommend you consider other Bluetooth receivers and avoid having to deal with the beginning of your music mysteriously dissappearing. product_name: Denon DBT-1713UD 3D Ready Blu-ray disc, DVD, Super Audio CD Player with Networking
review_title: Suffers from serious technical flaws and high cost
review_text:
I've been a long time Denon fan, but unfortunately, the DBT-1713UD shows that Denon is a mere shadow of its former self. I first purchased this unit as a refurb, and it was a dud right out of the box. Ok, it happens, right? So, I return it to Denon directly who, after several weeks of me requesting status, decided to send me a brand new unit.

Thinking that was the end of my trouble, I soon realized that Denon is out of its depth when dealing with streaming. I purchased this unit to replace it's adequate but painfully slow predecessor, the DBP-1610, because I wanted a unit that offered streaming capability as well. The performance of this unit is somewhat faster when handling blu-rays, and that's about the extent of its benefits.

The firmware in this device is horrible; even after a few updates, it is not production quality. The streaming mode, whenever the streaming menu is shown, is a dedicated mode and must be exited using the remote before even trying to eject the tray to put a disc in. The buttons on the unit are unresponsive until you exit this mode.

The interaction between the device firmware and the built-in Netflix app is ridiculous. To register the device, the netflix username and password must be entered using an onscreen keyboard. Much more inconvenient than entering a device code from the Netflix website like many other players use. This is especially frustrating when the player will "forget" my credentials after a few failed attempts when trying to stream. Half the time when I select a title to play, the player drops out of the netflix app. I must re-enter the streaming menu, select the netflix app and start again. Every so often, after a few of these dropouts, my credentials are gone and I need to re-enter them... on that !@#$@! on screen keyboard.

The Hulu app seems much more stable, but the navigation for it is not intuitive compared to the browser version. The youtube app is probablythe best of the bunch, as it seems the most stable and the easiest to navigate.

I would say 1 out of 8 discs I initially insert cause the player to freeze and become unresponsive while it tries to access it, this is especially true if the player has already been in a streaming session. It requires that I power cycle the machine, and then it begins playing the disc normally. This is with BD-Live disabled, of course, which I did first thing. The BD-Live functionality I found is much more trouble than its worth and slows down disc interaction quite a bit.

Other manufacturers are providing the same level of video and audio performance, coupled with much more capable firmware features for, in many case, a fraction of the cost of what Denon is offering. It pains me to say that this will be my last Denon product.

But rather than blame my myself, I realize that these are the only earbuds I've ever owned that I've had that problem, including another pair of Philips sport ear buds that work just fine (I also tested them against Amazon basic, and Onkyo earbuds.) Unfortunately, I can't exercise or do anything active while I hold the earhooks at just the right angle to listen. Or I could just accept the fit as is and forgo any kind of bass response. product_name: StarTech.com HDMI Over Dual CAT5 / CAT6 Extender with Infrared IR 100ft /30m HDMI Over Ethernet Cable Extender Power Free 1080p
review_title: It works well, IF your HDMI port supplies enough voltage to the unit
review_text:
Ok, here is the deal with this device. It's a passive device, meaning it does not have a power supply that plugs into it, it uses PoE or power over ethernet, in this case, power over HDMI. This was the feature that was so attractive to me for this device because I do not have utility power at the receiver point in my blu-ray to projector setup. So the transmitter unit relies completely on the power it gets from the HDMI port of your device. IF your device (blu-ray, computer, game system) does not provide sufficient current to the transmitter unit from the HDMI port, it can not stay connected whether you run 28m or 3m of cable. This was the case for me. I would plug the device in and it would flash the display for a moment and then go away. The lights on the StarTech would just blink. I must have re-crimped my CAT 6 connectors 4 or 5 times before I just got frustrated.

I had set up an return authorization with AV House to return the device but decided to give it one last try, so I went over to RadioShack and bought a $20 powered HDMI in line amplifier, key word being powered. This little bugger has a 5VDC/1A power supply that ramps up the power of the HDMI signal and when I plugged that in front of my StarTech transmitter, the signal locked in and I had a very solid transmission that has streamed without lag, skip, or fail to this point.

My advice, would be to buy a powered unit to avoid the hours of frustration I had to deal with, but if you can't supply utitlity power to the receiver end of your extender then this device is a better option. Just be prepared to potentially drop another few bucks on a powered amplifier if your device can't support it.

product_name: Sony NWZE38 Walkman MP3 Player
review_title: Not as good as older Walkman
review_text: I bought this player about a year ago. I intended to use it to replace an older 8-gig Sony Walkman. The sound quality seems about the same as the older Walkman, but in almost all ways the older Walkman is better than this one. So I've kept my older one for use in situations where the new one is frustrating (when driving, walking or exercising at the gym).  My biggest frustration is just turning the thing on. To turn it on, you press any of the buttons. Then you wait a few seconds until it says it's on hold. Then you hold down the OPTION button for a couple of seconds until that goes away. Then it goes into a "creating library" phase that usually lasts from 2 to 20 seconds. Then you press the play/pause button and it finally starts to play. Figure around 8-20 seconds to turn it on, while having to watch the screen. So I especially do not recommend this player if you, like me, want to use the player in the accessory input of your car radio. It's just too much of a driving distraction to turn it on. For the older Walkman, a touch of a button turns it on. If it's been used within the last 24 hours, it comes on immediately. Otherwise a several second delay but no other actions needed.  The older Walkman isn't much larger than this one, but it has a much larger screen. It displays more info about the song being displayed - title, performer, album, year released and music category. This one only alternates between showing the performer and song title.  The layout of the older Walkman made it very easy to use the controls by feel. When in my car, going for a walk, exercising in the gym or listening to music in bed, I like to be able to control it by feel. With the layout this one has, I have a much more difficult time using them by feel, and often hit the wrong button. Of course, it is a lot better than a touch screen if you want to go by feel, but Sony has really gone backwards from the older model.  The one feature that this one has that my older one did not haveis a sleep timer. I really like that feature, except that it's implemented poorly in this device. When the sleep timer is active, you cannot use either the BACK button or the OPTION button without first cancelling the sleep timer. This means you can't, among other things: Switch to a different playlist. Search for an album or artist. Display details about the song being played. You can't even display the current time.  Playlists are similar on both devices, with one big difference. The older Walkman remembers the songs you've played in a playlist, while the newer one doesn't. The newer one doesn't do this. So, for example, if I have a 200-title playlist and listen to it over ten sessions of 20 songs per session, turning the device off in the meantime, the older Walkman will have played each song exactly once. The newer one will have played a lot of duplicates, and a lot of songs wouldn't have been heard. In practice, I usually listen to about 10 songs each evening, and I usually hear at least two or three songs that I listened to the night before.   So - sound quality is fine, it's only the controls that are frustrating. I use Windows Media Player to construct playlists, and use the automatic sync to keep the two players in sync - works great with both players, so no gripes there.

review_text:
I just started looking for bookshelf speakers and after reading rave reviews, the Zensor 1's were on my short list to audition.

I had high expectations but I found the speakers to be veiled in the midrange, adversely affecting vocals. The bass was muddy and the soundstage was small. Perhaps my expectations were too high for a $400 speaker. The same day I auditioned the Wharfedale Diamond 220's. They were $50 less and sounded better, but still had a veiled midrange. However, for $350, they are a good deal.

I have no horse in this race and I do not work for any of these speaker companies. Audio has been a hobby of mine, on and off for 30 + years. My recommendation to anyone looking to purchase is to audition these for yourself as well as some more expensive speakers to see how they differ. That will also reveal areas of weakness. Then, you will be able to determine what is important to you and how much you will need to pay to find something you enjoy.

review_text:
I started taking an interest in headphones ever since my Dad brought me the sony mdr zx 100 for my birthday. At that age I didn't really care about sound quality or the cheapness of a headphone, just something I can listen to. But a couple of years forward my interest in headphones began to peak. I was listening from headphones like Audiotechnica m50x, JVC S500's and even the Sennheiser Momentums. So when I browsed amazon one day and found this little upgraded version of my first headphone, I was a bit excited. I started having this interest in comparing the two headphones. I also had brought the SONY MDR ZX 110 for a little extra.

So is it really an upgrade? Unfortunately, the looks and comfort of the headphone can only defined as an "upgrade".

The sound of the headphones is a bit bland, as it losses a little of the bass that the previous SONY MDR ZX 100 and 110 had. And though this headphone, the SONY MDR ZX310, has a bit, and I mean a tiny bit, more clarity then the SONY MDR ZX 100, it losses it's exciting signature from the previous models. And yes I have burned these headphones in for a decent amount of time.

In terms of outward appearance, these are definitely a step up. Personally the white and the lime green version of the headphone are a deal breaker for me as they really stand out. The only problem with the white is that it's literally a cheap looking version of the white SONY MDR ZX 600. On this headphone the outer rim of it gives off this nice black metallic look, similar to the SONY XB 450. There is also the green cord that comes with it, ending the tip of the L- shaped audio jack with a gray finish.

Yes this is a gray headphone, with green earpads, not black.

Comfort though is a bit debatable. You see these headphones come with ear pads that are like the cheap version of the SONY MDR ZX 600's. The feeling is like the same plastic material of the original SONY MDR ZX 100 but stretched out and more "clean" looking. There really isn't much padding as it's very thin, but because of the lightweight, you really wouldn't worry about it. They block out more sound outside then the SONY MDR ZX 100 and 110, but it's nowhere near the XB 450.

Also the pads do make your ear's sweat a little after extended use, but honestly I would pair them up with the replacement ear pads they sell on amazon for an extra five bucks. That's just my personal preference.

So if your excited about the sound these headphones deliver, you'll be a bit dissapointed, as the recessed bass is the only significant difference between the older models. But if your looking for a headphone your not afraid to wear in public, this is definitely a good start.d more "clean" looking. product_name: CTYRZCH(TM) Wireless VGA Signal Extender Booster Signal Ethernet Cable Including a Wireless Transmitter and a Receiver 1080P Extending the VGA Signal 60 Meters by a CAT-5e/6 Cable
review_title: Confusing product descriptions detract from a product that actually works as designed for the intended purpose.
review_text:
First of all, I think this product does exactly what it is intended to do. However, the Amazon site documentation, and the product packaging have, at best ambiguous and, at worst misleading, information. What I really wanted was something to transmit and receive a VGA signal through the internet. The Amazon description includes the following:

"The transmitter which is linked with main engine will convert the VGA signal to standard TCP/IP and transmit by internet.
This receiver which is connected with the display will convert the standard TCP/IP signal into VGA signal."

At another place it says the transmission is over a single wire. To me those statements are contradictory. I expected the latter was correct, and that the former has a very limited definition of "internet". I don't think just using a Cat5e or Cat6 cable really defines an internet transmission.

I ordered it, since it was inexpensive, to be sure.The good news is that if you make the connection across a single ethernet cable, it works flawlessly. Across an actual internet connection (even a wired one) it does nothing.

To further confuse things, the front of the box it comes in describes what it actually does, but there is another statement there that I can't understand at all. It says:

"Converts Coaxial or Toslink digital audio signals to analog L/R audio"

That would be a neat trick since it has no Toslink, Coaxial or analog audio connectors. This text is directly beside a picture of the product that clearly shows that statement is impossible. So what the heck is that about? It didn't matter to me because I wasn't looking for that functionality, but it certainly is bizarre. So if you need to extend a VGA signal over a longer Cat5e or Cat6 cable, you're in business, but don't expect anything else.

review_title: Just didn't live up to expectations

The waterproof feature of the speaker is top-notch, and it has survived several trips to the pool, where my kids promptly put it into heavy use by taking it into the water. It then became a bit of a toy as they threw it back and forth to each other. This hasn't affected the performance or functionality of the speaker one bit. That said...

I just don't like it as much as it's non-waterproof brother (The NYNE Portable Bluetooth Speaker: http://www.amazon.com/NYNE-Multimedia-Inc-Portable-Bluetooth/dp/B00I9ID070/ref=sr_1_8?ie=UTF8&qid=1429031820&sr=8-8&keywords=nyne+speaker). I understand the waterproof aspect of the speaker has a detrimental effect on the sound (even out of water), but I'm a total baby about how speakers perform. This speaker sounds tinny, and has very little bass response. Bluetooth speakers in general don't always have the best performance, but there are a few on the market - including the NYNE speaker I linked to above - that provide substantially better sound.

If you're needing a speaker you can totally abuse for your outings to the pool, lake, etc, and you don't really care too much about the sound, then this should definitely be your go-to. However, if you're an audio baby like I am, I would recommend going with it's big brother I linked above.

review_title: A choice worth considering, especially if you need to charge more than NiCd & NimH AA/AAA
review_text:
In comparing this charger to my Lacrosse BC-900, I still prefer the Lacrosse.

Good features:
+Charges Lithium ion batteries and more sizes due to the sliding contacts.
+Charges cells independently
+Recognizes cells with low voltage (a common problem with other chargers)

Bad Points:
+Not as programmable as others (no refresh mode for multiple cycles), though it can test capacity, discharge and charge
+Preset charging current of 500mA
+Really loud beep when finished with each cell, that can't be turned off
+Not quite as smart at detecting full charge voltage drop

Overall, if I absolutely needed to charge LiON cells or I could get this charger for a good savings compared to the well known brands, I'd consider it again.

product_name: House of Marley Uplift Midnight In-Ear Headphones
review_title: These House of Marley headphones are good, not great
review_text:
These House of Marley headphones are good, not great. I’ll get the major drawback out of the way first. Because of the braided fabric cord, the microphonics (you know that loud sound you get when the cord rubs against your shirt or jacket?) are TERRIBLE. These have to be the worst pair of headphones I’ve had in this respect although, to be fair, this is my first pair ever with a fabric-covered cord. My previous pairs (MEElectronics M9P, Apple, some other random Panasonics, Sonys, and others – none particularly HIGH quality) have been better than the Marleys. If you jog with these, forget about a clean sound.

Also, the cords are not as tangle-free as others. Better than some, but not as good as others. They still tangle, in my experience.

On the positive side, they do have a very distinctive look, if that’s your thing. I don’t mind them. The sound is also pretty good, if a bit bass-heavy. My pair has a mic with a single button (mutes when on a call, pauses/plays music) which works on my Android phone. Sound quality is acceptable, I’m told, although you pretty much do have to hold the mic up to your mouth and shield any kind of wind – mic is average. They also seem fairly durable in the 5-6 months I’ve had them, given that I travel frequently and use them every trip (I do have a pair of Bose QC25’s I use when on the plane, but tend to use the Marleys otherwise).

In all, I think there are better options out there (the MEElectronics M9P, for example, I would recommend over these for the price, or the Sennheiser MM30), but these are a decent set and would have rated better, were it not for the microphonics.

review_title: Heavy. Uncomfortable. Too quiet. Poorly designed. But nice concept. (Or, "earbuds vs RP-BTGS10")
review_text: 11/10/2015: I have updated my review by one star after using this item pretty much daily for the past few months. I still feel it is uncomfortable, and the volume is too low, and the battery compartment stuff is cheesy, but the convienience of not having cables is really nice. It also makes you look like a Borg with little ear pieces sticking out (but not covering your ears). I am sold on the concept of wireless headphones like this, but feel there is much room for improvement in design. I'd say: definately get something like this, but unless there is a great cost savings with this Panasonic model, look elsewhere.  Oh, Panasonic. Weren't you once a leader in electronics? The Panasonic arr pee dash bee tee gee ess ten (why are product names so awful)? is a great concept. I like the idea of the around-the-ear earphones rather than the traditional over-the-head type, and perhaps there is an advantage if the unit it light, but the RP-BTGS10 is not light. After a week of daily use, I still find it heavy and uncomfortable.  The unique feature of this Bluetooth headset is that it isn't actually earphones. Instead of two earbuds that go in your ear, there are two soft pads that press against your skull just in front of your ears, leaving your ears open to the outside sounds around you. I was thrilled at this concept, since when I listen to audio at work, I only put one earbud in so I can hear people sneaking up on me. (I still smile every time I have to pound outside someone's cube to get their attention while they have earbuds in and cranked up, only to see them jump with surprise when they realize I am there.) This part works surprisingly well -- but the volume, even at max, is too quiet if there is any background noise. I can't hear anything while water runs in the sink in the breakroom, for instance. So far, my "one earbud in, one earbud out" method is better for noisy surroundings.  The next feature, Bluetooth, is simply great. I have pretty much always used earbuds (except in my home studio where I use large headphones). I have gone through many pair of earbuds over the years as the cable would get snagged and eventually cause one bud to short out. Without wires, this problem wouldn't happen. RP-BTGS10 wins here.  The unit is powered by a AAA rechargable battery, and claims to get around 4 hours of playback, though I was able to get through most of a full work day. Battery life seems okay, but be prepared to buy a spare AAA to keep charged unless you want to stop mid-day and wait for the "about an hour" recharge time. The included USB charger has slots for two batteries, but they only provide one. I guess they like their customers being inconvienienced. I'm going to give earbuds the edge here since they never need batteries.  Speaking of batteries, the battery compartment is ridiculous. There is an outside flap you have to open, then it hangs loose on a small strand, and then there is the battery door you push down on to open up on a hinge. Really, Panasonic? The AAA battery then slides in ... but which way? In an absolutely brilliant (sarcasm) design, the small diagram that shows which way the battery gets inserted is covered up when you open the battery compartment. Have the design engineers at Panasonic ever seen an Apple product? They should spend some time looking around an Apple Store to see how these problems have been solved long ago.  This device is "one size fits all", and they provide two colors of the same size rubber bands you can put on to tighten it. The bands have loops at each end and are meant to slide to some tiny notches. I gave up using these quickly, as they made the unit painfully tight, and the bands just kept sliding back over the notch. Awful design here, too.  This is really a poorly designed product. However, I have been using it in place of my earbuds (except when charging) because (if the area is quiet) wireless is so much more convienient (except for the recharging) than wired earbuds. I was expecting to use them while biking since it would leave the ears open to hear other bikes approaching -- but it seems clear that the wind rushing past would drown out any audio from these lackluster headphones.  Panasonic did do a decent job on the controls. On the back of the left arm is a toggle up and down that controls the volume. When you hit max volume, it beeps (muting the audio under it during the beep).  On the right is another up/down toggle for skipping tracks. On the outside right is a button that is supposed to start/stop the audio, but it only sometimes works with my old iPhone 3GS. I'm not sure why it's so intermittant (the physical earbuds always work ;). On the left side is another button for answering or hanging up a call, but I do not have phone service on my old phone (I use it just as an MP3 player and biking computer) so I was unable to test it.  I do like the carrying case. It has a removable pouch that holds the charger, though I am not sure why I would want to remove it since you always need the charger if you go anywhere for more than four or so hours. The headphones fit nicely, and then it zips closed and had a ridged outer shell. The case is the best part of this product.  Overall, if you don't find it heavy and uncomfortable, and are using it in quiet areas, it's a really cool headset. The quirks in the design of the RP-BTGS10 (that name just flows off the tongue, doesn't it?) are ones you quickly figure out, and it does do the job. I just hope there are better alternatives that are lighter and more comfortable (and maybe louder) out there. For all I know, this wretched thing may be best-in-class. That would be unfortunate.  Design quirks aside, YOU might find this totally comfortable and, in that case, my only critique would be the low volume level and short battery life. I am enjoying how well the "nothing in my ear" audio works.  I just don't enjoy Panosonics industrial design for this product.  I may updatethis review again in a few more weeks if anything changes.

review_title: TL;DR Great quality speaker broke down 4 months in deployment
review_text:
It is with a heavy heart that the United States of Mondo has the sorrowing duty of giving you this news. On Wednesday the 8th of April 2015, there were signs of your gift Shark Boombox was not holding a charge. Many attempts were ordered to help recover Shark Boombox (or "Gomez's Shark Boombox" as he was named) including: fully depleting the current charge, charging overnight, using different cables, using different chargers, continuity testing with a multimeter, and charging off ship however it seems that all wars have casualties. Although it may not be a casualty in the common use of the word, all losses are great to those who s/he was important to.

I only knew Mondo's Shark Boombox for maybe 4 months. However it is not the amount time together that defines a relationship, but rather the quality. Boombox has a heavy unit. His solid construction gave a quiet shout of confidence that even more expensive bluetooth speakers did not have. I personally dropped Boombox a number of times as well as him flying off somewhere due to heavy seas only to brush off the dust without missing a beat.The sound quality was nice, great even. However there would be a slight loss of low end when using very bass heavy music (particularly some hip-hop). High and middle of EQ'd great.

Run time was probably Boombox's specialty. Long run times were great. Plan the night before and youll be playing music on the go out on town or just bring it along at work.The ease of use of his setup maybe all to common these days, but it is a benchmark of a nice unit. I never got to use his phone ability due to the fact that Boombox was a forward deployed speaker, however I would like to think that had I used that ability while he was in service the duties would have been followed through with great detail.

Although there will be possible others (such as : NudeAudio Super-M, Creative Sound Blaster Roar, and Photive HYDRA Rugged Water Resistant Wireless Bluetooth Speaker) I can say that the time I had with BoomBox was great although I wish he would have made the entire deployment.

V/r,

product_name: Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System
review_title: an improvement over tv sound, but you can get better sounding equipment at this price
review_text:
I requested the Bose TV sound system hoping it would be an improvement over the cheaper Polk Audio soundbar we got a few years ago. Unfotunately, the sound isn't nearly as good on the Bose system.

We did back to back tests with tv sound, the soundbar, and the Bose system while watching music videos and a television show. The Bose system is definitely a huge improvement over the television's built-in speakers, but it doesn't come close to matching our Polk Audio soundbar. It's not surprising that our Polk Audio soundbar, which has a dedicated subwoofer would out-perform the Bose Solo system on bass, but even in the mids and highs and better on the Polk Audio system. The highs especially sound a bit tinny on the Bose system, and voices sound just a little less full on the Bose system than they are on our Polk Audio soundbar.

Comparing the Bose Solo system, which is designed to rest under a television to a soundbar that can't do that is a bit unfair. If you need a television sound system that can rest under the television so that it won't take up any extra space, the Bose Solo system is a huge improvement over standard television sound. But if you have the flexibility for another speaker configuration, there are definitely better options for your money.

product_name: Harman Kardon Aura Wireless Stereo Speaker System
review_title: Great sound, amazing design, but hindered by weak firmware and companion app.
review_text:
This unit sounds great and looks amazing. I'd like to give it a few more stars, but it suffers from a few key issues - there are some rough edges on the firmware on the unit itself, and general weirdness in the phone app used to control/configure the device. Wouldn't be a big issue in a $200 product, but for something that retails for $400 bucks, you'd hope they'd have the kinks worked out.

Notes:
- I love the all-in-one design of the Aura. An elegant one piece unit nearly eliminates cable complexity and fills the room with full and rich sound.
- If you're going to use this as an AirPlay speaker, there doesn't seem to be a way to enter the password for wifi network. The only way to do it seems to be to have it copy the settings from your phone. It worked with my iPhone, but it seems clunky.
- The iPhone app is pretty useless aside from initially configuring the wireless.
- The Aura is about 30 ft from my router, joined to a 802.11g network. It holds the connection and streams well 95% of the time, but can sometimes disappear from the AirPlay on both my phone and desktop iTunes. This is probably less of an issue with the device than it is with the AirPlay protocol itself.
- The controls and indicators on the device could be better. The power and volume buttons are touch-sensitive, but don't give any sort of feedback, so I'm always left wondering if the command I just tried to give it has registered.
- I don't have the same concerns about Bluetooth pairing that the other reviewers mention, but I could see how this would be an issue for you if you lived in a dense apartment building.

Bottom line:
It's great if you can set it and forget it. But if you use it primarily as an AirPlay speaker, you'll have to fiddle it every once in a while when it drops the connection. When that happens, you'll be annoyed that the process isn't a little smoother in something you paid $400 for. Without a firmware update and a new version of the companion app, it's a reasonable value at $300, a steal for $250, but overpriced at $400.ion of the companion app, it's a reasonable value at $300, a steal for $250, but overpriced at $400.

product_name: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)
review_title: Enjoyable, but leaves me wanting more
review_text:
I've had this device for a few months now, and have had my eyes on other reviews to see what others think of it. I'm ready to join the fray.
-Sounds quality: I'm pretty happy overall, coming from an iPod Classic, I notice a bump in quality. This perceived difference is certainly impacted by the type of music and quality of recording. Jazz, electronic, and certain types of rock sound pretty great. Most of my music is either MP3, AAC, or ALAC, and all are handled well. Sound is the recent I got this, and for the price, it has delivered.
-Hardware: Nice slim form, easy controls I can use without looking at them. Screen is plenty big and lack of touchscreen is not missed at all. Scrolling through lots of songs/artists can be a bit tedious with only directional keys, but not terribly onerous. A big negative here though, and something I don't see often from Sony- poor build quality on the SIM card slot (which I've seen mentioned elsewhere): the door barely stays closed and is not flush. Not a deal breaker, but annoying. Worse, is a slight opening in the casing along the side with the volume buttons. Sure, I've probably dropped this thing a few times by now, but a couple of feet off the ground, not off a building. I'm not concerned, but my old iPod was a solid as a rock (not to mention totally seamless).
-Device software: Basic and functional. Options to look at photos and watch videos, and frankly, I don't think it's necessary. It's easy to access playlists, the music I'm looking for, shuffle, and equalizer settings. It's not as sexy as the iPod software, but it does the job.
-Computer/media transfer software: I have a Mac, and should note that Sony did put out an updated transfer software release (Content Transfer version 1.1.11140) that solved many issues from transferring music and playlists from iTunes. By dragging and dropping, it is easy to move songs (and the artwork goes along with it). The strange part is the playlist- if you transfer a playlist, it doesn't just move over the info of what songs to play, it moves over all the songs (again). So, if you make a new playlist in iTunes, then drag it over to the Walkman, it will attempt to move each and every song over (and, again and again, realize the file is already there and move to the next). This takes forever for what amounts to a text file.

-Memory: Major pros/cons here. The 64 GB on board storage is a good start. But, with lossless files, fills up quick. I purchased a 128 GB micro SIM card to max it out. The device can seamless play files from either storage location, but putting them on there requires careful planning- once one fills up, don't expect the software to know to start moving files to the other location. Still, the 192 total capacity is great with flexibility to put files on other cards.

Overall: I feel like most of my points were negative, but I generally like using this Walkman. I think it could use some fine tuning: software, transfer software especially. Ideally, I'd love to see Sony find a way to make a plug-in for iTunes so I can interface directly (not sure how Apple would feel about it, but worth dreaming about). iPods were famously easy to use, and should be the benchmark for any portable audio device. If you are looking for something that will sound better than your smart phone, this is a great place to start.

product_name: LG Electronics LAP240 Sound Plate 100W Slim 4.1 Surround Sound Speaker System with Built-In Sub Woofer and Bluetooth
review_text:
I purchased this LG sound system recently from Amazon as having purchased one of the TV models a few months ago that was listed as compatible I found that while the TV (the 50 inch model) has a spectacular picture but terrible sound. The reason for the poor quality is due specifically to the fact that the speaker has to be mounted on the back of the TV to keep its slim form factor. So while the TV is beautiful to look at all the sound that comes from it is coming out the back speaker and being reflected off the wall back at the listener. It makes the sound seem muted and dull. So again, I purchased this sound plate because the TV can sit on it and come out from all sides of the set.

Of course there has to be a "but" coming up...

But while hook up can be done wirelessly or wired (and it does come with an optical wire) the bass is very deep and tends to drown out much of the spoken work. There are 3 sound settings to choose from but they really sound very much alike.

It is a very definite improvement but far too over priced for what you get. One last detail; it comes with its own remote control that is about the size of a credit card in ALL dimensions and tends to get lost very easily.

Would I recommend it to a friend, possibly. Is is worth the price, definitely not. Is it better than the stock sound that comes out of the LG, yes. So I rated it in the middle and leave it up to you to decide.

review_title: Actually 4.5 stars.  Great idea with a few minor issues and suggestions.
review_text: I was asked by Sharkk to evaluate and review the Sharkk Power Strip and USB smart charger.  This power strip has four AC plugs and four smart USB charging ports in one device.  The power strip is 10  5/8"  long, 2 3/4 " high and 1 1/4" deep.  The cord is 5' long and is three pronged, just like the AC outlets.  The four outlets are spaced so that four 1 1/2 " transformers can fit with no issues.  Since the power strip also has four USB ports, it is designed to be mounted above a desk and not sitting on the floor.  With this in mind the design of the power strip is very smooth with the sides curved instead of square edges, a very European style that is very pleasing to the eye and makes this more than just a utilitarian object.  The power strip appears to be aluminum with plastic around the AC outlets and on the two end caps.  All in all a very stylish design.   The four USB ports are able to provide 6 amps total with a single port providing up to 2.4 amps, enough to charge an IPAD air with no problems.  It should be able to charge two IPADs at the same time.  This is one of the few  USB chargers that I have encountered that can actually charge a Nook HD.  Unfortunately, there is no capacity information printed on the power strip stating this information.  I got this from the web site.  The back of the power strip does state that the strip can handle 15 amps and for a capacity of 1675 watts and is only 120 volts.  The strip can be mounted on the wall and two screw holes are provided for that purpose.  It would be nice if they provided a paper drilling template to mount it but at least on this version.  The instruction sheet is short and to the point.  Unfortunately all the dimensions listed are metric so I posted my measurements in inches..  The power strip states that it can handle power surges, with is nice to have to protect any electronics, but I can find nothing that states how much of a surge it can handle.  One minor oddity that I saw with the unit is that while the unit is designed to be mounted horizontally the Sharkk logo and lettering on the front are vertical so you have to turn your head to read what is on the front.  Another small issue with the power strip is that with the unit mounted on the wall, the power cord comes out the upper right side of the strip, just above the on/off switch and hangs down beside the switch about 3/4" from the switch.  It would have been better if the location of the power cord and the switch were reversed so this would not happen.  Besides the issue of swapping the cord and on/off switch and needing some documentation and mounting template, this is a very nicely designed power strip that adds four USB chargers for one low price.  One review of this product talked about the price ($30) being high for this.  When you look at the fact that a good USB smart hub is $25, this power strip is priced very fairly. I was provided with a free copy of this item for testing and my fair and honest evaluation.

review_title: Simple solutions to common complaints about this clock.
review_text: I bought this clock about a week ago. Several reviewers have mentioned that the display on this clock is too bright, even when the display dimmer is used. Personally, I don't think the dimmed display is all that bright. Dimmed display or not, I have discovered a simple solution to this problem: CLOSE YOUR EYES. The nice thing is, I no longer use my bedroom nightlight for the times I have to get up to answer nature's call. My nightlight was brighter, but this clock casts an adequate glow on the ceiling. Saves me a tiny bit of electricity by unplugging the nightlight. The OTHER problem mentioned by reviewers is that, with the exception of the "snooze" bar, the REST of the control buttons are all the same size, and very small, and so are hard to distinguish one from another, especially when you are trying to operate the alarm functions in the dark. The control button design IS poor, and you shouldn't have to do what I did, but it works, and for the price of this otherwise decent clock, it was worth the effort. I simply purchased a pack of those little rubber-like, self-adhesive, pea-sized, cushioning beads (available at Wal-Mart, Target, hobby stores, etc.) and stuck one bead to each of the 2 alarm buttons. Voila! NOW I can feel the alarm buttons in the dark without wondering what function I am about to change, and with the 2 now-easy-to-feel alarm buttons as "home base," in the dark I simply count buttons to whichever other function I want to operate. Works perfectly. I suggest wiping the alarm buttons with a little rubbing alcohol first, to help the beads to stick better. Other than this, I am very happy with this clock. And, really, the big, bright display makes it easy to see the time when your eyes are clogged with sleepiness in the middle of the night.

review_title: Great design, meets the mark for many of the classic Sony headphone merits
review_text: UPDATE:  After the original unit malfunctioned (read original story below if interested), I received a free replacement and they have functioned perfectly for almost a month thus far. I don't have any reason to suspect these will stop working prematurely. It did seem the first unit I received was an aberration, and in any case it was easy to get it replaced with a working unit.  My updated impression of these headphones is they are ideal in most respects: they are light, stick well in the ears, have the conventional over-head headband design, etc. The only real downside is that when compared to the cheaper price of the old Sony models (often between $8-16) they don't feel as "disposable" and thus I'm a little for paranoid about things happening to them. Still, if they last for several months (let's hope!) they are easily worth the $25 for any runners who are attached to this style of headphone.  ORIGINAL REVIEW:  I was excited about these headphones because, like many others, I perceived them to fill the void left by Sony's various "sport" headphones which have been discontinued. The first day or two using these for running had me excited to report that they were indeed everything that I'd been hoping for. So many of the nuances are right: good fit, decent sound, long cord, appropriate flex in the headband. It's a great design in many respects.  I'm torn about how to review the product because unfortunately, after less than two weeks of use the audio cut out on one earphone. I'm used to this, as I'm sure any runner is: after months of use under running conditions, headphones inevitably break down like this. Even with the utmost care the jostling of the cables eventually leads to a shorted out wire or something else that spells the end, then you suck it up and buy another pair.  But I can't suck it up and buy another pair after two weeks.  To be completely fair I'm going to buy one more pair and hope for the best that this was an aberration. I see some other reviews alluding to short life expectancy so I don't know if there is a systematic problem or if some of us are just bound to get unlucky. If I have a better experience with the new pair I will update this review, but I want to put the problem out there so other folks who may experience it can corroborate the experience.  Update April 6, 2015 11PMEST: I think it's worth noting that within a day of writing this review I had a response from the sellers (see below) politely explaining a possible cause for the defective behavior, and offering to refund the purchase (which I have now seen come through via Amazon). There's an obviously negative angle to my review above, but I hope it also comes through that I want the product to be great. Hopefully I will find that my first experience was an aberration, and will definitely update the review and star rating if so.  In any case I would like to commend the particular sellers for being on top of their feedback and proactively seeking to remedy things.

product_name: Micca COVO-S Compact 2-Way Bookshelf Speakers
review_title: About as good as you can do at this price.
review_text:
The Micca Covo S's are an interesting speakers. They have some very good points along with some bad ones, and some that are just so so. I will highlight each of these below.

Just as a provisor, I've only had these speakers for about two days now and I've only listened to them for about three hours. I've also played pink noise through them for about four hours so they've had approximately a seven hour break-in period so far.

The Good
1. NIce design - they are small cube-like speakers that have an attractive, understated appearance. They won't be winning any design awards, but they won't look absurd with most decor either.
2. Five-way binding posts are a welcome and rare feature for speakers this price. They make attaching wires or using banana plugs a snap. My standard double-screw banana plugs fit into them just fine.
3. They really hit low for speakers this size. I was able to get them to hit as low as 60hz, but sound was definitely distorted at this frequency. They sound best with ones 120hz and higher. Still, for a speaker this size, their bass is quite remarkable. I think this is do to the fact that they are rear ported giving their woofer good excursion.

The So So
1. I would put their overall sound quality in the 'so so' bracket. It is still some of the best for speakers in this price and size range. I've definitely heard worse for more money. However, If you go up by $20 to the Dayton B652AIRs you'd notice an obvious upgrade in sound. I have both the B652AIRs and the Covo S's, and I definitely prefer the B652AIRs. Having said this, the Covos are not bad if you only have $40 to spend on a set of speakers.
2. Where these speakers really struggle is in the mid-range frequencies. Voices are muffled and a little distorted. Listening to fiddles, guitars and bag pipes on tracks from Skeryvore is a joy, but once the vocals kick in you can instantly hear the shortcomings of these speakers. Again, I've heard worse, but for just $20 more you can get quite a lot better.
3. The grills are not magnetic! This is not a necessity, but is a very nice feature found on the Micca MB42 and 42Xs. Since it's not a deal breaker I put it in the 'so so' section.

The Bad
1. My main complaint with these speakers is that they can't get very loud without noticeable, and even painful, distortion. I would not recommend them for a room larger than 12'x12'. My pair is connected to a SMSL SA50 amp - which is rated at 50WPC - and they struggle to fill my 20'x15' living room. You an hear them throughout the room, but sound becomes thing the father away you are.
2. As a bit of an ancillary, but still note-worthy, complaint; You have to bee at least a foot away from these speakers for optimal sound quality. Any closer than that and you lose treble and bass is a little embellished. As I write this review they are about 8" from my face and they don't sound as good as when I back up a foot or so. This is definitely something to keep in mind for your application.

So...should you purchase the Micca Covo S speakers? Well, I would say that depends on two factors.

1. What is your budget? If it is just $40 then I'd say "yes." If you can spend just a little more look elsewhere.

2. What is your application? If you plan to use them in a small space where you don't have a lot of extra room and your room isn't too large they will work great. If you have the space and budget I'd definitely recommend upgrading to something like the Dayton B652AIRs or Micca MB42Xs. I've auditioned the MB42Xs and at twice the price of the Covos they are well worth it. They would be my main recommendation for budget hi-fi audio if you have a money and space. They need at least 8" of open space behind them for their rear port to function properly. This is something to keep in mind when choosing speakers for you space.

My plan for the Covos is to use themin my bathroom connected to a Lepai LP-2020A+ amp and an Airplay receiver. The total cost for this system will be just under $90. I wouldn't want to spend too much more than this on a system that will be in such a humid environment. They Covos are a great choice for this application because they are fairly inexpensive, compact and sound good despite their price and size.

THe reason I have given the Covo S speakers four stars is because of their lack-luster mids and inability to play that loud. Stay tuned for further updates on their long-term use.

ONE MONTH UPDATE

I just set these speakers up in my bathroom. I paired them with a Lepai 2020A+ amp and a cheap Airplay receiver. For this application they work great! I did not want to spend a lot of money on a system for my bathroom, but I still wanted decent sound. These speakers fit the bill perfectly! I am very happy with this system overall. The total cost was $78 plus the speaker wire that I had laying around. Much better than any iHome system you could get and about the same price.

FIVE WEEK UPDATE

Even thought It has not been a lot longer I still wanted to share a couple more flaws I've observed as of late.

The first observation I've made is that the Covo S's do best with more acoustically based music. Genres such as jazz and big band really shine on these little cubes offering a nice soundstage with plenty of stereo separation. However, where they really seem to struggle is with rock music that is driven by electric guitars. The guitar tones come off a little muted and even distorted at times. I believe this is due to the size of the these speakers. Most smaller bookshelf speakers - and even some larger ones - struggle to properly reproduce the sound of rock music.

I've also notice that the bass on these speakers sounds a bit strange. I believe that this is due to the fact that these speakers reproduce bass acoustically - meaning, theyuse rear porting and sound echoing rather than relying on large woofers with high excursion. This results in a more boomy rather than tight bass. This more evident in genres such as hip-hop, R&B and dance that have a punch bass track to them.

Despite these newly observed flaws I'm still giving the Micca Covo S's a four star rating. I still believe that they are an excellent value. They really do work well in my bathroom setup filling the room with warm, pleasing sound. Stay tuned for further updates.

product_name: Sony CMTX5CD Powerful NFC Bluetooth Speaker with CD Player
review_title: Good sounding bluetooth speaker with lots of features
review_text:
Pros: good sound quality, good build quality, sleek design, ease of use, included remote control, Songpal app
Cons: good (but not amazing) sound quality, small display faces upward and not easily visible unless standing over the product, remote control required for full access to the device menu

I ordered this for casual music listening in bedroom/office. I wanted a small, unobtrusive speaker system with bluetooth capability and good quality sound. I also wanted a remote control, which is not very common in this category - other products included the Fluence Fi30 as well as 'portable' systems like Jawbone Jambox, Oontz, etc. The Bose, B&W, and Sonos products were above my price range.

The X5CD is a very good product and serves my needs perfectly. It appears to have good build quality. It sounds very good and low and medium volumes and is certainly sufficient for a medium sized bedroom. It has user-selectable equalizer presets, custom equalizer option, and a few digital sound processing presets (e.g. can mimic wide soundstage). After trying several combinations, I found that the Sony suggested preset called CA+ sounds best to my ears.

Bluetooth pairing was simple and bluetooth streaming audio quality was good. The product supports AptX and AAC codecs for improved streaming sound quality.

The remote control is small but contains all the functions. Conveniently, the remote's battery is pre-installed. Note that the remote control is REQUIRED to access the menu of the X5CD. Also, the X5CD can be controlled with the free Sony Songpal app from your iphone/android - the app can replicate most functions of the remote and the app can control the X5CD as long as it's already paired via bluetooth. Using the Songpal app for adjusting the equalizer and settings is far easier than using the remote and navigating through the menu via the small display.

The X5CD has a small display on the top of the unit. Unfortunately this display can only be seen when the user is standing directly over the device, as the display faces upward. review_title: A musicians take...dont listen to the reviews about too much bass
review_text:
Will try and keep this short and sweet. Don't do a lot of 'reviewing' but for this product, I just had to! Do my fair share of research on most of my purchases, so know how important these reviews can be. For the R6, I found some to be helpful but still lacked in some detail. Here's the deal, I've been a musician for 20 years and I have music in my ears for hours a day, everyday. Like most, I still live on a budget and although I have pricier and more "studio friendly" equipment I use for playing, I wanted something for the day to day, ie, working out, listening at work, etc. The Klipsch R6's fit the bill!

I tend to like a more 'bassy' mix and based on reviews this seemed to be the right product. Let's clear that up. While the Klipsch R6 DOES have a 'bassier' feel, its a lower toned rumble, not the "kick in your ears" I was expecting. Bass is good but certainly not overwhelming. That being said, the thing I do like about the bass mix, is its not muddy. I can still pick up great highs that aren't too "tingy" and good mids.That can be an issue with bassier headphones.

As far as built quality and durability, you wont be let down there. Size and weight are great too. Feel very little ear fatigue, even after hours of wearing them. You will want to take time and see which ear tips work best for you, go too small and you will get frustrated with them falling out during more strenuous activity, not to mention, you wont be getting the full affect of the bass and the noise cancelation (which btw is great).

That's all I got. Would have given 5 stars if the bass gave me more of a kick but other than that, you wont be sorry you made this purchase!

Be aware with this series of plugs that wires are not held in with set screws. They are fed through a tube and the stripped portion of the wire doubled back over the tube and held in place when the end cap is screwed on. Not a very good description, but I don't know how else to describe it.

With this design, they will work best with 12 gauge wire, or maybe 14. Smaller gauge wire will not fit snugly enough to work as well. Although it may fit, a cheaper series would probably function better.

The plugs are also rather wide. So if space is a consideration, you might want to consider a different series or brand.

I bought these because they were on sale. Otherwise I would have bought something cheaper. After all, the main requirement is just to get good contact at the end of a speaker wire. If you're using quality heavy gauge wire these would be a good fit. If you're using cheapo 18 gauge, it's like putting $300 Pirellis on a Yugo.

review_title: Great basic UPS unit!  **SET the 'SENSITIVITY' option to LOW!**
review_text: My local WalMart had these on clearance for $45, and for the price I am really impressed! This is just what I am looking for, since heaters in the winter and ACs in the summer always seem to disrupt my work. No need to restart my computer and reset the home network while I switch back the circuit breaker! :-)  PROs: - Very easy to setup. Clear instructions. US-based support [in my home state of RI]. - Strong enough to support my desktop PC, router, cable modem, and VoIP - Optional software allows for many customizations and monitoring. This was especially useful when I noticed the battery backup kicking in briefly when I turn on other appliances in my home. Just **SET THE SENSITIVITY TO LOW** and this shouldn't happen anymore. CONs: - Not powerful enough to support my laser printer (inkjet printers are OK though) - The optional software (PowerChute) disables some of Microsoft Windows's power options, like the 'on AC power' vs. 'on battery' options. However, this CAN be fixed: After installing, open Device Manager. Under Batteries, open 'APC UPS'. Go to the 'Driver' tab and 'Rollback' the driver and restart your PC. Voila! Windows's power options are restored and PowerChute still works!

If anyone, consumer or Audiosharp themselves, can direct me to a source of replacement cables for this model: Sur S520, let me know, and I would be happy to note it and up to five stars.

product_name: Grado Prestige Series SR325e Headphones
review_title: Game changer for old school audiophile
review_text:
For 25 years i believed that in order to have audiophile quality sound you needed a good home system and great SPEAKERS. After owning the grado SR325e's for a month or so (and a good break in period) I now believe that it is possible with HEADPHONES! I like to hear details and balanced sound (not too much bass, or to hot in treble). Of course this is subjective, but I'll try to describe what I've experienced. For about 14 years my headphones were sony mdr7506. Maybe i got use to their sound signature and thought it was good enough. They seemed detailed and some good bass with lively punch. However, i would usually tire of listening to them and feel the treble was a little shrill. Also the music soundstage? Sounded a bit distant compared to the grado that makes you feel almost in the middle of the performance! After a few months i tried to go back and listen to the sonys...i was almost sickened to think at one point i told several friends and even facebook that the sonys were a great headphone. Maybe for their price they are ok. The 325e had more bass, great detailed highs that are seldom shrill, unless listening to poor cd,file,or equipment. What am i trying to say?? These headphones WILL REVEAL weaknesses in source recording and equipment. They won't gloss over, they will give a clear reproduction. The upshot? If you have good equipment and sources YOU WILL BE REWARDED with almost blissful sound and hear your recordings as if for the first time. Especially if you've had budget headphones before.

Now, my grado experience started at the store listening to sr60, sr80 and sr125e's. I decided since the sony 7506 were about $90 I'd shoot a bit higher in price and started with the sr125e grado's at home. I spent a good week or two playing music through them while I was at work. I know they say not to play them continuously, so I made a cd with about 30 min silence and 40 min or misc. music. believe me breaking in the headphones HELPS!! don't judge them right out of the box. it took about 50 hours or so until they mellowed out enough in the treble to sound nice. remember I'm talking about the sr125e's right now. I'm not sure if they seemed bass heavy and treble shy for my tastes. I kept thinking "there has got so be more stuff i'm not hearing in this recording" like ambience decay of reverb etc... so, before my 30 day trial was up I returned the SR125e's to the store and picked up the SR325e's because I had been reading that the 325's or more detailed or brighter...and one review said "not in a bad way".

So, now you should know that ALL grado headphones are OPEN BACKED so they WILL NOT block out much if any outside noise. so if you want to block out sound or use them in noisy places YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. I believe the open backed design helps facilitate a VERY sensitive response to music signals and the driver moves very easily. this results in good bass, but detailed harmonics. you feel like you hear almost every nuance within the sounds. it is very easy to focus on just a guitar part and hear all the subtle timbre characteristics. maybe I used that word wrong?? lol cymbals splash and swish and oscillate. they don't go "shhhhh" or "pshhhhh". I can hear background singers DISTINCTLY!! one annoying thing is you can also hear engineering mistakes and over compression distortion very easily. thankfully its not obvious on all recordings, but my 2014 led zep II remaster is hard to listen to, but I realize that is what it is... sometimes I wonder if certain high frequencies are a little over pronounced or the response not as smooth as they might be in higher models, but that only shows up every now and then....

some people complain about the comfort of the grado headphones. I will not say they are bad, but they sound so good I am willing to fiddle with them every now and then to stay comfortable. the sr125e had flat pads that seemedto block some of the treble and got irritating kinda quick. while the sr325e come with L-cush pads which I liked better. I LOVE THE CORD its kinda big, but the best part is ALMOST NO NOISE when cable moves across clothes or hits something. plug is 1/8" with 1/8 to 1/4" adapter

I am preparing myself to upgrade to the PS1000e in the future! and this is coming from a guy who NEVER thought great audiophile sound could be had from headphones...until now.

in conclusion I WHOLEHEARTEDLY recommend grado SR325e for audiophile type listeners that like detailed sound that is not overly heavy on bass. if you want a rolled off treble and strong bass check out the sr125e'sle and got irritating kinda quick. while the sr325e come with L-cush pads which I liked better.
