review_text: Overall solid piece of equipment for those of us who don't like cords. I bought this for the wireless, sport style and great reviews. I'm not a runner by any means but find myself in varying situations of physical movement - from a desk to a shop environment. The amount of up and down movement this set allows vs cords is second to none. Not getting caught on something anymore is a magical feeling. I had no interest in the big over the head studio phones for the reasoning of heavy physical movement and price. I can use this set for just over a week straight in 1-4 hour streaks without having to recharge it. It fits comfortably on my head and seals out most sounds pretty well (just ask everyone who's tried to get my attention). The only time it gets moderately uncomfortable is from having only one side hanging on my ear and the other on my neck. Sound quality is great and clear, only lacking in the true bass department. If you push these against your ears for a better seal you'll get the missing bass tones. Connecting these aren't a big hassle either. I use this primarily with my LG G3 & off and on with my laptop. Every now and then you have to go a screen or two into the control panel on the phone for it to transfer all sounds to the headset. The LED indicator light that blinks for any setting is based in one corner and doesn't do a great job of lighting the entire clear section up. Phone calls are about average from what I've been told by those on the other end of the call. The ear pieces are wide and will make you look like Princess Leia, but I wasn't exactly going for looks. It may also take you a few times to figure out where the user control buttons on the right ear piece fall. I've found myself trying to click volume up only to hit skip forward 4 times. I would definitely suggest these to a friend or colleague if they're looking for a headset that will stay on their head no matter how much they move around.

review_title: Finally can use all six outlets
review_text:
The problem with six-outlet electrical plugs is that you rarely can use all six. Somehow, the electrical engineering wizards who design these things place the outlets way too close to each other, which basically defeats the purpose of using any appliances or electronics devices that have odd shaped adapters.

In the case of the Belkin Pivot Wall Surge Protector, the design is spot on with six outlets; each outlet can be independently swiveled. Other swivel outlets only let you swivel a bank of three at a time, which basically presents the same problem as a standard flat six-plug wall mount--you can't fit all your devices because the plugs are too close together.

This Belkin provided enough space to use every one of the outlets for my electronic gadgets. The most offending shaped one wasn't even an AC adapter, but a very large, round nightlight that hogged up two spaces. But with the Belkin Pivot, I just simply swiveled the outlet 90 degrees, and voila, problem solved.

product_name: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen 1287632 Beolit 15
review_text:
Many people have long had a need for a portable sound system that can move from office to workout room to patio. Once upon a time, this role was filled by ungainly "blasters". The advent of Bluetooth has enabled a flood of new devices, and Bang & Olufsen have joined the fray with rather mixed results.

Out of the box, the Beolit 15 makes a good first impression. While fairly small, it's solid with some heft. The look is tasteful and conservative (we'll talk about the strap in a little while). I appreciated the fact that there's an internal power supply--no wall wart--and that the power cable tucks nicely into the back. Bluetooth pairing with my iPhone was quick, and music was coming out ten minutes after taking it out of the box. At first I enjoyed the wide frequency range, but the thumping bass soon got the better of me. Bass is usually the attention-grabber in a sound system, but too much of it can wear out its welcome quickly. That was the case here.

So it was time to look at the user guide. It turns out that the booklets included with the Beolit were mainly warnings and warrantees. The user guide itself was only a couple of pages. No specifications were included and the instructions were at the reading level of a cat. How to tame that bass? I found the web page for the product line. There was really only a page of specs there: most of the website was dedicated to the designer and the overall look was more like a lifestyle catalog. But that's what B&O has always been.

It turns out that there are no tone controls of any sort on the device. At a minimum, some sort of "superbass" switch would have been appreciated. in the end, an EQ app from the App Store was able to smooth the sound and achieve a satisfactory balance. At a minimum, B&O should have provided such an app with the device.

There are more positive things to say. Bluetooth range was quite good, with solid connection all around a large house--even across two floors. Battery life was claimed at 12 hours and that was easily exceeded at moderate playing levels. Higher sound levels would probably shorten battery life somewhat, but I think this claim was easily met.

But there were many missed opportunities. There's a USB connector, but it's charge-only. If you want to connect your iPod and charge while you're playing, you'll need two cables--audio AND USB. Even the base audio system in my car will play music through the USB cable. B&O missed the boat on this. There are also no play controls other than volume buttons. There are no start/stop or skip buttons. This means that you always have to keep your phone or tablet close by. There's more than enough room for 2 or 3 more buttons. Not having those buttons really impairs the ease-of-use of this device.

B&O also proudly proclaims "240 watts peak power". Peak power is a sham term that respectable manufacturers dropped decades ago. Obviously some marketing type at B&O likes big numbers but doesn't know what they mean. If you dig a little you'll find that the Beolit has a pair of 35-watt amps. That's really quite a respectable number for a device like this and it's more than adequate for the task. Why not use the real number. It's worth noting that they distribute amps and speakers in such a way that the result is mono. This was done to ensure even frequency distribution around the room (not fully effective, but fair), but I'd have preferred stereo. Of course if you're playing music for a cookout, you don't really care.

And there's that strap. It's a piece of unfinished leather, attached to a couple of pegs--just like a guitar strap. It clashes with the overall styling and gives the Beolit the appearance of a lunch pail. The unit does need some way be carried, so why not a handle? There's plenty of room and it could be nicely-styled. The strap looks like an afterthought.

Bang & Olufsen hasbeen around for quite a while, known more for their styling (from beautiful to bizarre) than their audio quality (middle of the pack). It's clear they have the makings of a very nice product line here, but they need a strong UX (user experience) advocate inside the company. That would make an enormous difference.

I can't compare them to 8 other headsets on the market like some of the other reviews, but they are good enough for my needs. The sound quality for both phone and music is excellent, in my humble opinion. I am hearing things I haven't heard before in some of my 'most played song list'

The only issue, is none of the UE pairs I have purchased from Logitech have made it > 1 year before sound loss/cord fraying occurs in one ear. The loss in first pair was partly my fault, but the second I treated with kid gloves, always storing properly. While I don't really expect them to last much longer that (after doing quite a bit of review research on amazon, it seems sets 2-3x in price have the same issue), it would be nice not to have to purchase a new set each year. Something could also be said about the fact that I continue to buy them, hopefully my review doesn't lose too much credibility for that....

Anyway, for ~$50 w/prime these are a great deal. I suggest you snag a pair before they are no longer available. At this rate, I suppose next year I'll be looking at the 7 or the 900s, but who knows, maybe these will set a new longevity record!

Cheers

review_text:
Was looking for a portable headphone with good sound quality. Picked this over the Sennheiser momentum after a lot of research on the net.

Build Quality 4.5/5
First of all, I must say, I am really impressed by the build quality of this pair of headphones, especially at this consumer price bracket. Everything except the headband are of sturdy build. The brush metal finish is higher quality than the sony mdr-1a, and looks freakin amazing with the red accents. The stock cable is nothing good or bad. Does its job and nothing beyond.

Comfort 3/5
The headband pressure and the clamping force is a real pain (physical) to deal with. I had to bend and twist it to stop it from making a dent on my skull. The earcups are soft and comfortable. However, after an hour of listening or so, they can get a little warm. On a side note, the msr7 is by no means light. I consider it slightly heavy for a portable headphone (when compared with the momentum).

Sound Quality 5/5
The SQ is what really matters most after all, and this pair of cans surprised the heck out of me. The soundstage is very wide and deep for a closed-back headphone. Comparing to my home-use Q701, the soundstage is more defined, and when amped properly, more airy than the q701 although less wide. The Msr7 is definitely bass shy in every way, anyone who cannot live without a good amount of bass should stay away from it. Bass was amazing out of the box, too bad they disappeared after burn-in, but they are still very well textured. Sub-bass extension is mediocre, but mid to upper-mid bass are well done. Upper mids and highs are the real gems here. The clarity and shimmer don't lie to your ears. The amount of details is just absurd with amping. No wonder the high-res tag. Even without amping, with my cowon J3, it reveals decent amount of detail. Although sound isn't completely grain free and smooth like the much lower priced Fostex TH7, the MSR7 doesn't sound harsh to the ears either despite its highs focused signature. In general, I will recommend the MSR7 to female vocals lovers. Whoever listens to Pop and movie soundtracks will be very pleased with the purchase.

Isolation 3.5/5
Isolation is adequate for indoor usage. Just don't bother trying wearing it on the streets. It's not enough for outdoors. It's not a lightweight headphone either and not to mention it gets warm after a while. If sweaty ears isn't your thing, just don't. I guess its a bit of compromise made by ATH for the great soundstage and SQ.

Value 4.5/5
At this price point, I must say the MSR7 has a really high c/p value. You can only turn away from this headphone because of its ridiculous headband, or that bass4lyfe is your life motto. Did not regret my purchase at all.

review_title: Steps for Audio Fix and Copyprotection Fix - Windows 7 - Ezcap now works perfectly for me!
review_text:
This product DOES work with my Windows 7. I had problems at the beginning getting it installed correctly, because the company doesn't put the correct drivers on the disc, as many others have also stated. I found this solution WORKS, from another reviewer with Windows 7:
1.Plug the ezcap into a USB port on your computer.
2. Go to Control Panel, click on the main heading: Hardware and Sound, then click Device Manager
3. In Device Manager, look under `Sound, video and game controllers." If you see "USB EMP Audio Driver" it needs to be changed.
(This is how to do that):
4. Right click `USB EMP Audio Driver' then `Update Driver Software'
5. Click `Browse my computer for driver software'
6. Click 'let me pick from a list .......'
7. Select `show compatible hardware'.
This should give you two driver options, Window's own `USB Audio Device' and the `USB EMP Audio Device' driver.
8. Select `USB Audio Device'.
9. Restart your pc and try using the ezcap again. It should work now.

There is one more little problem having to do with the arcsoft capture software thinking I'm trying to pirate copyprotected material (and I'm not, these are home videos). This happens when the tape has gotten warped for some reason (maybe it is bent in a certain location or has degraded over time) and the capturing process reads this as a copyprotection code. But I'm now trying another simple fix, just following the instructions of yet another buyer here on Amazon to edit an .ini file within the Arcsoft program. It is very simple to do and doesn't require any fancy software, just Notepad which comes with your Windows pc. The instructions are as follows: [NOTE: I changed the instructions to fit my location in the "Program Files (x86)" Folder. You may have to look under just "C:\Program Files\ArcSoft\Total Media ShowBiz\com.ArcSoft.CaptureModule\"

1. Navigate to:
C:\Program Files (x86)\ArcSoft\TotalMedia ShowBiz\com.ArcSoft.CaptureModule\

2. Open "CaptureModule.ini" with notepad. Add "ProtectOn=0" under "[CaptureModule]" and save.

If it does not let you save, it is because your pc user permissions need to be changed.
Right click on the file, select properties
select "security" at the top
click on "users" and click on the "edit" box
Put a click in all the boxes and click on "apply"

I'm enjoying seeing my old videos again, and now they are shareable on Facebook and Youtube. I encourage anyone with old magnetic tape formatted home videos to buy this and start saving them now. Yeah, there might be a slight learning curve, but you can do it, and this product does work. It would be nice if the manufacturers would start putting the answers into their packaging. I decided to give it Four Stars because of this, but otherwise it would rate 5.

product_name: MEElectronics Balanced Armature In-Ear Headphones for iPod, iPhone, MP3/CD/DVD Players
review_text:
This is without a doubt the best sounding in-ear headphone for the price, or anywhere under $100 for that matter. For its price it has a very flat frequency response curve, i.e. what you hear is as close as possible to what was recorded. I have also tried the M-Duo from MEElectronics, which I suspect people who really like their bass will prefer over the A151. Personally, I prefer the A151 which delivers adequate bass without being overwhelming or making the mids and highs sound muddy.

The microphone works great even when it is hanging by the side of your head and not right next to your mouth. The remote can play/pause music on my Android phone. Comfort and sound isolation are pretty good, and also better than the M-Duo on account of the in-ear portion of the A151 being smaller. There are multiple silicon eartips to choose from, and you can where it over the ear if you want.

I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 for issues with durability. Two pairs of the first-generation A151 that I have owned have failed within a year of use; one due to a problem where the cable meets the headphone, and one due to a problem where the cable plugs into the computer/phone. The second-generation A151 has an L-shaped strain relief where the cable plugs into the computer (straight strain relief on the 1st-gen) which will probably help with durability, but the strain relief where the cable meets the headphone is unchanged. (The 2nd-gen also has a marginally better balanced armature, although I honestly can't hear the difference.) I'm not sure whether the 1st or 2nd-gen model is what's being sold by Amazon, so if you really want the 2nd-gen you might have to order directly from MEElectronics.

Another minor issue is the cable cinch on the A151P (i.e. the models with the in-line microphone). The cinch is below the microphone, so it can't really go up far enough to do its job. (Or maybe my head is just the wrong size.) The combination of the cinch andin-line microphone also seem to make the cable more susceptible to tangling. Again, only a minor issue unless you plan to take these headphones along for your workout.

product_name: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_title: A great little music player, as long as you're not looking for heavy/deep bass...
review_text:
Let me start by saying this little music player does sound fantastic with the right equipment. The customizable EQ allows for the mids and highs to be very audible and crisp. The bass is also there, but even with the low frequencies maxed out on the EQ, its not as deep as I would like, but this is just personal preference. Everyone has different hearing to some degree and prefer different EQ's. The audio quality this device can deliver is very respectable. With over 11,000 reviews averaging 4-5 stars, its obvious this player suits the needs of most people.

I like how this device can deliver a flat signal for music, which I find useful for the line-in application to my computer, which already has my customized EQ for increased bass and highs and reduced mids for the type of music I prefer. This is the only way I am currently using this player for now.

In comparison to the [[ASIN:B003JME32C Cowon J3]] (one of the best-sounding music players to date, unfortunately, it seems to have been discontinued), even with bass amplification from the [[ASIN:B005HJWWW8 Fiio E6]], the bass for the Clip+ is noticeably deeper but not as heavy as the Cowon J3 without amplification. This is the only thing I found most disappointing about the player for my own personal needs.

For the record, I prefer to listen to music with [[ASIN:B00HYH7HXA V-Moda LP2]] Over-ear headphones and [[ASIN:B001LNO722 Monster Turbine]] In-Ear buds. I wouldn't put these up against high-end professional sound equipment, but they're capable of amazing sounds compared to the crappy ipod buds I see a lot of people walking around with. I believe the Dr. Dre line of products are also capable of great sounds, but I don't think they're as durably constructed as V-moda.

The features for this player are perfect for the purpose it serves: Listening to audio. It doesn't have anything extraneous that it wasn't designed for, and it comes in such a compact package. The expandable memory slot is an added feature that I find to be genius. This player does a lot right and nothing wrong. If It was one thing I'd ask for in perhaps a "Clip+ 2" version, it'd be a bluetooth feature.

I would recommend this player to friends and family as long as they're not all about the bass...

product_name: Klipsch Reference On-Ear Premium Headphone
review_text:
These headphones are superb quality in all aspects. The packaging, the fit and finish, and most importantly the audio performance are all excellent. I am extremely happy with these headphones second only to my Bose QC15.

This is my first pair of on-ear headphones, I have always preferred the over the ear style. I find that the foam on these ear-pieces is very comfortable for long periods of time. The foam is compliant enough to allow the ear pieces to block out some of the ambient noise. Most importantly they don't pinch my ears into my glasses as bad as my other pairs allowing me to listen for longer periods of time.

These headphones deliver exceptional dynamic range allowing me to hear subtleties in songs I know well, but just never heard with other headphones. I have been unable to hear any distortion with the maximum volume an I-phone or Dell PC can deliver. More importantly I don't feel that I need to crank these up to hear the details.

The cord is a flat ribbon which is a good length if you are plugged into a device you are carrying with you but a bit short for sitting at a desk plugged into a stationary computer. I really wish the cable had connectors at both ends so it could be replaced if damaged, but that isn't the case. The cable end is a very small diameter so it should work with all phone or tablet protective cases. The cable is a 4 contact style and has worked fine with most devices with conventional 3 contact connectors, but sound was garbled with 1 adapter that I had until I pulled the cable out of the connector slightly.

There is a microphone on the cable near the top and it has 3 buttons on it. The center button will pause and play Pandora if that app is running, otherwise holding it brought up Siri (I-phone). The top and bottom buttons are volume control on the phone. Having a phone conversation using these headphones and microphone is as clear as can be.

My only criticism of this product are the flat cable which is not replaceable and seems like it would be prone to kink. The other issue is a weird interaction between my ears and the on-ear design which causes me to hear high frequency more clearly if I move my jaw a certain way. An issue not experienced by others, but I think these push a little too hard on my ears.the flat cable which is not replaceable and seems like it would be prone to kink. review_text: Outwardly, the MagicBox speaker is really adorable. I love how compact, yet sleek it looks.The top and bottom are made with a sturdy, non-stick rubber. It features a rewind, play/pause, forward, and call button. On the side of the device you'll find a micro-USB port to charge it (charging USB cable included), an on/off button, and an auxiliary port to connect the speaker directly to your phone if you prefer. Fully charged, you'll be able to enjoy use for up to 10 hours.  Using the MagicBox bluetooth speaker was incredibly easy! I turned it on and it immediately beeped and flashed a blue light. As soon as I turned on the bluetooth on my phone, it found the speaker. I pressed "Pair" and it was ready to go.  The sound quality is crisp, clear, and plays at a decent volume in smaller spaces. In my bedroom, I thought the volume was loud enough to hear, but I did need to keep it turned to its loudest setting to get the full experience. While the bluetooth was paired with my phone, I was even able to accept a call, just by answering with the speaker's "call" button and talking into it. That was such a bonus feature to this device!  Now, because of its compact size, the volume projected from the speakers is medium, but not able to fill a large room. Outside of my house, the surrounding noise overwhelmed the sound coming from the device. I also found it a little tedious to hold the rewind/forward button to increase and decrease the volume. I would have preferred a separate volume button.  Watch my demonstration: http://youtu.be/xiMrINYE0WQ  The DKnight MagicBox Wireless Speaker is a great portable bluetooth speaker to use to project music from your phone. It's not super loud, but I don't expect any of the compact speakers to go beyond a certain volume. It still has a clear and exceptional sound quality with good playback time. And of course it's ultra portable and user-friendly.  *Disclosure: I received this product free from the company in exchange for my honest opinion and review.

review_text: I'm giving it a 5 star because it's performance in a very difficult environment. I first must comment on perfect packaging and delivered as promised. We also would spend hours trying to move or direct the antenna for best results and lock it down. We simply replaced current antenna with our new 8008 and did absolutely nothing else to it. We immediately upon our scan pulled in 13 clear channels without ever trying to direct the position. The closest tower is 50 miles away in Springfield through the forest and up down the hills. We were hoping we would get our 4 channels but 13 was a nice surprise. We have been camping there for years and didn't know some of these channels existed. So we didn't get 50 or more but pulling in these 13 in these conditions has more than satisfied my expectations. I highly recommend to purchase this antenna. I also plan to let other camper friends know of our success because it's been a topic from time time on how to get better tv reception. I hope this helps other RVers and campers when they hit their home sites.

review_title: Excellent sound and value for the price!
review_text: I purchased these at Best Buy since I didn't want to wait to get via delivery, but the price is the same as Amazon, so for those who are ordering, I wanted to give you a review. I have tried many earbuds, from inexpensive to extremely expensive and right now my favorite wired earbuds are the RHA T10's which run $185 here at Amazon and $200+ elsewhere. I needed a pair of bluetooth wireless that had good sound and tried many from $150 to $300. On a whim, I went and purchased these at Best Buy and tried them in the parking lot. Wow! These are the first wireless earbuds that match the sonic quality of the RHA's. The highs are crisp and clean with nice thumping bass that are not over exaggerated. The mid-tones are a little too flat, but for $99 these are no-brainers. Ed Sheeran's X sounds crisp and clean you can hear him sliding his fingers across the guitar. Next up was Al Green's Let's Stay Together, Yeah! Green's velvety voice comes through without blending into the arrangement. The horns are crystal clear and the bass is not over powering. Okay, how about some jazz. John Coltrane's Blue Train came through with all it's power. Coltrane's saxophone takes center stage with no clipping at the high notes. Ummm...yeah. Paul Chamber's bass is ever present in the background and Lee Morgan's trumpet comes through without competing with Coltrane. Now let's really test them, Green Day's American Idiot. Yowzah! These babies crank! The separation in this stereo recording is fantastic and the Sol Republics reproduce them without any issues. The power of the track comes through without any problem with a tight bass throughout. Okay, these passed the test for me. Are they perfect? No, I don't think any set of earbuds or cans are, but for $99? I don't think you can get better sound than these for that price point. Unlike others have said, I don't have any problem with the design of these in-ear headphones. They're comfortable and the band feels comfortable around my neck. If you are looking for clean sound regardless of being wireless, check out the RHA 10T's, but if you need wireless and want to save some bucks, don't hesitate, buy these puppies. review_title: This thing seems to do everything
review_text: I needed an audio system for a work area. I already owned a pair of speakers so thought an integrated amplifier would be the appropriate choice. I store my music on a Mac Mini and this can be connected to an amplifier through the headphone connection. I looked at many integrated amplifiers hoping that a review would lead me to a good choice. I became interested in the amplifiers that would work as a DAC particularly the Teac AH-01. I thought I might get better reproduction by not using the headphone output on the Mini. I looked at the Teac NP-H750 and thought that accessing my home network and internet radio stations would be a nice plus. When I saw it on sale I decided to buy it and have been very pleased with the purchase. My first impression was that this a very well built item. The unit itself is very nicely made. The unit and particularly the knobs are very solid. The unit is a nice compact size. The remote is very solid and good looking. Setting up the unit was pretty straight forward. The instruction book was very clearly written. Entering my network password was a bit slow because you have to scroll through upper and lower case as well as digits but you only do this once. I went to the site listed in the directions and downloaded the Teac Radio Guide to my computer. This allows you to select stations using the controls of a computer instead of making due with the controls on the Teac and sends the information to the Teac. This made selecting internet radio stations much, much easier. You can try stations and if not satisfied easily delete them. Connecting directly to my Mac Mini was a little more of a challenge. First you have to download and install some software. This procedure is listed at the front of the instruction manual before the basic set up procedure and easy to miss. The unit, since it works with Apple Air Play wanted to use that instead of the direct feed from the computer. It's necessary to go to the system preferences on the computer and select the USB over the headphone output. Through a little trial and error I got it working and was pleased with the results. I have found the sound produced in all modes to be very satisfactory. I'm not an audiophile but have decent audio equipment and believe this unit to be quite good. All in all I have found the Teac NP-H750 to be a very good quality, very versatile, good sounding unit. I haven't tried it at high volumes and suspect by the output rating it might be limited in that regard. Perhaps someone else will comment on that.

product_name: Kvart & Bolge Sound Sommeliers Quarter Wave Speaker Wenge Wood with Black Trim (Pair)
review_title: Clean and open sound, better than they have any right to be at their price.
review_text:
It is probably redundant to add another five star review here, but I am highly impressed. These were purchased strictly for music. I am very old school (and probably very old) and listen to all of my music collection in stereo. I received the Sound Sommeliers last Monday, so this review is based on only seven days worth of listening, about twenty hours. However, in that time, I have some very firm opinions of the capabilities of these little speakers.

One (and most impressive), amazingly open. The sound is like that of one of the older dipole speakers like the original Quad Electrostatic or three panel Magnaplanars. When you pull the speakers into your room a minimum of 18" to 24" from the walls, the speakers honestly disappear and you hear only the music. No localization. Simply wonderful sound from beyond the boundaries of the speakers in both the lateral as well as the front to back planes. This is most true on acoustic music and vocals, but also comes through well on electric music. Symphonic music is not handled quite as well (I don't think). Have only listened to a few favorites here and the material was tough for any speaker.

Two, very good bass response down to about 50hz. I have not had the desire to connect any of two available sub-woofers to the setup which could extend the bass down to 20hz-25hz range. The bass is open and fast via the 3-1/2" full range driver and I have seen the addition of a sub-woofer actually muddy the sound of some full range speakers. I plan to live with these units for a while (at least a year) prior to any decision to extend the bass. Besides, on most recording, there is very little output below 40hz anyway so unless you know you are looking for some extremely deep output, you probably won't be missing much.

Three, articulate treble response. I am unfamiliar with the full range driver, but it is surprising that it has response that has such good midrange and upper midrange/lower treble response. At my age, I know I have little hearing above the 5khz-7khz range, so extended treble response is relatively unimportant. If someone in their twenties were to tell me these roll-off treble response, I can stand corrected on this. However, my wife's hearing is still pretty good (according to hearing tests, not me) and she likes what she hears and doesn't think the units are missing anything. She also likes that they don't seem to get sibilant on voices, cymbals and other instruments that sometimes bother her.

Four, WAF. Yup, the good old Wife Acceptance Factor. These are so slight that they pass most WAF's with flying colors. Not only that, easy to hide when not in use and if you want some background music, sound is acceptable up against a wall.

What's not to like.

Received mine with one top end cap off. Cut myself attempting to get it back on. My bad. Should have sent it back but didn't want to wait.

Wish they came with a stable base.

Absolute volume is not very loud without some distortion. Still loud enough to enjoy most music. If you are young and you still want to put on something and "CRANK IT UP", you better look somewhere else.

Nice job K&B.

By the way, these are being used instead of Infinity Interlude IL-40's matched with Infinity sub-woofers which are now officially in the closet (subs had been in the closet since sometime in 2012). No side-by-side comparison. K&B definitely more open. Definitely not as much detail and won't play as loud. Playing loud is not a criteria at 63 years old.nge/lower treble response. When we set this up we had a wireless DVD player but then we upgraded to 3D and needed a new DVD player which meant we had to have a HDMI cable running to the TV and we no longer had the nice clean look we were hoping to achieve. We got this and we were able to plug in our DVD player and Home theater system and run it out to our hidden HDMI cable and now we are back to no more cables hanging on our wall from our TV.

The picture is great with this too. And now we don't have to switch our TV input over to DVD when we want to watch it.

There are a couple ways to switch devices with this. There are arrow buttons on the remote so you can go back and forth or if you know the number of the devices you can just press the number on the remote or like I said above if you can't find the remote you can always change it on the switcher.

product_name: Aune T1 MK2 (Second Generation) 6922 24bit/192kHz Tube Amplifier Mini Hi-fi USB DAC Decoder "Fashion Black"
review_text: I recently received this DAC and headphone amp to upgrade my Topping D1 Mark 2 DAC. I must say the Aune T1 MK2 is amazing and the extra cost over the Topping DAC is well worth it. Last night I listened for hours and heard detail I had never before heard before, and the imaging was fantastic. I listen with a pair of Shure SRH440 headphones and am using the 6922EH tube supplied with the DAC.  (I have a Gold Lion on order).  While the DAC used in the Aune is capable of 192KHz, the USB front-end is limited to 96KHz. The tube is used in the DAC stage, not the headphone amplification stage.  As others have mentioned, the Aune is heavy. It is beautifully made and solid. My only complaint is about the plastic cover over the tube. I had to file it down on the bottom in order for it to fit and I broke one of them (fortunately they send two of them which might not be enough if you swap out tubes). The +/- 15v power supply is heavy as well. The large volume control is smooth, but I recommend starting out with it turned way down since this is not an iPod and should have the power to drive any headphone.  When you power it on it will remain mute for 30 seconds to give the tube time to warm up before a white LED under the tube lights up, a nice effect.  Almost all of the music I played was in FLAC format, ripped directly from my CDs although one piece I bought in FLAC format, 176Khz, 24-bit.  My laptop is running OpenSUSE Linux and I used Amarok to play my music. Linux recognized the USB audio device which required no special configuration.  I played a lot of Pink Floyd including the Endless River and David Gilmore's Live in Gdansk (MP3). The sound was more detailed than I remember and very musical.  I then played Escala, however I found listening to this album was difficult. It sounded muddy and distorted and actually harsh. In order to see if it was the DAC or the recording I next played the Sheffield Track and Drum Record (CD FLAC).  When I played the Sheffield Track and Drum record I heard a lot more detail than I had ever heard before, especially in the percussion. The soundstage was absolutely amazing where I could exactly place every percussion hit and every note. I want to say that it sounded very technical and exact, not overly warm but extremely detailed. It may even be just a bit bright, but that may also just be my headphones which I'll admit aren't the best ones out there.  I next listened to a recording of Stravinsky's The Firebird Suite (1919) (FLAC) which was recorded at 176KHz, 24-bit. The FLAC files retain the original 24-bit, 176KHz recording. This was amazing. I could place every instrument in the orchestra and hear detail I had never before heard. It was an amazing experience.  Compared to the Topping T1 Mark 2 the Aune sounds much more detailed and richer and the bass is much stronger. The Topping T1 also has a problem when a cell phone is nearby in that the signal gets amplified from the headphone cord. I had to place ferrite beads over my headphone cable as well as the USB cable. Topping could easily fix the problem by putting some RF filtering in their op-amp stage. I found no such problem with the Aune T1.  I will update this after I receive the other tubes I have on order.  Update: I got the Gold Lion tube and am pleased to say that it only improved the sound. The detail is still crystal clear but it doesn't sound quite as bright and more musical with a nice tonal quality to it. I have figured out how to better tune the audio subsystem in Linux which sucks with its default settings.  The default Linux ALSA and Pulse Audio settings leave a lot to be desired. The following changes will significantly improve the audio quality:  Add the following two lines:  defaults.pcm.dmix.rate 96000 defaults.pcm.rate_converter speexrate_best  to ~/.asoundrc  Copy /etc/pulse/daemon.conf to ~/.config/pulse/daemon.conf and change or add the following lines:  resample-method = src-sinc-best-quality default-sample-format = s24le default-sample-rate = 96000  This change significantly improves the sample rate conversion quality and allows it to output and mix at 96KHz.  Update 2: One thing I really love about this DAC is the fantastic imaging. When listening to a Reference Recordings 24-bit 176 KHz FLAC recording I have of Stravinsky's Firebird Suite I can place each instrument on the sound stage. It's not just simple left, center, right but far more detailed. When I close my eyes I can place each instrument playing in the orchestra. As a test I played the Sheffield Track and Drum record recording (ripped from CD to FLAC). The detail was simply amazing. When listening to the percussion parts I could easily place where each hit was struck, even the soft background ticks. When Jim Keltner is brushing the drums you can hear which direction the brush is moving, the imaging is simply amazing as is the detail. I heard a lot of things I had previously missed, such as the soft background ticks which I had never noticed before with my Topping headphone DAC.  The tube warmth is certainly there though I would not consider it to be strong or adding significant coloration to the sound.  So far my only real complaint is that the plastic pieces that go over the tube are quite delicate. When transporting it I managed to break one of the tabs on the bottom of my second set. I also had to file the tabs down in order for them to fit.  While the T1 MK2 is fairly immune to interference caused by a nearby cell phone it is not completely immune. Adding a ferrite bead with one wrap of the headphone cord seems to have completely eliminated the problem. My Topping T1 MK2 DAC on the other hand was far more sensitive.

review_text: It's a nice toy for adults/athletes.  4 stars for effort.  If worn correctly, the HR monitor is accurate. The accelerometers work well as seen by comparing actual distance walked with number of estimated steps.  The sleep analysis claims made by the manufacturers are based on the quality of computer based algorithms that try to model the sleep states based on combining a very limited set of parameters, or what is known as BodyIQ. Unfortunately, since it is not practical to strap on a multi-core processor on your wrist,  what you are left with is a spartan micro-processor running an algorithm that seems to model a very wide Gaussian distribution of sleep parameters.  In simpler terms,  the sleep analysis is limited and seldom correct (unlike the 90% claim by the manufacturer).  But that's ok.  The customer needs to be realistic.  The FitBit has the same problem, by the way.  So, bottom line: cool gadget, a bit overpriced, know its limits.

review_title: Microfiber "Cooling Towel", in Blue, 39" x 11", from "D & S"
review_text:
Suddenly these microfiber 'cooling towels' are all the rage with online sellers.
I was offered one for testing and impartial consumer review, and after trying it, here's what I think:

Nice product. Pleasant blue color. Comes in a reusable heavy-duty transparent vinyl ziplock bag for transport. 39" long by 11" wide.

All the advantages of microfiber. Machine washable, but also air dries quickly.
A textured weave, but smooth, and finely woven and does not seem prone to 'snag' like some microfiber weaves in the past.
This is NOT that velvety, fuzzy-towel sort of fabric I see on the microfiber cleaning towels at the Dollar Stores.

As I understand it, the technology is simple. You just wet it (salt water from the beach will also work) and it cools by evaporation, but MUCH faster and more efficient evaporation than something like a cotton bandana.
So the cooling effect is much more pronounced.

This feels good, and it really does cool. It will keep cooling as long as you keep wetting it so it can evaporate.

This is noticeably cooler, as if you took a wet towel out of the refrigerator and applied it to your neck.

However, be realistic. It's not an 'ice pack'. This won't chill down a bottle of warm beer, for instance.
But on your neck or face, it does feel noticeably cooler than a comparable wet cotton bandana (I've tried them side by side).

So yes, I like this. It's in my gym bag now, and I'll be bringing it along on warm weather hikes and camping.

I hope this info is helpful as you comparison shop online. Happy trails, everybody.

review_title: TL;DR: you get what you pay for.
review_text:
i'm a fairly new to hot yoga practice (2-3 mo) and bought this mat originally because i didn't see a point in investing in an expensive mat. "what could the difference really even be?", i thought. for my first few yoga lessons, i was happy with this mat + a yoga towel. however, (and i'm not sure if it was repeated use or just my increased awareness from practice) over a few weeks of 3 classes per week, i started noticing how much the mat was stretching between contact points during standing poses. even in down dog, i could feel my feet and my hands slowly stretching apart - not just slipping forward - and would have to keep readjusting my position. my towel was bunching up like crazy as the mat spread beneath me. i also don't think it has adequate wrist support for poses like wheel because, while thin, it's very spongy and stretchy, so you end up pressing all your weight into your wrist instead of distributed evenly across your hand (per my teacher). i've now upgraded to a more pricey mat built for hot yoga, and the difference is HUGE. i can focus on my breath and my balance without having to worry about my legs slowly stretching apart on the mat.

all that being said, if you're new to yoga and aren't looking to get into some intense hot yoga classes, just want to do some very basic poses at home and give it a try, it's not a bad option. but if you're looking for something to support you and really get you into practice, you'd be wasting your money.

Loading
The gun is easy to load with a spring load and a notch in the mag. No need for a speed loader if you have a funnel top BB jar. Resetting the mag spring was tricky the first few times. Make sure to push the mag a bit further when you think it's in.

The CO2 chamber is well designed and solid. No hex key needed, but a little leak when seating.
The CO2 lasted a couple hundred shots.

Power and accuracy
The gun isn't the most powerful: roughly 275-300 fps for .2g bbs.
The first 25 shots were pretty accurate. 1/5 were a little off. The accuracy improved for the next 75 to 100 shots.

It its fun to shoot a full clip using the semi automatic action.
The trigger has a nice 3-4 lb. pull.
The safety is convenient to the index finger if you are a right- handed shooter.

All in all, in is fun to shoot, easy to load and looks and feels great.

Part of meditation is having good posture and if its too squishy its harder to maintain your posture. Another big issue is that they tend to be heavy and cumbersome.

This pillow is good on both fronts. Its very light for a meditation pillow and its stuffed to the gills. Before buying, I read a bunch of the reviews and I noticed all the negative ones mentioned that its "too hard" and I can only assume that the people who wrote that are new to meditation. This pillow is way more comfortable than many others I have used while still being sturdy enough to promote correct posture. I personally do mindfulness (Vipassana) meditation and part of that is not allowing yourself to be too comfortable because that will lull you to sleep or make you forget your mission.

This pillow is perfect for my needs and I believe anyone else who is in need of a meditation pillow would do well to buy this one. The price is pretty good and the quality (of mine at least) is fantastic.

review_title: Crosman P1377 American Classic Multi Pump .177-Caliber Pneumatic Pellet Air Pistol
review_text:
This is a very basic pump-up air pistol with excellent potential. There are hundreds of "mods" (modifications) out there to make it "better".

PROS: Excellent trigger out of the box; Accurate; Quiet; Reasonable weight; Comfortable grips

CONS: Sights - Front is too short, Rear is crap. Cannot be adjusted "as is" to put the pellet where you aim. Front can be modified to raise it to make the gun shoot lower. Rear is stamped sheet steel that is "adjusted" by loosening the screws that hold it to the gun, moving it in the direction that you want the shot to go, and retightening it. Rear has a square notch on one end and a very small round peephole on the other. The notch is properly sized for the front sight (but too high at its lowest setting), but the peephole is way too small for shooting the pistol at
arms-length.

There is NO provision for mounting an optical sight (scope, red dot, etc.) on this gun - as is. The most common modification is replacing the plastic breech the gun comes with a steel breech, also sold by Amazon (Crosman Steel Breech Kit [.177 Caliber] [Fits 1377, 1389, 1740, 1760 & PC77]).

The gun will take up to 10 pumps (max), but the last 4-5 are difficult for some people.

Because of it's relatively compact size, light weight, and limited resource requirements (no CO2) - there's interest by backpackers, and preppers.

review_title: Very good niche product for the gym
review_text:
I ordered these on Prime day and saved a few additional dollars. I just finished my first arm workout with them and I was impressed. I've worked out off and on for 25 years. Religiously for about 10 years and then sporadically after marriage and my career took up more of my time.

I can't remember when I had a better biceps pump after a workout. Fat gripz challenged my arms in a completely different way than what I am used to. Some free and hopefully helpful advice and my thoughts on some of the reviews and comments I've read here. First, a few people have used the term "snake oil" to describe this product implying that it is fraudulent. I believe continued use of these will give you very good results. I've been lifting long enough to be able to tell if something will work for me fairly quickly. That being said - in lifting like most all things in life positive results do not come overnight. You have to consistently put in the time and effort. Aside from training hard you also need plenty of rest and good nutrition to get the most out of your body.

If you haven't been lifting very long you should probably stick with the basic dumbbell and barbell curls until you gain strength and arm development. I would then try these after you reach a sticking point in your arm training. You get bigger and stronger by confusing your muscles i.e. when they begin to adapt to an exercise and load you do something different.

I used these on an Olympic barbell and a set of York dumbbells. No slipping on either one but there was a small gap in the fat gripz that didn't affect me at all. I lifted with the gap out of contact with my hands and also with the gap touching my hands and it didn't make a difference to me. I typically use chalk when I work out and these have a nice tackiness to the material that is easy to grip without chalk, resin, etc.

Elite level lifters in a variety of strength sports have been using thicker(larger diameter) bars for some time now to increase strength. Those bars can cost hundreds of dollars. You can get most of the same benefits with fat gripz at a fraction of the cost.

These aren't essential to getting big and strong. You can definitely get there without fat gripz but I like them and feel they are well worth the cost as an addition to my home gym. I also do grip strength exercises and feel these will help in that area as well.

Bottom line for me - adds a new dimension to my workout program, seem to be very durable, and are not too expensive. I don't regret my purchase at all. I went from being pipe cleaner skinny in high school (135 lbs) to 6'5" 275 lbs thanks to working out. I'm far from an expert but do know a thing or do about lifting - most of the negative comments about this product seem to come from people who may not know as much about lifting as they like to think they do. I rely on reviews when purchasing products. These have almost 1500 reviews with the majority of them being overwhelmingly positive. That tells me something.

These also come in a package that states - "For maximum results and safety do not use these until you visit fatgripz.com/secret. That is the only part I'm not satisfied with. If they have information they want to share they should include it in the packaging. I went to the website and they want you to download a file to view the big secret and learn how to use these safely. Well, I'll pass on the download. I think I can get the results I expect and frankly, if you can't figure out how to use these safely you might want to pursue a hobby that doesn't involve lifting heavy weights.

product_name: Summer Infant Digital Color Video Baby Monitor - Dual Coverage
review_title: Unsatisfied With This Monitor Set. Would Not Recommend
review_text:
Unsatisfied. For the price I paid, I could have bought a better set.

1. Flimsy construction and feel. I don't know about you, but when my baby is not sleeping, she likes to play with the monitors. These are not sturdy enough to handle being played with by a baby. The screens are soft. They don't have a hard plastic cover to protect it. So if you press on the screen, the image flexes and the liquid crystal inside shifts around. I don't know why they do this. Never mind a child but honestly it's not sturdy for an adult either. Won't last a month in my house. Plastic is light and brittle feeling. Feels like the kickstand would break off.

2. Screen stays on until you turn it off. This is OK. I'm just not used to it because the other monitor I have by Levana, the screen comes on when the baby cries or moves. And will turn off after a few seconds of inactivity...like if baby falls back asleep by herself

3. Constant streaming audio. This is what I dislike the most. I don't want to be kept up all night with a constant stream of the audio from baby's room. Baby's are noisy sleepers. They coo, wail, gurgle, moan, giggle, and make all sorts of sounds in their sleep. As a mother of a young baby, I am hyper vigilant whenever I hear any sounds so the constant stream of audio coming from this monitor keeps me up all night and I cannot relax. My Levana only comes on when baby cries of moves. That is...both screen and audio. I can even set the sensitivity so I can get some shut eye, and only be awakened when it is actually needed.

4. Night vision picture quality is poor. It's worse than my very basic (cheapest model) Levana which I thought was just OK. But with this one, sometimes I don't even see a baby in the crib. She completely gets blended/blurred with the crib linens.

This set made me appreciate my Levana so much more (Haha). I sent this set back after using for just 2 nights....before I lost any more sleep and before me or my kids break the monitors.or my kids break the monitors.

I am really glad I bought these as they have served me relatively well for 3 babies... I would certainly buy another Withings product in the future as I think they really are pretty innovative. review_title: We used it on our 3 week old and we've now learned that this device is not recommended for newborns
review_text:
Full disclosure for this review: We used it on our 3 week old and we've now learned that this device is not recommended for newborns. However one of the reasons for the low review is that I feel the age range needs to posted SOMEWHERE on the packaging but instead it is printed in small print in the manual. The box just says "safe for children". In fact on the first page of the manual it states it is "suitable for people of all ages".
That being said, we also tested it on ourselves vs 2 different axillary digital thermometers (both orally and under arm) and the San Sero showed 1.6 and 1.1 degrees higher. If we were talking a difference of 97.1 to 98.6 degrees F, that isn't too large of a number. But when we're talking a difference of 99.4 to 101 F we're now in hospital territory for a newborn. Because of this 101 degree reading our 3 week old was admitted into the hospital, put on an IV, and had multiple tests ran on him to search for an infection that we've no learned did not even exist. This thermometer may be a good purchase for some, but for us we're disappointed in both its readings vs other thermometers and the fact that it is not clearer on the packaging or in the manual that this device is not intended for newborns.

product_name: RECARO Performance Coupe 2015 Infant Car Seat
review_text:
Looks like we're not the only consumers having the same issue of the seat not being able to detach from the base.

We've had 2 such failures in the span of a 6 month period. We're now on our 3rd (2nd replacement) of the car seat. The first incident occurred straight out of the box (on the third attach / detach) and we were able to promptly return to Amazon for a replacement. Not soon after getting our replacement (within 3 months) did we experience the same issue once again. After getting this second failure, I did some research and seems like this issue is starting to become prevalent on this model. On both failures, there were no straps, debris, etc. that would prevent the detachment of the seat from the base so this is obviously a design defect.

I've read reviews where Recaro required a video along with the S/N, P/N, and manufacture date. In reading these reviews, I went ahead and took numerous pictures along with videos showing the issue before contacting Recaro. It took me a couple of tries on different days and was able to contact them via their online chat on a Friday afternoon (about 2 PM PST). The customer service rep was polite and did not require me to send videos / pictures of the issue but I did mention this was the second time with the failed attach / detach. I gave all the required info S/N, P/N, and manufacture date to her right then and there and she mentioned Recaro will either send a replacement or refund my money. We decided to get a replacement since we bought the seat as part of a travel system with the stroller. Once our baby boy has outgrown the seat, we'll end up using the stroller. Our replacement seat is not currently being used as we've decided to use another brand by Simple Parenting. The replacement seat will be our backup for now as the reliability is only good for 3 months or so.

All in all, we thought the quality and reliability of Recaro was well known but obviously not for their child seat division, especially for the Performance Coupe model. Also, one last comment - their "Made in USA" statement is a little bit of a misnomer as there are some components that are foreign made. From what I understand, you can claim made in USA provided the majority of the components are domestically sourced while some percentage can be foreign sourced. Technically, it's better stated to claim "Assembled in USA" than "Made in USA."

There are 5 preset volume settings; a dial is much better so I'm disappointed with the 5 fixed volume options.
Buttons are hard to press. It just feels kind of cheap.

Battery life on the parent unit is a joke. Has never lasted through the night, not even once.

review_text:
I am extremely happy with this treadmill. It is light and compact, smaller than i expected really which fits perfectly within my 500sqft apartment.

It was easy to set up and put together with just your hands, a screwdriver, and some elbow grease, everything screws in. It is incredibly simple to use too.

The buttons push fine and work as they should. They are clearly labeled as to what they do and the screen is easily read even for my bad eyes. It goes up quite fast! This is a great treadmill for walking or power walking. I cant run because of my heart and asthma but my boyfriend got a good jog in.

The incline gives a small boost to the workout, sure id like to incline it more but its fine where it is too. The handles are soft and nice to hold on to. I have NO balance whatsoever so its nice to have comfortable grips.

Walking is easy and you get used to it fast. The tread is a good feel under my feet even if it does slip sometimes.. The treadmill comes with oil to use and after a few months of having this my machine is making a "feed me" noise so i may have to give it some. It is explained how to do this.

The machine does get dusty, it does get creaky and it does need checking over every few months but it should last a good long while. I got the three year warrenty just in case. Its a great treadmill for the price and i love it!

review_text:
I bought mine through walmart but the people need to know. AT 6' tall, I was worried about stride length and so I found 4 different stride estimates for this machine on other websites. One said 13" another said 11-15" another said 16" and another said 18". I managed a decent HIIT workout on a friend's 12" so I figured I wouldn't have an issue with this one. At the very least, I thought that I could still get a decent pre-workout warm-up out of this and it did make me sweat but the pedals angle downward so much that my toes jam into the front of the pedal base and I can't lean back and concentrate the movement into the back of my legs. With feet stuck all the way forward, the stride length feels shorter than friend's 12". I feel all the burn in the top of my knees/bottom of thighs. Stacking some of those foam puzzle floor pieces under the front of the machine helps me lean back a bit but this wasn't the worst issue.

The worst issue was the lack of resistance. Notch 1-7 feels like zero resistance and notch 8 feels like a little more than zero resistance. It was like pedaling a bicycle after the chain falls off. If anyone knows how to manipulate resistance or jury-rig it, please let me know. Also, the LCD display lights up but doesn't work. Duct-taped a dollar store digital kitchen timer over the LCD screen

review_text: Bought last year as a store demo.  I knew it squeaked but figured I could tighten it up(lots of complaints about that). The one that did the trick was on the main bottom beam(the one the monitor is attached to).  See photo.  I tightened all those bolts and the machine is as quiet as a mouse.  I know I will need to repeat tightening a greasing everything ever so often to keep the machine quiet.  I am now unsure about the heart monitor.  Seems it jumps around.  Maybe it is something I am doing wrong.  Will have to figure that out. Seems sturdy enough. I'm only 5.5 and weight 140 lbs.  My husband and son hate the thing. product_name: Bicycle Dragon Back Playing Cards (Pack of 3), Blue/Red/Gold
review_title: A good deal on three very colorful decks.
review_text:
More great quality cards from USPCC. I've been looking at these for a while, and finally picked up this set. All three decks have the same high quality card stock. Other than the colors, these are the same, except for the original gold design.

The gold deck doesn't actually have any metallic inks present; the dragons are two tones of brown or tan. The deck has a color 808 Joker, and a black-only guarantee Joker. The royals use the darker tan from the dragon art, with a dark blue and a dark red. That same dark red - or burgundy - is the only red used on these decks, so the two red suits are the same darker color. The Joker uses these same colors as well.

The red deck has five colors present in its backs, though these are all fairly dark, so it doesn't see like it's that colorful. The same jokers are present as in the gold deck, though the colors are different; he's decked out entirely in dark red with tan trim, and the bike is colored a dark green-blue. On the faces here, the colors are the same dark burgundy red and green-blue colors, with light tan trim. The red suits use the same dark red.

The blue deck also uses five colors for the backs, with the dragons comprised of two shades of blue, and the trim using two shades of tan. The Joker is decked out in blue this time, with a dark tan bike and light tan trim. As expected, the face cards use these same colors. However, the red suits here are actually blue; blue diamonds and blue hearts.

The red and blue decks come with one double-backed card each, as well as an ad card. The gold deck doesn't have any extraneous cards whatsoever. The red and blue decks are also very subtle one-way backs.

Definitely well worth the money. Ideal for collectors and players alike. If you like these designs, there are also yellow and green dragon back designs available.

product_name: LifeSpan TR1200-DT3 Under Desk Treadmill
review_text:
Excellent treadmill. Terrible packaging. First treadmill arrived with the plastic case broken. Amazon did promptly send a replacement treadmill and a label to ship it back, but that doesn't change the fact that I had to wrangle a very heavy treadmill around an extra time. Second treadmill arrived with a loose piece of plastic, but I couldn't find what it was a part of. I actually did not ask for a replacement. The Amazon rep I contacted was on autopilot and didn't read my complaints about the packaging.

I have been using it for a month. The console is kind of stone age to work with, modify settings etc. Would be nice if you could just control it via an app wirelessly, but I get how you have to have a console anyways in case that doesn't work for some people.

The way the belt is arranged it's kind of a pain to lubricate especially with the spray bottle Lifespan sells, but life goes on. Your best bet is to just lubricate the center where you can really lift the belt and then cycle it to spread the lubricant.

This is a long treadmill. It takes up a lot of space which is not desirable for a standing desk where there is really one sweet spot to stand in and that is it. Maybe there is a technical reason for why a long deck is still necessary?

*edit*
I have had this maybe 6 months and have walked hundreds of hours and miles on this Treadmill. The Bluetooth integration is completely non-functional and I can't connect a device. Not a huge deal, but it would have been nice.

The treadmill is also very loud at this point. I think the copious dust and dog hair in my apartment has gotten into the motor causing it to rattle. It doesn't rattle if it is running without me on it. The vibration from my steps messes something up. They don't make an effort to filter the air going into the motor. A few dollars worth of filter could make this thing last longer and run quieter. No way you can use it in a shared space.

The console is still laggy and unresponsive and a pain to work with.

That said I am not changing the number of stars. I have docked the product enough. It works really well at it's core purpose and I enjoy it and would purchase it again if I couldn't find a better option. I love having a treadmill under my desk and it has done wonders for my health and well-being.

product_name: FitDesk Under Desk Elliptical
review_text: Fits nicely under my corner desk where my computer sits and the gauge sits handily on my desk. Since I work at my computer a lot, I tend to keep my feet on the pedals and 3-5 times during my 8-hour day use it for periods of 10-15 minutes.  I have mild arthritis in my knees and fibromyalgia so to avoid overall joint pain, shorter sessions work best for me. Mostly I go for endurance (time) and don't worry much about distance or speed. It also helps with my overall fitness routine because I don't feel pressured to spend as much time on the treadmill or standing elliptical when I get home from work in the evening giving me time to do resistance training and still eat dinner at a reasonable hour.  And, on nights when I have an appointment after work and don't get home in time to work out, I feel like I've at least done something! This way, I can meet the recommendations for getting some exercise every hour in my sedentary desk job without interrupting my work flow and work to meet my overall fitness goals. (I still get up to stretch occasionally.)  I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for someone with really severe arthritis in their knees, but otherwise it should work for most people. (I also tried an under-desk bike and found it too hard on my joints.)  As others have noted, it did begin to squeak a bit after about a week, but a spray of pledge on the plates under the pedals stopped that. Overall, I think this has been a great purchase for me!

product_name: NcStar Tactical Green Dot Scope Built-In Red Laser
review_title: Exceptional optic if you put it together correctly!
review_text:
Bought one and encountered the same problem that has plagued some one-star reviewers. The green dot and the laser both lost power after a dry fire, never mind putting live rounds downrange. Being somewhat of a troubleshooter, I found that tightening the battery terminal cap obviated that problem. It looks fragile, but as long as you don't cross the threads you can cinch it up pretty firmly without worrying about stripping it.

On test firing, windage was dead center, but the elevation was 3" high at 25 yards on the first group. Setting the BZO was thus very straightforward and afterwards it made for a fun evening annihilating the gallon jugs I've been stashing in my garage for the express purpose of shooting them.

For such an inexpensive optic, I'm perfectly happy with it after feeding a few mags through my AR with it on top. After cinching down the battery cap more tightly, the power loss issue didn't make an encore appearance. My only gripe is that the tri-rail 'armor' makes this sight an extremely cumbersome piece of gear on top of a 16" barrel AR. I'd prefer a blank piece of aluminum up top (doesn't need more tacti-cool crap hanging off of it) or a more robust casing that doesn't need an extra piece of metal screwed onto it to protect against rough handling.
